<!-- #2743 (fix/2743-pg-single-create-on-conflict) -->
### Fixed (postgres single-create now honors `on_conflict` — both-backend parity with sqlite single-create + bulk)

- **`POST /api/v1/memories` on a POSTGRES-backed daemon no longer silently upserts (overwrites) a pre-existing `(title, namespace)` row's content — it now honors the request `on_conflict` disposition exactly as the sqlite single-create arm and both #2725 (CB-23) bulk arms already do** (refs [#2743](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2743); follow-up to [#2725](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2725); epic #2705; CWE-284; data-integrity North Star; T3 fail-open→fail-closed on a network write surface). `create_memory_postgres` (`src/handlers/create.rs`) never resolved `body.on_conflict` and always wrote through `store_with_embedding`'s upsert arm, so a single `POST /memories` whose key collided REPLACED the stored content with no pre-overwrite snapshot — the same silent-overwrite class CB-23 closed for bulk, leaving the postgres BULK path STRICTER than postgres SINGLE-create (the tell). **Fix:** the postgres arm now resolves the shared `crate::mcp::tools::OnConflictMode` BEFORE `build_create_memory` (so a `version` rename is what the #626 attestation gate signs, mirroring the sqlite ordering) and BEFORE the content-replacing write + the #1795 daily-quota charge (the CB-23 ordering) — `error` (default) probes `MemoryStore::find_by_title_namespace` and returns `409 CONFLICT` carrying `existing_id`, never overwriting; `version` renames via `MemoryStore::next_versioned_title`; `merge` keeps the upsert-via-`store_with_embedding` path. The per-row #1919 attestation gate + namespace governance walk are preserved. Regression: `tests/pg_single_create_on_conflict_2743.rs` (`sal-postgres`, live-PG cells that run in the Postgres feature gate under `AI_MEMORY_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` — no `#[ignore]`, mirroring `g6_postgres_quota_enforcement_1795.rs`, since that gate runs `cargo test --features sal-postgres` WITHOUT `--include-ignored`) asserts default-`error` refuses a pre-existing collision with `existing_id` and does NOT overwrite (out-of-band re-GET), `merge` upserts in place returning the pre-existing id, and `version` writes a renamed new row leaving the original intact. The behavior-change blast radius was swept: `tests/cov_ga2_pg_handlers_2.rs`'s two `pg_detect_contradictions_*` cells seeded duplicate `(title, namespace)` rows via single-create (pre-#2743 those silently upserted to ONE row, so the array-only assertions passed vacuously); they now seed DISTINCT titles (and a shared `metadata.topic` for the topic-filter cell, which now genuinely synthesizes a `contradicts` link).

<!-- #2487 (fix/2487-release-binary-attestation) -->
### Security (release binaries + mobile artifacts + Docker image now ship OIDC-bound Sigstore build-provenance attestations, not checksums alone)

- **`.github/workflows/release.yml` now emits a Rekor-logged, OIDC-bound `actions/attest-build-provenance` attestation for every released artifact — the Rust binaries + deb/rpm packages, the iOS xcframework tarball, the Android JNI tarball, the CycloneDX SBOM, and the GHCR Docker image — closing the supply-chain gap where the SDKs shipped cryptographic provenance but the Rust binary (the actual product) did not** (refs [#2487](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2487); epic [#2705](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2705); CWE-494 supply-chain). A checksum proves the bytes you downloaded match the bytes the release job PUBLISHED; it says nothing about whether the release job published the bytes it was SUPPOSED to. An attacker who cannot touch git but who can influence a release job ships trojaned binaries with perfectly valid checksums — a strictly larger hole than an unsigned committer field. The repo was already internally inconsistent about this: `publish-sdks.yml` uses OIDC Trusted Publishing (`id-token: write` → PyPI Trusted Publisher / npm `--provenance`, both Sigstore/Rekor-backed), so the Python and TypeScript SDKs shipped attested build provenance while the release binary did not. **Fix (mirrors the SDK OIDC/Sigstore precedent):** each artifact-producing job (`release`, `mobile-ios`, `mobile-android`, `sbom`, `docker`) declares the minimal `permissions` (`id-token: write` + `attestations: write`, plus the `contents: write` / `packages: write` each job already needed) and runs `actions/attest-build-provenance@v2` after the artifact is built — `subject-path` over the local artifacts for the file jobs, `subject-name` + `subject-digest` + `push-to-registry` for the GHCR image. The attestation is **ADDITIVE** — the existing sha256 checksum sweep (#2449) and the fail-closed installer are unchanged; every artifact now carries BOTH a checksum and an OIDC-bound provenance attestation naming the workflow + repo + commit SHA, signed against GitHub's identity and appended to a public append-only Rekor log the developer cannot rewrite. The release TRIGGER is unchanged (still `workflow_dispatch`, operator-gated) — attestation fires when the operator cuts a release. **Consumer verification recipe** (`gh attestation verify`) documented in `docs/production-deployment.md` §"Verifying release-artifact provenance". This is a precedent-application of the SDK OIDC/Sigstore mechanism (T6 does not fire); no new signing scheme was invented and no external code was introduced.
<!-- #2475 (docs/2475-single-authority-review-model) -->
### Docs (single-authority review model documented truthfully; CODEOWNERS / required-review overclaims reconciled)

- **The governance docs now document the review model as it actually operates under the operator's single-authority directive, so no artifact claims an independent per-PR review that structurally cannot exist** (refs [#2475](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2475); epic [#2705](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2705); same "declared ≠ enforced" class as [#2443](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2443); bet-the-farm claims-audit standard). Root cause of the finding: `release/v1.0.0` carries no `required_pull_request_reviews` object, so `required_approving_review_count` is `0` and `.github/CODEOWNERS` (`* @alphaonedev`) gates nothing — while `docs/AI_DEVELOPER_GOVERNANCE.md`, `docs/ENGINEERING_STANDARDS.md`, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` all asserted an enforced CODEOWNERS approval / "1 required approving review" / "human review before merge, no exceptions." That `0` is a **mechanical CONSEQUENCE** of single-authority (one authority account authors + merges; GitHub forbids self-approval; no second approver can exist), not negligence. **Disposition (Fable 5, DECIDED):** document the real review model truthfully — do NOT add a per-PR mechanical review gate (self-attestation) and do NOT require per-PR operator approval (contradicts the autonomy directive). New `docs/AI_DEVELOPER_GOVERNANCE.md` §5.0 "Review model (single-authority)" states the three review layers: **(1) AI layer (per-PR)** — Fable 5 code-reviews AND security-audits every PR (green CI is not sufficient), substantive but NOT independent of the merger; **(2) independent human layer (per-release)** — the operator-gated GA tag-cut, the genuinely independent review at release granularity; **(3) mechanical layer (per-PR)** — the 32 required CI contexts (`scripts/qc-allowlists/required-contexts-release.txt`, the CB-1 SSOT) with `enforce_admins: true` + `strict: true`. Reconciled every overclaiming line: `docs/AI_DEVELOPER_GOVERNANCE.md` §5.1 + §5.4 note, `docs/ENGINEERING_STANDARDS.md` §1.3 branch-protection table (`0 required` / stale-dismissal inert) + §6 Key References + the "no code reaches main without explicit approval" line, `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Branch Protection & Code Review", and the misleading first comment in `.github/CODEOWNERS` (mechanic unchanged; the comment now states it is a routing marker, not an enforced gate). Docs-only: no branch-protection settings changed, no CI gate added, no review bot added.

<!-- #2572 (fix/2572-cli-write-verb-pg-refuse) -->
### Fixed (class-(a) CLI write/read verbs REFUSE on a Postgres store instead of phantom-writing a throwaway SQLite file)

- **The ~20 class-(a) local-SQLite CLI verbs (`store` / `link` / `resolve` / `update` / `promote` / `forget` (+`--show-receipt` / `--verify-receipt`) / `get` / `list` / `delete` / `gc` / `stats` / `namespaces` / `archive` / `consolidate` / `auto-consolidate` / `namespace {set,get,clear}-standard` / `reown` / `share` / `offload` / `deref` / `reflect` / `atomise` / `reembed` / `mine` / `sync` / `calibrate confidence`) now REFUSE on a Postgres-served deployment rather than opening a conjured local SQLite that the served store never reads** (refs [#2572](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2572); epic [#2705](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2705); relates [#2490](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2490)/[#2568](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2568) which closed the same class for `export`/`import`/`backup`/`restore`; CWE-670; data-integrity North Star). Root cause: every one of these verbs calls `db::open(--db)` (or, for `calibrate confidence`, a raw `Connection::open`) directly, and `db::open` CREATES a missing SQLite file and runs the full migration ladder on it. On a deployment configured with `AI_MEMORY_STORE_URL=postgres://…` (or the `AI_MEMORY_STORE_URL_FILE` `0600` channel, or `--store-url`), a `store`/`link`/`forget`/… **write phantom-landed in a throwaway SQLite file the Postgres store never reads — reported as success while the data was silently LOST** (the exact false-success class #2490 proved by executed evidence for the durability verbs), and a `get`/`list`/`stats`/… **read returned an empty conjured database** (a WRONG result, not a degrade). **Fix:** each verb now routes through the shared `crate::cli::backup::refuse_pg_store` funnel BEFORE any `db::open` / raw open (and, for the read-then-write verbs `mine`/`reembed`/`offload`, before the first side-effecting read), reusing the already-hoisted `#2444`/`#2490` `resolve_sqlite_store` gate under `StoreDisagreement::Refuse`: a `postgres://` store URL is refused with a DSN-redacted message naming the HTTP-daemon remedy (`ai-memory serve` / MCP-over-HTTP), an unrecognised scheme / an argv-vs-env store-URL disagreement / an ambiguous `sqlite://` target are likewise refused, and a plain local-SQLite deployment (no store URL configured) is byte-identical to before. Disposition decided by a UNANIMOUS 5-agent adversarial vote (memory `4d3ea1c5`, 5/5 REFUSE over Route) — Route-through-SAL for the trait-covered verbs is deferred to [#2772](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2772). Carve-outs left node-local-by-design (NOT guarded, to avoid fail-closing the governance spine / key custody on a pg deployment): `governance check-action` (incl. the PreToolUse hook), `governance install-defaults`, on-disk key custody, and the `src/erasure/` cold tier. Companion doc fix: the `reown` "Both sqlite + postgres" overclaim in `docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md` is corrected to state the CLI verb refuses on a Postgres store and to re-own via the HTTP daemon. Mechanical coverage: `tests/cli_write_verb_pg_refuse_ceiling_2572.rs` (modeled on `tests/db_open_funnel_ceiling_2445.rs`) enumerates every production CLI local-SQLite-open site and pins its disposition (guarded-refuse vs carved-out), so no verb slips the guard and every future CLI verb must classify; it includes an R-203 leg (`resolve_sqlite_store(..., Refuse, ...)` on a `postgres://` URL returns the typed refusal; on `None`/local it returns the `--db` path unchanged).


<!-- #2764 (test/2764-flaky-export-isolation) -->
### Fixed (`export_reflections::test_memory_export_reflection_mcp_tool` no longer intermittently fails with `memory not found` on macOS)

- **The reflection-export MCP integration test is now deterministic across a process boundary** (refs [#2764](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2764); epic [#2705](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2705)). `tests/cli/export_reflections.rs::test_memory_export_reflection_mcp_tool` is the ONLY test in the module that reads the seeded database from a SEPARATE process — it seeds the reflection with an in-process `rusqlite::Connection`, drops it, then spawns an `ai-memory mcp` subprocess that reads the row back by id. `db::open` opens the DB in WAL mode with `synchronous=NORMAL`, and rusqlite's `Drop` -> `sqlite3_close` checkpoint-on-close is best-effort, so on macOS (APFS + WAL) the just-committed reflection row could still be sitting in the `-wal` sidecar when the subprocess opened the DB — surfacing as an intermittent `memory not found` (a test-isolation/durability defect in the harness, NOT a substrate defect; the on-disk row was always correct). **Fix:** the test now forces `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` via the existing `db::checkpoint` on the writer connection BEFORE dropping it, guaranteeing the committed row is durably in the main DB file the reader process opens. This is a durability barrier, not a timing hack — no `sleep` was added and no assertion was weakened. Each test already runs against its own `tempfile::TempDir` DB with a per-test namespace, so no cross-test state is shared.
<!-- #2763 (test/2763-cb19-coverage) -->
### Tests (CB-19 trusted-handler split: focused branch coverage for `resolve_namespace_standard_caller`)

- **A focused unit test pins both branches of the CB-19 (#2721) namespace-standard caller-resolution split, greening the Per-Module Coverage Thresholds gate** (refs [#2763](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2763); relates [#2721](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2721); epic #2705). The functional #2721 regression (`set_standard_wire_reserved_sentinel_is_not_honored_2721`) exercises the handlers end-to-end, but the non-required Per-Module Coverage gate dipped below floor on the pure resolver `mcp::tools::namespace::resolve_namespace_standard_caller` introduced by the trusted-handler split. `mcp::tools::namespace::tests::resolve_namespace_standard_caller_branches_2763` covers it directly: (a) a `trusted_caller` is returned VERBATIM even when a reserved sentinel is present on the wire (the out-of-band operator surface); (b) a wire `agent_id == sentinels::DAEMON_PRINCIPAL` with no trusted caller falls to `sentinels::ANONYMOUS_INVALID` (the security-critical CB-19 branch); and (c) a legitimate non-reserved wire `agent_id` resolves to itself (the `Ok` arm of the `unwrap_or_else`). Test-only — no production behavior change.
<!-- #2513 (fix/2513-pg-lease-acquire-wiring) -->
### Fixed (postgres lease surface documented truthfully as MCP-stdio/sqlite-local at v1.0.0; SAL reachability pinned)

- **The dormant `MemoryStore::lease_acquire` / `lease_renew` / `lease_release` / `lease_get` postgres surface is now documented truthfully instead of reading as a live cross-backend capability** (refs [#2513](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2513); relates [#1709](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/1709) Pillar-1, [#1675](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/1675), [#1718](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/1718)). The lease acquire/renew/release/get operations are surfaced on exactly ONE production path — the MCP stdio handlers (`crate::mcp::tools::action::handle_lease_*`), which hold a bare `rusqlite::Connection` and call the `crate::actions::lease_*` free-functions directly; MCP stdio is structurally sqlite-only (#1675). There is deliberately NO HTTP lease route (a single-holder lease is node-local and does not federate — unlike the action-transition / signal / checkpoint coordination primitives that received HTTP send surfaces under #1718/#2391 for W-of-N fanout), so on a postgres-backed daemon those four `PostgresStore` trait methods have no production caller — they are correct + live-PG-tested (#2310) forward-scaffolding, dormant until a pg-reachable lease wire surface is added. **Fix:** the trait docs on `MemoryStore::lease_acquire` (`src/store/mod.rs`) and the MCP handler doc on `handle_lease_acquire` (`src/mcp/tools/action.rs`) now state this reachability boundary explicitly, and — the load-bearing invariant — a future lease wire surface MUST dispatch through the SAL trait (`app.store.lease_acquire(...)`), never a direct `crate::actions::*` call, so BOTH backends are served (the discipline the L4/L2 `capture_turn_idempotent` / `recover_turn_idempotent` methods already follow). Contrast `lease_sweep_expired`, the one lease method that DOES have a pg production caller (the `daemon_runtime` pg-maintenance loop). Regression: `tests/lease_sal_reachability_2513.rs` (`lease_acquire_reaches_sal_trait_sqlite_2513` always-on; `lease_acquire_reaches_sal_trait_postgres_2513` `#[ignore]` + `sal-postgres` live-pg twin) drives the full lease lifecycle through a `&dyn MemoryStore` object, pinning that the acquire operation genuinely reaches the SAL trait (not the default `UnsupportedCapability`) on both backends so a future pg lease caller routed through `app.store` is served. **T1/T3 flagged for Fable review:** whether to instead EXPAND the public REST contract with a node-local HTTP lease surface (acquire/renew/release/get routed through `app.store`) — making pg leases live — is a T1 route-shape decision deliberately NOT self-authorized here; this PR takes the truthful-documentation path the issue offers ("explicitly document/gate leases as sqlite-only at v1.0.0").

<!-- #2747 (cb19-2721-reserved-sentinel-wire) -->
### Fixed (reserved `daemon` principal can no longer be self-asserted from the MCP wire in `namespace_set_standard`)

- **A wire MCP caller can no longer spoof the reserved daemon principal to bypass the namespace-standard ownership gate** (refs [#2721](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2721); CB-19; relates [#977](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/977); CWE-284/CWE-290). `mcp::tools::namespace::handle_namespace_set_standard` resolved the caller with a special-case arm that honored a wire-presented `agent_id == sentinels::DAEMON_PRINCIPAL` VERBATIM (`src/mcp/tools/namespace.rs`), routing around `validate::validate_agent_id`, whose #977 contract is to reject the reserved `RESERVED_AGENT_IDS` sentinels that the cross-tenant gates carve out as the "internal path is exempt" signal. Combined with `authorize_namespace_standard_bind`'s unconditional daemon-principal pass, a stdio MCP caller sending `agent_id:"daemon"` could bind ANY memory as ANY namespace's governance standard (the policy gating every downstream write into that namespace) AND forge the #913 audit attribution as `daemon`. **Fix:** the caller is now resolved via `resolve_namespace_standard_caller`, which distinguishes an INTERNALLY-SYNTHESIZED trusted principal from a SELF-ASSERTED wire field. The reserved daemon principal is producible ONLY out-of-band, via the new `handle_namespace_set_standard_trusted` entry that the in-process CLI operator surface (`src/cli/namespace.rs`) calls with `DAEMON_PRINCIPAL` passed as an explicit argument — never through `params.agent_id`. The MCP wire entry (`handle_namespace_set_standard`) resolves the caller strictly through `identity::resolve_agent_id`, so a wire-presented reserved sentinel (`daemon`, `system`, or any other member of the `sentinels`-built `RESERVED_AGENT_IDS` set) fails resolution and downgrades to `anonymous:invalid` — a non-owning principal the #929 ownership gate refuses on any owned row, with the refusal chained into the #913/#2634 forensic audit trail by construction. The legitimate internal producers (curator/autonomy self-writes via `CallerContext::for_admin`, the CLI daemon surface) are NOT tightened. The HTTP surface was already safe — `resolve_http_agent_id` runs the strict validator and neutralizes a wire `X-Agent-Id: daemon` to `anonymous:invalid` before it reaches the handler. Design decision recorded via the 5-agent adversarial vote (memory `4d3ea1c5`): the wire disposition is DOWNGRADE-to-`anonymous:invalid` (byte-consistent with every other reserved sentinel on the MCP surface, preserving the CB-24 audit-capture guarantee), not a per-tool hard-refuse. Regression: `src/mcp/tools/namespace.rs::tests::set_standard_wire_reserved_sentinel_is_not_honored_2721` (wire `daemon`/`system` refused + downgraded on an owned row; HTTP header resolver rejects a wire daemon claim; the trusted out-of-band daemon self-write still succeeds as a control).

<!-- #2749 (fix/2728-2729-release-html-ssot) -->
### Fixed (release-workflow non-native darwin assertion + procurement-page CLI-count drift with an html-aware docs-vs-SSOT gate)

- **`.github/workflows/release.yml` no longer EXECUTES the `x86_64-apple-darwin` binary on the arm64 `macos-latest` runner to assert its compiled features, and `docs/compliance/nsa-csi-mcp.html` no longer ships stale `89/91` CLI-subcommand counts against the SSOT `90/92`** (refs [#2728](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2728) CB-31 + [#2729](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2729) CB-32; epic #2705). The release "Assert compiled features" step ran `ai-memory features` on every matrix target, so the cross-built x86_64-darwin artifact was exercised under Rosetta 2 on the arm64 runner — a failure that could surface only during a real tag cut. The step now runs the executing feature self-report ONLY when the target CPU is native to the runner (which keeps the arm64-darwin execute check) and, for the non-native x86_64-darwin cross-build, verifies the artifact's architecture WITHOUT running it via `lipo -info` / `file`; the compiled feature set is identical across both darwin targets (same `cargo build --release --features sal` invocation), so the native arm64 job's assertion already covers the feature contract. Separately, `scripts/check-docs-vs-ssot.sh` had ZERO html coverage (the same class as #2668 E-20 for `benchmark.svg`), so `nsa-csi-mcp.html`'s CLI counts drifted from `EXPECTED_CLI_SUBCOMMANDS_DEFAULT=90` / `_SAL=92` invisibly when #2676 moved the SSOT; the gate now walks the operator-facing `.html` compliance page for the `N CLI subcommands in the default build` / `... / N under sal` anchors, and its `--self-test` plants a stale HTML count and asserts rejection (R-203).

<!-- #2752 (feat/2438-measurement-scaffolding) -->
### Added (capacity-measurement scaffolding for the certification-scope campaign)

- **#2438 measurement scaffolding — a 5-droplet Digital Ocean load-generator cluster + a Universal Scalability Law fit that MEASURES one substrate module's throughput-vs-concurrency curve and PROJECTS (labelled ESTIMATED-not-MEASURED) toward a 500-agent block** (refs [#2438](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2438); relates [#2437](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2437); certification-scope campaign). This closes the "14-cell ops/s grid has no producer" gap #2438 documents: it builds the throughput INSTRUMENT so a committed number can be a MEASURED number with a cited host, not a guess. Additive extension of the existing `infra/do-hive` provisioning + the `infra/pillar4-envelope/measure-envelope.sh` op-mix harness — the default IronClaw-hive path is byte-identical and the money-gate / VPC / `:9077` firewall / teardown are UNCHANGED. It is BUILD-ONLY: no `terraform apply`, no droplets, no spend; the operator drives the paid run under the existing `spawn.sh` money-gate.
  - **`infra/do-hive/cloud-init-loadgen.yaml.tpl`** — a load-generator droplet bootstrap (curl + python3 only; NO IronClaw, NO XAI key, NO LLM inference bill) that drops the canonical `store -> link -> recall` op-mix worker + a per-droplet runner at `/opt/loadgen/` and a DISABLED systemd unit (mirrors the agent template's not-enabled-by-default discipline). ASCII-only (the #1880 `check-cloud-init-ascii.sh` gate) with embedded bash using only unbraced shell vars so Terraform's `${...}`/`%{...}` interpolation never collides with it.
  - **`infra/do-hive/main.tf`** — an additive `agent_workload` variable (`ironclaw` default | `loadgen`) that selects the load-gen cloud-init via a `templatefile` path ternary. The var map is unchanged, so the default hive path is byte-identical.
  - **`infra/do-hive/measurement.tfvars`** — 5x smallest `s-1vcpu-1gb` load-gen droplets + one bumped `s-2vcpu-4gb` substrate droplet (so the measured knee is a real substrate knee, not a swap-thrash artifact), `agent_workload=loadgen`. Cost ~$0.096/hr, ~$2 campaign budget, zero inference.
  - **`infra/pillar4-envelope/measure-capacity-ramp.sh`** — the orchestrator-side ramp driver (sibling of `measure-envelope.sh`). It SSHes into an ALREADY-provisioned cluster (never spawns droplets, never calls terraform), drives the concurrency ramp at droplet-counts N in {1,2,3,5} x an internal per-droplet ramp so the cluster offers 8..512+ concurrent workers against one module, collects per-op ops/s at each offered-concurrency level using the SAME reducer as `measure-envelope.sh` (so numbers are comparable to the already-populated cells), and emits a machine-readable results JSON. `--self-test` validates the JSON contract into `usl-fit.py` with no droplets.
  - **`infra/pillar4-envelope/usl-fit.py`** — a numpy-free (python3 stdlib) least-squares USL fit `T(N)=lambda*N/(1+sigma*(N-1)+kappa*N*(N-1))` via the exact linearization + a column-scaled 3x3 normal-equations solve; reports (lambda, sigma, kappa), the knee `N*=sqrt((1-sigma)/kappa)`, and the projected `T(500)` with a leave-one-out confidence band. Every projected number is labelled ESTIMATED-not-MEASURED; interpolation inside the measured range is MEASURED; a ramp that never reaches the knee degrades to a LOWER BOUND, never a fabricated point estimate. `--self-test` recovers a known (lambda, sigma, kappa) from synthetic ramp data to ~1e-13.
  - **`infra/do-hive/README-measurement.md`** — the run recipe (`source <DO vault>` -> `spawn.sh -var-file=measurement.tfvars` -> `measure-capacity-ramp.sh` -> `usl-fit.py` -> `teardown.sh`) and the honest-scope statement: a MEASURED per-module unit + a composition rule (`M = ceil(A / A_module*)`, mesh bounded at <= 50 peers), NOT a 1000-agent single-federated-system claim (which crosses the ~50-peer ceiling into an architecture that does not exist at v1.0.0).

<!-- #2753 (fix/2710-2720-fed-pending-identity-quorum) -->
### Fixed (federated pending-action lane: consensus quorum stuffing, forged REJECT decider, and pending-row bait-and-switch)

- **The federation `/sync/push` pending-action lane no longer lets a peer pre-stuff the local approval quorum on a fresh insert, stamp the signed audit trail with a forged REJECT decider, or overwrite a still-pending row a LOCAL operator authored** (refs [#2710](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2710) CB-5/CB-9 F-6 + [#2720](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2720) CB-8 F-12 / CB-9 F-7; epic #2705; CWE-284 + CWE-346; data-integrity North Star; sqlite lane). Three sibling wire-trust gaps in the same governance funnel, closed as one change by mirroring the established federation identity discipline (`resolve_inbound_attribution` / the memory + transition lanes) and the #2529 decided-column precedent — no new mechanism.
  - **(CB-5 / CB-9 F-6, CONSENSUS QUORUM STUFFING — `db::upsert_pending_action`, `src/storage/mod.rs`.)** #2529 closed the `ON CONFLICT` branch against wire-written decision columns but the FRESH-INSERT branch still bound the wire `approvals[]` / `decided_by` / `decided_at` verbatim, so a peer could push a fresh pending pre-stuffed with a full approval quorum (or a `decided_by` stamp) under a namespace governed by `ApproverType::Consensus(N)`, then land a single `pending_decisions[]` vote and cross the N-of-N threshold — a human quorum satisfied by one relayed vote. The INSERT now hard-pins `status='pending'`, `decided_by=NULL`, `decided_at=NULL`, `approvals='[]'`: a wire-originated pending always starts with zero local quorum, and approvals are gathered locally via the signed-approval gate (`src/approvals.rs`) as `pending_decisions[]` votes converge — never trusted from the `pendings[]` row. This is the #2529 "decisions converge only via `pending_decisions[]`" precedent extended to the insert branch.
  - **(CB-8 F-12, FORGED REJECT DECIDER — the `pending_decisions[]` REJECT arm, `src/handlers/federation_receive.rs`.)** APPROVE routes through `db::approve_with_approver_type` (self-approval refusal + `is_registered_agent` + approver-type policy) but REJECT called `db::decide_pending_action` with the wire `PendingDecision::decider` VERBATIM, so an in-scope peer could stamp `pending_actions.decided_by` AND the signed `pending_action.denied` audit row with ANY identity string, including a real operator's — forging the governance audit trail (#2532 made REJECT symmetric on WHERE, not on WHO). A new `resolve_inbound_decider` helper — a faithful mirror of the memory lane's `resolve_inbound_attribution` — binds the recorded decider to the attested peer: a relayed third-party decider is kept only when the operator authorized this peer to author as that agent (or on self-relay / zero-config faith-based), otherwise it is REBOUND to the attested sender so the audit records the real actor while the reject still converges.
  - **(CB-9 F-7, PENDING-ROW BAIT-AND-SWITCH — `db::upsert_pending_action`, `src/storage/mod.rs`.)** The `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` refreshed `action_type` / `memory_id` / `payload` on a still-`pending` local row regardless of WHO authored it, so an in-scope peer satisfying `pending_author_authorized` (which sets `requested_by` to itself) could take over a pending row a LOCAL operator queued and swap its `action_type` / `payload` (e.g. `store` -> `delete`) before a human approved what they believed they queued (`upsert_sql_does_not_clobber_decided_status_2529` pinned only the DECIDED direction). The conflict `WHERE` now also requires `pending_actions.requested_by = excluded.requested_by`, mirroring the identity-binding discipline: a convergence update lands only on a row the inbound author already owns, so a peer cannot rewrite a differently-authored row while an originator's legitimate re-push of its own row still converges.
  - **Regression:** `tests/fed_pending_identity_quorum_2710_2720.rs` (a peer-stuffed `approvals[]` / `decided_by` is dropped on the fresh insert, end-to-end via `/sync/push`; a differently-authored peer cannot clobber a local operator's pending body while a same-author re-push still converges; a forged REJECT decider is rebound to the attested peer while a zero-config reject still converges) plus `src/handlers/federation_receive.rs` unit test `resolve_inbound_decider_rebinds_forged_decider_2720` (rebind / keep-authorized / keep-self-relay / zero-config-faith-based). Postgres is unaffected: `sync_push_via_store` buckets `pendings[]` + `pending_decisions[]` into `unsupported_on_postgres` and never reaches these funnels.

<!-- #2754 (fix/2716-erasure-restore-race) -->
### Fixed (federated erasure DLQ: the restore-race is closed on the POST path, and the live-row guard no longer silently cancels a legitimate erasure)

- **A queued federated erasure no longer destroys a legitimately-restored replica on a peer, and a legitimate erasure is no longer silently cancelled mesh-wide by an LWW resurrection** (refs [#2716](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2716) CB-12; relates [#2666](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2666); epic #2705; data-integrity North Star; both defects are Tier-2 unintentional data loss). The `federation_push_dlq` erasure lane (`src/federation/push_dlq.rs`) discriminated "the id is LIVE again" with a bare existence probe, which cannot tell an AUTHORIZED restore from an LWW RESURRECTION; the fix makes the discriminator the live row's `updated_at` versus the erasure's `failed_at`, on both backends. Design chosen by a 5-agent adversarial vote (memory `4d3ea1c5`, 4-1 for the DLQ-layer `updated_at`-vs-`failed_at` form over a `db::delete`-writes-a-tombstone rewrite and a supersede-on-success verb).
  - **(F9 — restore-race, the #2666 residual.)** `#2666`'s one-shot liveness probe ran only inside `expand_erasure_sentinel`; after a sentinel fanned into per-peer delete rows, the replay POST path had NO re-check, so an operator `restore_archived(id)` that landed AFTER expansion still had the pending delete replay and destroy the peer's just-restored copy. A new `FederationDlqSink::erasure_delete_superseded_by_restore` runs on the replay POST path for every delete-shaped payload (erasure-outbox per-peer rows AND #2498 delete-lane DLQ landings): when the id is LIVE locally with an `updated_at` at/after the pending row's `failed_at` (an authorized restore/re-store, which stamps `updated_at = now`), the delete is SUPERSEDED — cleared, never POSTed — closing the race even in the widest window (a receiver refusal leaving the row pending indefinitely). Any read error FAILS SAFE: the delete is left UNSENT for the tick, never risking a restored replica.
  - **(F10 — silent-cancel of a legitimate erasure.)** `db::delete` (the `memory_delete` path) writes no `forget_tombstone`, so a peer catch-up re-delivery of a just-deleted id was re-created by `insert_if_newer` carrying the peer's ORIGINAL pre-delete `updated_at`; the old `live > 0` guard then read the id as LIVE and returned `SupersededByLiveRow`, cancelling the erasure mesh-wide behind one WARN. The guard now supersedes ONLY when the live row's `updated_at` POST-dates the erasure; an LWW resurrection (older `updated_at`) makes the legitimate erasure PROCEED (fan out). The dangerous "silently delete a restored row" direction cannot arise from clock skew because the only branch that classifies a LIVE row as an authorized restore compares two instants stamped by the SAME draining node.
  - **Loud, never silent:** every supersede (both guards) emits a WARN naming the id + `failed_at` and increments the new `ai_memory_federation_erasure_superseded_total` counter, so an operator can tell an authorized restore (correct cancel) from a case that needs the erasure re-issued. Comparison is by PARSED RFC3339 instant (never lexical), fail-safe toward supersede on any unparseable timestamp ("never cause unintentional data loss" OUTRANKS "purged content must not resurrect"). Backend parity: sqlite (RFC3339 TEXT) and postgres (`TIMESTAMPTZ`, normalised to RFC3339) run the same comparator. Regression: `src/federation/push_dlq.rs` unit tests `erasure_sentinel_over_lww_resurrection_proceeds_2716` (F10: an older resurrection fans out), `erasure_sentinel_over_authorized_restore_supersedes_2716`, `pending_delete_superseded_by_restore_is_not_posted_2716` (F9: the delete is cleared, never POSTed), `pending_delete_for_absent_row_still_posts_2716`, and `restore_supersedes_is_fail_safe_and_instant_ordered_2716`; the existing `tests/federation_erasure_replication_2446.rs::restore_after_delete_supersedes_the_queued_erasure_2446` still passes (its restored row's `updated_at` post-dates the erasure).

<!-- #2755 (feat/2648-create-extension-allowlist) -->
### Added (supply-chain: `CREATE EXTENSION` allowlist gate)

- **A new CI gate HARD-BLOCKS any `CREATE EXTENSION <name>` in the repository whose `<name>` is not on the closed `{vector, age}` allowlist** ([#2648](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2648); supply-chain / data-integrity North Star). A PostgreSQL extension installs AS SUPERUSER inside the process that owns the substrate — below the SAL, below governance, below the signed audit chain — and persists into `pg_dump`; it is code executing beneath every control this release has spent its audit verifying, so which extensions the substrate may create is now pinned to an enumerated allowlist rather than trusted implicitly. `scripts/check-create-extension-allowlist.sh` extracts the extension NAME from every `CREATE EXTENSION [IF NOT EXISTS] <name>` occurrence across the repo — in `.sql` files, shell `printf`/`psql -c` strings, Rust string literals, cloud-init `.tpl` templates and Markdown alike — and asserts each is allowlisted; the name is recognised only in canonical DDL position so English prose containing the words is never mistaken for a statement. It FAILS CLOSED on an empty allowlist (the #2504 class), and its `--self-test` plants an off-allowlist extension named `foo` (asserting a non-zero exit that names the offender) plus an allowlisted near-miss that must PASS (R-203). Wired into `.github/workflows/c8-precheck.yml` as the `create-extension-allowlist-gate` job (no job-level `if:`), mirroring the `vendor-literal-gate` / `git-dependency-source-gate` closed-allowlist + self-test precedent; the substrate's `CREATE EXTENSION` DDL is a static `include_str!` schema with no runtime name interpolation, so the script gate over `src/store/postgres_schema.sql` is the enforcement point and no runtime guard is required. The repository carries zero unallowlisted extension references today, and this gate keeps that currently-clean property clean at tag-cut.

<!-- #2761 (feat/2608-rerank-budget-scorer-seam) -->
### Added (autonomous-tier rerank gains a wall-clock budget + a pluggable-scorer seam)

- **The cross-encoder rerank stage now has a wall-clock budget (`AI_MEMORY_RERANK_BUDGET_MS`) and degrades to the pre-rerank hybrid ordering — never a wrong result — when a forward would exceed it; a new `PairScorer` seam makes the neural scorer substitutable so `neural_score_pairs` finally has CI coverage** (refs [#2608](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2608); availability + data-integrity North Star; 5-agent vote `4d3ea1c5`). The rerank forward is the LARGER read-path term (~1,063 ms of a ~1,290 ms autonomous p50; ~4 s on long-content corpora, #1588), and left unbounded it is an AVAILABILITY defect exactly as the #2577 query-embed budget documents (MCP stdio's single-threaded JSON-RPC loop stalls every subsequent tool call; each HTTP recall holds an admission permit, #2032 M3, so sustained latency sheds healthy traffic — including durable-truth writes — with 503s).
  - **Budget (`AI_MEMORY_RERANK_BUDGET_MS`, CLAUDE.md env #155).** The tri-state grammar is copied verbatim from #2577 (`AI_MEMORY_RECALL_EMBED_BUDGET_MS`): unset ⇒ `2000` ms (the substrate read-class ceiling); explicit `0` ⇒ DISABLED (pre-#2608 unbounded); unparseable ⇒ default + WARN (never silently WIDEN the failure window, the #131/FBL-14 rule). It fires on approximately nothing on the reference corpus — a TAIL cutter, not a throughput governor.
  - **PRE-FLIGHT admission, not a mid-flight abort.** A candle BERT forward is a synchronous CPU call with NO cancellation point, and the pool cap (`RERANK_POOL_MAX`) makes each rerank ONE forward over ≤ 20 candidates (no mid-flight checkpoint), so a wall-clock timeout could only abandon the waiting thread while the forward keeps burning a core — strictly worse at fleet scale (latency → CPU-exhaustion, firing hardest when the fleet is busiest). Instead the forward cost is ESTIMATED before it starts (candidate count × padded token length, both known up front; token length proxied from byte length so the estimate is a pure, model-free, deterministic function; the per-pair-token coefficient is a NAMED, documented, calibratable const grounded in the ~1,063 ms reference, an ESTIMATE not a measured guarantee) and, when it exceeds the budget, the neural stage is SKIPPED and the recall ships the pre-rerank HYBRID ordering. The enforcement differs from #2577's mid-flight future-drop by necessity; the 5-agent vote (`4d3ea1c5`) chose pre-flight admission 4-1 (deterministic, fail-closed, covers both dispatch paths uniformly).
  - **Data-integrity on degrade.** The recall stays hybrid (fewer, FTS/semantic-ranked results, never cross-encoded) and the operator's `AI_MEMORY_RERANK_SCORE_FLOOR` (#77) is STILL applied — the floor lives in the outer `BatchedReranker::rerank`, so a skip cannot silently return rows the operator configured to be dropped. The durable memory text is untouched and recall is pure. `RerankerScoreFloor::RelativeToTop` is scale-invariant on the degraded hybrid scale; `Absolute` is scale-sensitive (documented).
  - **`PairScorer` seam.** `neural_score_pairs` runs only on the `CrossEncoder::Neural` variant, which a CI host (no HF cache/egress) never builds (`new_neural()` degrades to lexical), so it had ZERO CI coverage. The new `pub trait PairScorer { score_pairs, scorer_is_neural }` (impl'd by `CrossEncoder`, mirroring the shipped `Embed`/`Embedder` swappable-for-tests pattern) lets a deterministic test double drive the neural-rerank blend + the budget-degrade branch without a BERT model. Production is byte-identical: the blend now lives in one place (`rerank_pairs_core`) the real cross-encoder delegates to, and the seam override is `None` in every production constructor.
  - **Observability.** `ai_memory_rerank_budget_degraded_total` counter + the `rerank.budget.degraded` WARN (the only channel on MCP stdio, which serves no `/metrics`). Regression: `src/reranker.rs::reranker_budget_seam_2608_tests` (tri-state grammar, cost estimate, degrade-orders-by-hybrid-score, over-budget-skips-forward, within-budget-applies-blend, lexical-never-gated, degrade-still-applies-score-floor) + the external-consumer seam proof `tests/rerank_budget_seam_2608.rs`.


### Fixed (audit-integrity: cert note pins an exact cut SHA; audit-corpus citations remapped to post-rewrite ancestors)

- **The ready-to-tag cert note authorizes an EXACT cut SHA instead of "any descendant", and the audit corpus / release-notes / CHANGELOG no longer cite SHAs orphaned by the 2026-08-04 SSH re-sign rewrite** (refs [#2726](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2726) CB-27 + [#2727](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2727) CB-28; epic #2705; data-integrity North Star). Docs-only. **(CB-27)** `docs/handoff/READY-TO-TAG-v1.0.0-CERT-NOTE.md` recommended cut tip `b1bd4c59` but added "Also valid to cut: any `release/v1.0.0` tip that is a descendant of `0130b2f1`" — a clause that silently admitted arbitrary later `security`-labelled commits the Gate-3 measure binary `c1c6055d` never covered, so it certified a class of artifacts rather than the one the operator will tag. The note now authorizes **only** the exact measured/reviewed SHA `b1bd4c59a84cc864095ab459ee84134e0a621a85`, states that no descendant is auto-authorized, and requires re-certification (re-run the gates + re-pin) on any drift; the operator-action and verification-command blocks are tightened to the same exact-SHA discipline. **(CB-28)** the prior cert re-sign (`ae9011ec`) remapped only the cert note, leaving `docs/audit/3x7-claims-register-2026-08-01.md`, `docs/audit/3x7-v1-cutline-ruling-2026-08-01.md`, `docs/v1.0.0/release-notes.md`, and the `[Unreleased]`/`[1.0.0]` cert region of `CHANGELOG.md` citing pre-rewrite baseline/verification SHAs (`e31dea74`, `5449b6da`, `03bbd556`, `cb09bb07`, `da3fb9cc`, and the R-203 parent anchors) that are no longer ancestors of `release/v1.0.0` — resolvable only on soon-to-be-deleted PR branches, so every "re-derive before citing" instruction was going unresolvable. Each such citation is remapped to its post-rewrite equivalent (identical tree + subject, verified an ancestor) via `docs/audit/ssh-resign-rewrite-map-2026-08-04.md`. The self-documenting `docs/audit/graph-engineering-epic-2682-completion-2026-08-04.md` (whose tables are explicitly headed "pre-rewrite" and which carries the rewrite map in §8.3) and the frozen shipped-release CHANGELOG sections are intentionally left unchanged, as is the one verbatim CI-log literal (`PR_BEFORE: 3023f6bb`, a transient PR-head with no mainline equivalent).
### Fixed (CERT-GATE-2 published-claims gates fail CLOSED on an analysis-engine error, not a false PASS)

- **The four CERT-GATE-2 claims gates no longer print a FALSE `PASS` when their own analysis engine errors instead of running** (refs [#2713](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2713) CB-2; epic #2705; control-integrity North Star; the #2444 "reports success while doing nothing" shape — inside the very gates built to stop it). This is a single-correct-answer fail-open→fail-closed control-integrity fix (the gate's OWN errors, not detection behaviour), so no crossroads vote was required. Every gate's real detection logic and `--self-test` are preserved.
  - **Root cause.** `scripts/check-ci-job-claims.sh`, `scripts/check-doc-symbol-anchors.sh`, `scripts/check-sdk-route-paths.sh` and `scripts/check-docs-vs-ssot.sh` each captured their Python analysis engine's output with a trailing `)" || true`, which under `set -euo pipefail` discarded the interpreter's non-zero exit status: any uncaught exception → an empty violation set → `exit 0` + a green `✅ … PASS` banner whose count comes from a bash-side `find`, attesting to work that never ran. The realistic trigger is one non-UTF-8 byte in a scanned doc/SDK file — `open(p, encoding="utf-8")` raises `UnicodeDecodeError` (a `ValueError`, not the caught `OSError`), which the `|| true` then swallowed.
  - **The fix — FAIL CLOSED.** Each heredoc terminator is now `if ! violations="$( … )"; then …; exit 2; fi`: an internal engine error exits non-zero (distinct code `2`, distinct message `analysis engine errored … refusing to report PASS (#2713 fail-closed)`), never a PASS banner. The two `check-docs-vs-ssot.sh` process-substitution rules (`check_schema_version_rule`, `check_narrative_count_rule`) — which fed `done < <(python3 …)`, whose exit status is unobserved under `pipefail` — were restructured to capture-then-check so a crashing engine there also fails closed rather than silently yielding zero rows. A stray non-UTF-8 byte is now a loud, actionable refusal on all four gates.
  - **Regression (R-203).** Each gate's `--self-test` gained a fail-closed leg that (1) reproduces the pre-fix SHAPE (`x="$(crashing-python)" || true` swallows a crash into an empty value and would print a false PASS) and (2) proves the FIXED gate exits non-zero with the distinct message and NO PASS banner under an injected analysis-engine fault (a test-only, shell-scoped `AI_MEMORY_*_GATE_SELFTEST_FAULT` env var, never set in production/CI). The natural non-UTF-8-byte trigger was verified end-to-end to fail closed on `check-ci-job-claims.sh`, `check-sdk-route-paths.sh` and `check-docs-vs-ssot.sh`.
### Fixed (federated checkpoint resolution confined to the anchor's STORED namespace)
- **An inbound federated commit-checkpoint RESOLUTION can no longer resolve a checkpoint the peer is not scoped to by presenting a different WIRE namespace than the STORED one** (refs [#2708](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2708); CB-3; CWE-284; the #2447 stored-vs-claimed split applied to the checkpoints authority lane). The `/sync/push` `checkpoints[]` Gate-1 choke (`src/handlers/federation_receive.rs`) validated the attacker-supplied wire `cp.namespace` via `inbound_write_namespace_authorized(LANE_CHECKPOINTS, …, existing=None)`, but `checkpoints::apply_inbound_resolution` CASes on `(id, state)` ONLY — `UPDATE checkpoints SET state=…,resolution=… WHERE id=? AND state='pending'` neither compares nor writes the namespace. So a peer enrolled + scoped to `public/*` could push a RESOLVED checkpoint whose `id` is a locally-pending `secure/ops` freeze anchor, present `namespace:"public/ok"` on the wire (which `resolution_signable` covers, so a self-signed resolution verifies against the resolver's enrolled key and passes the crypto gate), and have the CAS resolve the `secure/ops` anchor — an authority-granting write into a namespace it has no scope for. The confinement subject and the write subject were decoupled. The fix mirrors the memories lane (#2447) and the action-transition lane (#2649) exactly: the checkpoints receive loop now resolves the local row's STORED namespace by id via the new SCALAR `checkpoints::namespace_by_id` (never a full-row `get` — the #2488 decrypt-fail-closed lesson, though checkpoints carry no at-rest envelope) and passes it as `existing_namespace`, so `inbound_write_namespace_authorized` refuses when EITHER the claimed OR the stored namespace is out of scope. The two legitimate arms stay intact — a first-landing resolution (no local row) creates under the claimed namespace (checked; stored is `None`), and a resolution of a locally-pending anchor is confined to that anchor's STORED namespace. The by-id existence probe is elided when Layer 1 is not armed for the peer (`ns_scope_needs_existing`), so zero-config deployments pay ZERO extra reads and are byte-identical to pre-fix; an unresolvable probe fails CLOSED (a probe error cannot be reported as "provably no local row"). First-resolution-wins idempotency and the per-item conflict count are preserved — a refusal is a per-item skip, never a batch drop. **Postgres parity:** the pg funnel buckets `checkpoints[]` as `unsupported_on_postgres` (#1936) — it never applies a federated resolution — so this bypass and its fix are sqlite/MCP-native-only; the honest count is unchanged. Regression: `tests/federation_checkpoint_ns_scope_2708.rs` (a `public/*`-scoped peer cannot resolve a `secure/ops` anchor by wire namespace; an in-scope resolution still applies; first-resolution-wins idempotency held under the gate; zero-config federation unaffected).
### Fixed (`sdk/typescript` `storeBulk` posted the wrong body shape and typed a response the daemon never sends)

- **`AiMemoryClient.storeBulk` in the TypeScript SDK now posts a BARE JSON ARRAY and returns the true `BulkCreateResponse` ledger envelope** (refs [#2646](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2646)). The bulk handler is `Json(bodies): Json<Vec<CreateMemory>>` (`src/handlers/bulk.rs`), so the pre-fix `body: { memories }` OBJECT wrapper failed axum's `Json` extractor outright — every `storeBulk` call was dead on arrival — and the declared `{ created: Memory[]; count: number }` return matched nothing the daemon has ever emitted (`created` is a COUNT, not row bodies; `count` does not exist). `storeBulk` now sends the array verbatim and is typed `Promise<BulkCreateResponse>` — the per-row ledger (`sent`/`created`/`updated`/`deduped`/`rejected`/`errors`/`pending`, plus the conditional `deduped_rows`/`updated_rows`/`warnings`/`embed_status`/`embed_status_reason`) that `BulkLedger::into_response` actually returns, including the 207-Multi-Status partial and 202-Accepted all-pending 2xx statuses `res.ok` already accepts. A new offline round-trip test (`sdk/typescript/__tests__/client.test.ts`) asserts the request body is an array and parses a representative envelope with a rejected row — the missing test is what let both defects ship. The `sdk/python` twin was already corrected in [#2644](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2644) (bare-array body + the same `BulkCreateResponse` model, `extra="allow"`) and needs no change.
### Fixed (`ai_memory_memories` gauge counts the served postgres corpus, not the local sqlite sidecar)

- **On a `--store-url postgres://…` daemon the `ai_memory_memories` Prometheus gauge now counts the SERVED postgres corpus through the SAL trait, instead of the local sqlite sidecar — which was empty, so the gauge reported `0` for a populated corpus** (refs [#2621](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2621); relates [#2583](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2583), [#2444](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2444)). `prometheus_metrics` took `State<Db>` — the local sqlite handle, populated on EVERY daemon (the federation nonce cache and other host-local state live there) regardless of `storage_backend` — so both the scrape-path cold prime and the #2583 paced refresher counted the sidecar, not the served corpus. A gauge reporting `0` for a populated corpus is worse than an absent one: `up` stays 1 and any alert built on corpus size (growth stalls, mass deletion, quota planning) is silently disarmed (the #2444 "reports success while measuring nothing" class). The fix routes the count to the ACTIVE store the daemon serves from: `prometheus_metrics` now takes `State<AppState>` and its cold prime dispatches on `storage_backend` — postgres counts via `app.store.stats().total` (the existing SAL trait method — no new trait surface — the SAME physical `COUNT(*)` the sqlite `read_total` publishes), sqlite keeps the cheap single-`COUNT` path; and the paced refresher in `bootstrap_serve` spawns a postgres SAL loop (`memories_gauge::spawn_sal`, mirroring the `access_fold::spawn_sal` postgres-loop precedent) instead of being gated off on postgres, so the scrape path stays O(1) on both backends. The gauge's meaning (`stats.total`, a raw physical count including expired-pending-GC / lifecycle-hidden rows) is unchanged; whether the exported gauge should track `total` or `live` is a separate wire-meaning question, deliberately not folded in here. Regression: `src/background/memories_gauge.rs` unit tests (a `SqliteStore` standing in for any `MemoryStore` publishes its corpus count while the empty sidecar publishes `0`; a failed SAL read retains the previous value + freshness stamp; the `spawn_sal` loop ticks; a zero interval disables it) plus the live-postgres twin `tests/pg_memories_gauge_2621.rs` (the SAL gauge's published count grows by exactly the rows inserted into the pg corpus).
### Fixed (PreCompaction/PreArchive hooks advertised a destructive-op gate that never fired — one wired, one removed)

- **The `PreCompaction` and `PreArchive` hook events advertised a fail-closable gate over destructive operations but had NO production fire site — a governance control that reports a capability it does not have** ([#2637](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2637); data-integrity North Star; CWE-284; the #2444 false-success class applied to a governance control; 5-agent vote `4d3ea1c5`, verdict W-C 4/5). Both events lived in the public `HookEvent` enum, the `is_pre_event`/`event_class` tables, and their doc-comments promised fire sites — but `PreCompaction`'s only implementation was a `#[cfg(test)]` stub returning a hardcoded `true`, and `PreArchive` was never referenced outside the enum + tables. An operator who configured a `pre_compaction`/`pre_archive` hook with `fail_mode = "closed"`, believing they had interposed on a destructive path, had interposed on nothing.
  - **`PreCompaction` — WIRED (the genuinely-ungated destructive path).** The curator's autonomous `ConsolidationPass::run` (`src/curator/compaction.rs`) hard-DELETE-merges near-duplicate memories via a direct SAL `store.consolidate` call, which the caller-facing `PreConsolidate` consult (the MCP/HTTP `memory_consolidate` handlers) never covers — so this is the one destructive path with no gate. `run()` now consults the `PreCompaction` gate per eligible cluster BEFORE the destructive merge (no summarise, no persist, sources untouched on a Deny), via the process-global pre-event enforcement gate (`crate::mcp::consult_pre_event_gate`, the #1885/#2356 precedent). The curator boot (`Command::Curator`, `src/daemon_runtime.rs`) now INSTALLS that gate — mirroring `run_mcp_server` (#1885) and `bootstrap_serve` (#1924) — so the consult actually fires in the curator process rather than being silently inert. `PreCompaction` is now eligible to appear in `[hooks].required_events`, so an operator can declare it required and fail-closed the merge when no `pre_compaction` hook is present. Default (enforce off) is byte-identical to pre-#2637.
  - **`PreArchive` — REMOVED (vestigial; wiring was architecturally wrong).** Archive is REVERSIBLE (rows move to `archived_memories` and restore via `restore_archived`), and its only reachable fire site (`db::archive_memory_no_tx`) is a SYNC helper inside an open rusqlite write transaction / bulk-gc sweep, where a blocking async hook consult would hold the single sqlite write lock per-row across an unbounded hook round-trip (a self-deadlock hazard). Half-wiring only some archive paths would relocate the same #2637 defect, so the variant + all advertisement were removed rather than left lying. The client-visible `hook_events_count` capabilities value drops 27 → 26 (`HOOK_EVENTS_COUNT`), which is the truthful count — the envelope no longer advertises a phantom hook. A `hooks.toml` naming `event = "pre_archive"` now fails loudly at config-parse time (a loud error beats a silent no-op).
  - **Regression:** `src/curator/compaction.rs::run_pre_compaction_deny_aborts_the_merge_2637` (R-203) proves a Deny aborts the merge in a live `ConsolidationPass::run` — `memories_consolidated == 0`, both sources survive, no `[consolidated]` row, the summariser is never reached; at the parent commit the merge proceeds. The removed-surface count is pinned by `tests/hook_pipeline_exhaustiveness.rs` (26 events / 13 pre-events), `src/hooks/{events,timeouts}.rs`, and `tests/curator/compaction_test.rs` (`hook_events_count == 26`).
### Fixed (kg(AGE): the unreachable AGE `find_paths` Cypher reader is deleted, closing the `kg_backend=Age` honesty gap)

- **`PostgresStore::find_paths_cypher` and its `build_find_paths_current_view_cypher` builder are DELETED** (refs [#2613](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2613); "does what it claims" cert standard; 5-agent adversarial vote `4d3ea1c5`, unanimous DELETE). The builder emitted an `ALL(e IN relationships(p) …)` guard that Apache AGE 1.7.0 — the SSOT-pinned version — rejects at parse time (`ALL`/`ANY`/`NONE` are grammar keywords there, and AGE 1.7 implements no list predicates, comprehensions or `filter()`), so the AGE `find_paths` reader NEVER succeeded on the pinned version. Since [#2582](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2582) the `find_paths` dispatcher routes to the relational recursive-CTE UNCONDITIONALLY on BOTH `KgBackend` values (measurement-backed: a PARSEABLE AGE depth-4 traversal is a `Seq Scan` over all vertices that scales with |V| not depth, ~877x slower than the CTE with no crossover), so the reader was retained-but-dead — a trap advertising a `KgBackend::Age` capability the runtime never reaches. Porting it would have produced parseable-but-still-uncalled dead code; deletion is the truthful close. The now-moot #2032 L4 inlined-id Cypher-injection surface is removed WITH it (no such statement remains to guard).
- **Capability/telemetry honesty gap closed:** an AGE deployment now emits a one-shot connect-time WARN stating `find_paths` is served by the relational CTE (not an AGE traversal) — the honest replacement for the per-call `warn_age_fallback_pair` that #2582 correctly removed but left with no signal. `Capabilities.kg_backend` still reports `Age` because `kg_query` / `kg_timeline` / `lineage` DO use AGE Cypher; only `find_paths` is CTE-served.
- **Tests:** the misleadingly-named `tests/g5_find_paths_cypher_no_syntax_error.rs` is renamed to `tests/g5_find_paths_cte_served_on_age.rs` and repurposed as the regression proving `find_paths` on an AGE-installed daemon returns a 200 with a correct path via the CTE (no Cypher invoked); `tests/age_cte_equivalence.rs` + `tests/cov_ga2_postgres.rs` (and the `postgres.rs` live coverage test) are repointed at the `find_paths` dispatcher — what production serves — preserving the #1689 invalidated-edge invariant via the CTE's `valid_until` predicate; the two builder-only unit tests and the comment references across g2/g4/issue_1482/memory_find_paths are reconciled. `find_paths` results were and remain correct throughout (the CTE reads the durable `memory_links`).

### Fixed (federation catch-up pullers: row-loss on transient error, `serve`-puller stall, and inbound-attestation bypass)
### Fixed (`store_parity_gaps` pg inbox carve-out cell is now hermetic on a fresh postgres database)

- **The `store_parity_gaps::postgres_side::pg_parity_private_leak_and_bypass_a7_1720` cell no longer depends on accumulated certified-tier state — it establishes its own precondition and so passes on a freshly created postgres database AND the shared tier** ([#2645](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2645); test-hermeticity, single-correct-answer fix, no vote). The postgres visibility SQL keys the owner (`metadata->>'agent_id' = $caller`) and inbox recipient (`metadata->>'target_agent_id' = $caller`) carve-outs on `ctx.effective_principal()`, which returns `as_agent` when set (`src/store/mod.rs`). The cell set `bob_ctx.as_agent = Some(NS)` and `alice_ctx.as_agent = Some(NS)`, so both callers' effective principal was the NAMESPACE `"fortitude/X"` — which never equals the seeded `target_agent_id = "ai:bob"` / `agent_id = "ai:alice"`, so the recipient carve-out (line 2894) could not fire from the cell's own seeded rows. It only passed against the long-lived certified tier where a pre-existing row happened to satisfy the query — an undeclared dependency on accumulated state (it FAILED on a greenfield pg). The fix binds each non-admin caller's `as_agent` to its OWN agent identity so the owner + target carve-outs fire from the cell's own seeded rows, without weakening the assertion (it still proves the recipient reads the inbox row and a non-owner/non-recipient does not leak alice's private row).

- **The federation catch-up pullers no longer permanently lose a row on a transient store error, no longer stall the `serve` puller on an all-filtered window, and no longer accept a forged inbound write the `/sync/push` path would reject** (refs [#2714](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2714) CB-10 + [#2715](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2715) CB-11; epic #2705 B-4; data-integrity North Star; CWE-345). There are TWO catch-up pullers and a prior fix ([#2663](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2663), the #2441 `next_since` watermark) only touched one of them — the two defects lived on the paths #2663 did not fully close, so both are fixed here as one coherent change to the shared federation catch-up lane.
  - **(CB-10, DATA LOSS — `sync_cycle_once`, the `sync-daemon` puller, `src/daemon_runtime.rs`.)** The apply loop discarded each `db::insert_if_newer` result (`let _ =`) and then advanced the per-peer cursor to `advance_to` UNCONDITIONALLY of whether the row durably applied — and #2663's `next_since` fix made it WORSE, leaping the cursor to the peer's examined-watermark far past any individually-failed row. A transient `SQLITE_BUSY` (or sibling) on one pull therefore PERMANENTLY dropped that row from this replica, because the strict `updated_at > since` delta never re-offers it. The loop now adopts the `catchup_halted` discipline the `serve` puller got right in #1687: it HALTS at the first non-durable apply and advances `sync_state` only to the last DURABLE success (`/sync/since` orders rows `updated_at` ASC, so the pre-failure high-water is ≤ the failed row's timestamp), so the failed row — and everything after it — is re-pulled next cycle. Skips are logged + counted, never silent.
  - **(CB-11 part 1, STALL — `catchup_once_with_store` / `catchup_once_legacy`, the `serve` puller, `src/federation/receive.rs`.)** The `serve` puller read only `body["memories"]` and did `if memories.is_empty() { continue }`, never consuming the peer's `next_since` examined-watermark. A window the peer filtered entirely out-of-scope (its per-peer allowlist + `scope=private` filter run IN MEMORY, AFTER the SQL `LIMIT`) came back `count:0` behind an HTTP 200, so `sync_state` never advanced and the IDENTICAL window was re-requested forever — the replica could never reach the in-scope rows beyond it, while every signal read "in sync". The puller now consumes `next_since` through a shared, HALT-GATED, VALIDATED resolver (`resolve_catchup_advance`): a CLEAN window advances to the validated `next_since` (so an all-filtered/empty window converges), while a window that HALTED on a transient apply advances only to the last durable success — so closing the stall does NOT open the CB-10 row-loss on this puller. The peer-controlled `next_since` is held to the SAME #2718 cursor-poisoning guard `sync_cycle_once` uses (RFC 3339, within `PULL_CURSOR_FUTURE_SKEW_SECS`, strictly ahead), with `latest_ts` as the fallback for a legacy peer that publishes no `next_since`.
  - **(CB-11 part 2 / B-4, ATTESTATION BYPASS — both pullers, both backends.)** Both catch-up pullers applied pulled rows with only a namespace-scope check and NO per-write content attestation, so a forged `metadata.write_signature` the `/sync/push` receive path REJECTS was silently accepted through the pull door and rows landed with whatever `attest_level` the wire asserted. A shared read-direction gate (`crate::handlers::federation_receive::attest_inbound_pull_memory`) now verifies a presented signature against the claimed author's locally-ENROLLED key (`crate::identity::verify::lookup_peer_public_key` — the backend-UNIFORM source the federation signal/transition author lanes use), REDACTING to the to-be-persisted form first (#2340) so the attestation commits over exactly the bytes stored: a forged/tampered signature is an explicit `Err` → the row is REFUSED (skipped, fail-closed; no `.is_ok()` masking); a verified one lands `agent_attested`; an unsigned row (or an author with no enrolled key) DEGRADES to `claimed` (accept-and-flag — the pull direction has no attested relayer to hold accountable, so this is the North-Star "degrade, never corrupt"). A pulled row is self-attributed (there is no #238-attested relayer on the GET response), so the strict-flip's honored-third-party refusal is inert here and self-authored replication is never bricked.
  - **Backend parity:** CB-11's stall fix is on the `serve` puller (`spawn_catchup_loop_with_store`, which `serve` spawns for both sqlite and postgres backends — the store-aware SAL branch and the sqlite branch both consume `next_since` identically); CB-10's row-loss fix is on `sync_cycle_once`, the `sync-daemon` CLI puller, which is sqlite-only by construction. The B-4 attestation gate is backend-UNIFORM (the on-disk enrolled key store, not the sqlite-only `db::agent_pubkey` registration source). Regression: `src/federation/receive.rs` unit tests (`resolve_catchup_advance`: a halted window never advances to `next_since`; an empty/all-filtered window advances via `next_since`; a far-future `next_since` is refused) and `src/handlers/federation_receive.rs` unit tests (`attest_inbound_pull_memory`: a forged signature is refused, a valid one upgrades to `agent_attested`, an unsigned row is flagged `claimed`).

### Fixed (federation cursor poisoning: three peer-controlled `sync_state` vectors closed)

- **The federation sync cursor can no longer be poisoned by a peer** (refs [#2718](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2718); CB-14; relates [#2670](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2670); CWE-284/CWE-20). Three peer-controlled paths could permanently pin this node's per-peer catch-up cursor (`sync_state`) or silently skip undelivered rows, each behind an HTTP 200 that reads as "in sync" — the data-integrity North Star's "DEGRADE, never lose data" was violated. **(1) Pull cursor (`next_since`):** the `/sync/since` response field is peer-controlled and was written straight into `sync_state` through a monotonic (refuse-to-REGRESS) upsert, so a peer answering `next_since:"9999-12-31T23:59:59+00:00"` permanently PINNED the puller's cursor — every later pull returned zero rows and nothing could lower it without a manual DB edit. `sync_cycle_once` (`src/daemon_runtime.rs`) now validates the candidate via `validate_pull_cursor` BEFORE honoring it: it is REFUSED if it fails RFC 3339 parse, LEADS the local wall-clock by more than `PULL_CURSOR_FUTURE_SKEW_SECS` (300 s — generous for NTP drift, fatal to far-future poison), or is not STRICTLY greater than the current cursor (lexical, matching the downstream `sync_state_observe` / server `updated_at > since` semantics). On rejection the cursor is left UNCHANGED and a WARN fires — the pulled rows still apply; the node simply re-pulls the same window next cycle rather than skipping forward. The legacy `memories.last().updated_at` fallback (for peers not publishing `next_since`) is held to the same validation. **(2) Push clock (`sender_clock`):** the `/sync/push` receive funnel folded the sender's ENTIRE `sender_clock` into `sync_state` via monotone-max with NO per-key authorization (the #2670 class), so peer A could inject an arbitrarily-high timestamp for peer B's key and permanently pin B's cursor. The fold is now PER-KEY AUTHORIZED (`db::sync_state_merge_authorized`, called from `src/handlers/federation_receive.rs`): it accepts ONLY the entry keyed by `body.sender_agent_id` — a peer can advance its OWN clock entry and nothing else; peer A's push can never touch peer B's entry. **(3) Tie-group truncation guard (F7):** `/sync/since`'s `next_since_watermark` treated `examined.len() < limit` as "page not truncated", but `db::memories_updated_since` drops undecryptable rows (#2383) so `examined.len()` is POST-drop — one undecryptable row in a full page made it look short and advanced the watermark over a straddling tie group, silently dropping the rows sharing the boundary timestamp beyond the `LIMIT`. Truncation is now measured against the RAW pre-drop SQL row count (`db::memories_updated_since_counted` / `MemoryStore::list_memories_updated_since_counted`, overridden on BOTH the sqlite and postgres adapters — both drop undecryptable rows), so the guard is correct on both backends. **Postgres parity:** the `sender_clock` fold (vector 2) is sqlite-only — the postgres receive path never merged `sender_clock` into any `sync_state`, so it has no poisoning vector to gate and needs no new pg fold (adding one would ENLARGE the surface, not close a hole); vectors 1 and 3 are already backend-blind (the pull cursor rides the CLI sync client, and the tie-group raw-count fix ships on both adapters). Regression: `tests/federation_sync_state_merge_1709.rs` (a peer folds only its own key; peer A cannot advance peer B's key), `src/daemon_runtime.rs` unit tests (far-future / unparseable / non-advancing cursors refused, valid forward step + within-skew accepted), `src/handlers/federation_sync_since.rs` unit tests (a drop-shortened full page does not advance over its tie group), and `src/storage/mod.rs` unit tests (gated fold + raw count).
### Fixed (bulk_create honors on_conflict — default `error` no longer silently overwrites pre-existing rows)

- **`POST /api/v1/memories/bulk` now resolves each row's `on_conflict` with the SAME default as sqlite single-create (`error`), so a row colliding with a PRE-EXISTING stored `(title, namespace)` row is REJECTED as a `CONFLICT` (carrying `existing_id`) instead of silently, unrecoverably overwriting the stored content** (refs [#2725](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2725); CB-23; data-integrity). `bulk_create` never read `body.on_conflict`, so every row went to `db::insert` whose `ON CONFLICT(title, namespace) DO UPDATE SET content = excluded.content` replaced the stored content — and `insert_inner` takes NO pre-overwrite snapshot (unlike `db::update`'s `archive_reason='in_place_edit'` #1725 or the federation-merge `'federation_merge'` #1773), so the prior content was GONE and `ai-memory undo-edit` had nothing to restore. sqlite single-create has defaulted `on_conflict=error` (409 + `existing_id`) since v0.6.3.1; bulk had no such default. The fix resolves the shared single-create vocabulary (`error` | `merge` | `version`, `crate::mcp::tools::OnConflictMode`, default `error`) on BOTH backends: **`error`** (default) rejects a pre-existing collision into `errors[]` with the stored id and leaves the row UNTOUCHED; **`merge`** is the explicit opt-in to the content-replacing upsert; **`version`** renames the title to a fresh suffix so it lands as a NEW row. The **in-batch** `(title, namespace)` collapse (two rows in the SAME batch) is carefully distinguished from a pre-existing collision — sqlite snapshots the pre-existing ids BEFORE the sequential-upsert loop, postgres probes before the deferred batched INSERT — so it still collapses via `deduped_rows[]` and is never conflict-rejected. New envelope field **`updated_rows[]`** (`{index, superseded_by: <stored id>}`, mirroring `deduped_rows[]`) discloses, by input index, which rows overwrote existing content under `merge`. A conflict-rejected row now counts in `rejected`, never `updated`, so the reconciliation identity (`created + updated + deduped + rejected + pending == sent`) holds. Regression: `tests/bulk_on_conflict_2725.rs` (default collision is rejected + stored content unchanged; explicit `merge` updates + discloses the superseded id; in-batch dedup unchanged; a mixed batch reconciles) plus unit cells in `src/handlers/bulk.rs`.
### Fixed (HTTP+sqlite clear-standard enforces ownership; postgres unowned-vs-unresolvable)

- **`clear_namespace_standard_inner`'s sqlite arm threads the resolved caller into the clear params, and `PostgresStore::clear_namespace_standard` distinguishes an unowned standard from an unresolvable one** (refs [#2719](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2719) CB-6 + [#2704](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2704)-F2 CB-18; CWE-284). **(A, CB-6, HIGH)** the HTTP+sqlite clear path passed only `{namespace}` into `handle_namespace_clear_standard`, so its `identity_claimed` probe (`params.agent_id` present + non-empty) was FALSE and the entire #1777 owner gate + #2545 unresolvable-refusal block was SKIPPED — letting `DELETE /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/standard` from ANY api-key/keyless caller on a sqlite daemon delete the `namespace_meta` row, dropping the #2503 severed floor and re-opening the #2545 attack on the network surface (postgres already refused everyone here — the parity was inverted). The fix threads the header-resolved caller into the clear params EXACTLY like the sibling `set_namespace_standard_inner` (SET) path, so the same #1777 + #2545 gates run; a keyless caller resolves to a non-empty anonymous id and is refused against a named owner while an owner clear still succeeds and an unowned/`system` standard still passes (unowned-pass). **(B, CB-18, MEDIUM, postgres)** the owner pre-fetch decoded its `metadata->>'agent_id'` JOIN with `.flatten()`, collapsing `Some(None)` (row exists, `agent_id` SQL NULL → UNOWNED) and `None` (no joined row → unresolvable) into one `None`, so a legacy pre-#929 / federated / non-object-metadata standard was misclassified as unresolvable and REFUSED with a wrong "severed or dangling" error even though the sqlite twin ALLOWS it (the documented unowned-pass). The pre-fetch now decodes `Option<Option<String>>` and matches `Some(None)` (unowned → ALLOW, matching the sqlite `recorded_owner == ""` path) separately from `None` (unresolvable → refuse #2545). The #2545 unresolvable-refusal for a claimed/named caller is NOT weakened. Regression: `tests/ns_standard_clear_ownership_2719.rs` (sqlite: a foreign and a keyless clear of an owned standard are refused and the binding survives; the owner clear still succeeds) and `tests/ns_standard_clear_unowned_2704_pg.rs` (sal-postgres: an unowned standard clears via the unowned-pass; a severed `standard_id` still refuses with the unresolvable message).

### Fixed (Gate-1 lane census is now DERIVED from `SyncPushBody`, not a hand-written literal)

- **The `/sync/push` write-lane census is reflected from `SyncPushBody` and `sender_clock` is registered, so a new wire field can no longer land green without a census entry** (refs [#2723](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2723); CB-3 / CB-21). The Gate-1 module (`src/federation/push_lanes.rs`) claimed "adding a new wire field without registering it here fails the unit test", but `ALL_SYNC_PUSH_WRITE_LANES.len() == 13` was asserted against a literal and the array was compared against a hand-written expected list IN THE SAME FILE — so adding `pub foo: Vec<X>` to `SyncPushBody` compiled and left every test green, and `sender_clock` (a peer-controlled `SyncPushBody` field that mutates local `sync_state` via `VectorClock::merge` in `sync_state_merge`) was absent from the census entirely. Now: (1) a **compile-time exhaustiveness pin** (`reflect_sync_push_fields`) destructures EVERY `SyncPushBody` field with **no `..` wildcard**, so a new field fails to COMPILE until its author classifies it; (2) a **reflection test** (`gate1_census_is_derived_from_sync_push_body`) asserts `ALL_SYNC_PUSH_WRITE_LANES` equals the destructured write-lane serde names IN ORDER, so a new `Vec<_>` subcollection cannot land green without a `SyncPushWriteLane` entry; (3) `sender_clock` and the other five non-lane fields are registered in the new `SyncPushMetadataField` inventory (`ALL_SYNC_PUSH_METADATA_FIELDS`), each carrying the new `ConfinementKind::SyncMetadata` variant that documents WHY they are not namespace-confined (namespace-agnostic transport metadata) rather than silently omitting them; and (4) a structural pin (`gate1_every_lane_is_handled_by_the_receive_funnel`, `include_str!` over `federation_receive.rs`) asserts each declared lane's wire field is read by the receive funnel, so a census entry cannot be orphaned from the CB-7 confinement sites. Census/reflection integrity only — the CB-7 funnel confinement itself (#2711) is unchanged. Regression: the three new tests in `src/federation/push_lanes.rs`.
### Fixed (bulk_create runs the post-commit stages single-create runs — audit, dispatch, postgres fanout)

- **`POST /api/v1/memories/bulk` now emits per-row audit, fires the `memory_store` subscription dispatch, and (on postgres) fans out to federation peers** (refs [#2724](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2724); CB-22). `bulk_create` re-implemented the single-create funnel and omitted three post-commit stages — the same re-implementation-omits-a-stage root cause as #2550/#2551/#2552/#2588/#2594, now closed for the post-commit half. **(F1) Audit:** the bulk funnel emitted ZERO `AuditAction::Store` rows on either backend, so a fleet corpus load left an invisible gap in the tamper-evident chain while single-create wrote one Store row per memory (`create::fanout_and_assemble_create_response` sqlite, `create_memory_postgres` pg). **(F2) Dispatch:** the bulk funnel fired ZERO `subscriptions::dispatch_event` on either backend, so a registered `memory_store` subscriber received nothing from a bulk write while single-create dispatched the event on both backends. **(F3) Postgres federation fanout:** `bulk_create_postgres` ended at the batched `store_batch` with no `broadcast_store_quorum` / `bulk_catchup_push`, so a postgres daemon with `--quorum-peers` silently did not replicate bulk rows — the sqlite branch already fanned out; the fanout is now shared by both backends. All three stages fire ONCE per DISTINCT persisted row (`created + updated`, last-wins so an in-batch `(title, namespace)` collapse draws one audit line / one dispatch / one broadcast, never one per input index) and NEVER for a rejected / skipped / pending row, so partial-failure semantics stay honest and the reconciliation identity (`created + updated + deduped + rejected + pending == sent`) is unchanged; a post-commit federation failure still lands only in `warnings[]` (ADR-0001, never rolled back). Regression: `tests/bulk_post_commit_stages_2724.rs` (sqlite: a bulk write emits N Store audit rows; a wiremock `memory_store` subscriber receives one dispatch per committed row; an in-batch collapse and a rejected row draw no extra audit/dispatch) plus the `sal-postgres` federation twin in `tests/federation_postgres_fanout.rs`.
