### Fixed (federated governance-lane namespace confinement — `pendings[]` / `pending_decisions[]`)

- **The federated `pending_decisions[]` lane executed an ARBITRARY-namespace write, delete, promote and reflect, routing around every namespace gate the confinement campaign had landed** ([#2478](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2478), CWE-284). Approving an inbound pending reaches `db::execute_pending_action`, whose arms call `insert()` with the PAYLOAD's namespace, `delete()` on an attacker-chosen `memory_id` with no namespace check at all, `promote_to_namespace()` into `payload.to_namespace`, and `reflect()` over every `payload.source_ids[i]`. The only gate on the lane was `pending_author_authorized` (#1920), which inspects `requested_by` and the payload's `metadata.agent_id` — it never consults `pa.namespace` and never resolves `pa.memory_id`. Reachable under **DEFAULT config** by a correctly-enrolled, correctly-scoped, TOFU-passing peer; probed end-to-end to a destroyed row during the #2497 adversarial review. Both `pendings[]` and `pending_decisions[]` now route every namespace their execution would touch through the SHARED `receive_auth` verdict the `memories[]` / `deletions[]` / `archives[]` / `restores[]` lanes use, under the same ENROLLED-posture (`has_allowlist()`) wrap and honouring `AI_MEMORY_FED_REQUIRE_PUSH_NAMESPACE_SCOPE` (env row 147). Design decided by a 5-agent adversarial vote (`4d3ea1c5`), 5/5 ADOPT_WITH_AMENDMENTS; two lenses landed killer objections that changed the design, both recorded below because each would have shipped a GREEN test over an OPEN hole.
  - **`pa.namespace` is not the effect — gating it would have been theatre.** `execute_pending_action` **never reads** the pending row's declared namespace. A gate on that field passes while `payload.namespace` lands the write somewhere else entirely: a peer scoped `public/**` sends `namespace: "public/ok"` with `payload.namespace: "secure/ops"` and the arbitrary-namespace write lands exactly as before — now under a regression test asserting the lane is confined, and with the issue retired. The gate therefore resolves the **UNION** of every namespace the executor can reach: `pa.namespace` plus `payload.namespace` (store / reflect) plus `payload.to_namespace` (promote) as CLAIMED namespaces, and the STORED namespace of `pa.memory_id` (delete / promote) plus of every `payload.source_ids[i]` (reflect, which mints a signed `reflects_on` edge onto each source) as BY-ID namespaces. ALL must be in scope.
  - **The issue's own acceptance criterion was satisfiable by the wrong fix.** "A `public/*`-scoped peer cannot land a `secure/ops` row via the pendings+decisions pair" also passes if you gate ONLY the `pendings[]` injection — the pending never lands, so the decision has nothing to execute — while the lane the issue TITLES stays wide open: a `pending_decisions[]` push against a pending row that already exists locally, minted by a local operator or arrived in an earlier push. That cell (`exploit_decisions_only_against_local_pending_2478`, whose push carries **no** `pendings[]` at all) is the structural answer, and the pending row is resolved from LOCAL STORAGE rather than from the same request's `pendings[]` — gating against attacker-supplied input would be a TOCTOU on the gate's own premise.
  - **The `pendings[]` upsert is `ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE` over every column, so the primitive could simply move one hop upstream.** Without a stored-namespace check a `public/**` peer could RELOCATE and overwrite a `secure/ops` governance row by pushing its id under an in-scope namespace, then let a trusted LOCAL approver detonate it through an approve surface that has no peer scope to consult. That is the same merge-clobber vector Layer 1's stored-namespace check closes for `memories[]` (#2447), and it is now checked here too.
  - **The `promote` arm's DESTINATION is gated, which the issue text did not ask for.** #2478 named only "the target row's stored namespace" for that arm; `promote_to_namespace` **clones** the row into `payload.to_namespace`, so the destination is a write in its own right. `promote_to_namespace` requires an ancestor, so the escape is upward — a peer scoped to a leaf, promoting into a parent it may not touch.
  - **An unknown `action_type` is DEFAULT-DENY.** The type is parsed into the closed `GovernedAction` vocabulary and matched EXHAUSTIVELY, so adding a variant to that enum is a compile error at the gate rather than an arm that silently slips past it.
- **A federated pending-executed hard DELETE was INVISIBLE in the HTTP 200** ([#2478](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2478), data-honesty). It incremented no destructive counter at all, so an operator reading the envelope could not tell that rows had been erased by the push — the receiver reported `{"deleted": 0, "pending_decisions_applied": 1}` while the row was gone (pinned verbatim in the R-203 parent evidence). `deleted` now counts it. Because the executor's delete arm **discards** `db::delete`'s boolean, the handler cannot tell a removal from a no-op on an absent id after the fact, so existence is resolved by a scalar pre-probe under the already-held sqlite mutex; an unresolvable probe UNDER-reports rather than claiming a destruction that may not have happened. This widens `deleted` from "`deletions[]` entries applied" to "rows hard-deleted by this push" — verified NOT a wire-shape change: no sender path consumes it (`sync.rs` `post_once` reads `ids` / `unsupported_on_postgres` / `skipped`, and `success_report_non_ack_reason` never looks at `deleted`), so quorum accounting is unaffected.
- **A failed `execute_pending_action` was reported as a SUCCESSFUL decision** ([#2478](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2478), data-honesty). The error only WARNed while `pending_decisions_applied` had already been incremented and `skipped` stayed `0`, so `success_report_non_ack_reason` saw a clean report and the **sender ACKed a write that does not exist on the receiver**. It now increments `skipped`, which is what demotes the peer's 2xx to a non-ack (#2341).
- **The REJECT arm is deliberately left OUTSIDE the gate — a security decision, not an omission.** Gating it would make the posture WORSE: a reject is the only message that moves a row out of `pending`, and `execute_pending_action` gates solely on `status == "approved"`. Refusing a reject leaves the row `pending` and therefore still APPROVABLE locally, so the gate would keep alive precisely the authority-granting action the originator killed, while the sender saw a `skipped` non-ack it can never clear — the #2491 class with worse consequences. A reject grants no authority and writes only `pending_actions.status`.
- **Postgres — no behaviour change, and the claim is deliberately narrow.** `federation_signing_check::sync_push_via_store` already buckets `pendings[]` + `pending_decisions[]` into `unsupported_on_postgres` and never calls `decide_pending_action` / `approve_with_approver_type` / `execute_pending_action`, so the **federated** governance lanes never reach a pending-execution path on postgres — fail-closed AND honest, since `unsupported_on_postgres > 0` is a sender-side non-ack rather than a silent drop. That is NOT the same as "pending execution is unreachable on postgres": it IS reachable there through the LOCAL approve surfaces (`handlers::approvals`, `handlers::governance`), which are governed by local authz rather than peer scope and are out of scope for #2478. Per the #2488 lesson (the two funnels broke in OPPOSITE directions precisely because only one backend was covered) the pg disposition is now an executable assertion rather than a comment, plus a source note requiring any future trait-covered federation of these subcollections to route through the same verdict first.
- **Interaction with [#2503](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2503), stated so the issues cross-reference accurately — present at parent, neither introduced nor fixed here.** This PR's delete-arm gate confines WHICH memory row the lane may erase; it does not confine WHAT that erasure destroys. `execute_pending_action`'s delete arm calls `storage::delete`, which unconditionally executes a `namespace_meta` cleanup with no namespace predicate, so a delete this gate correctly ALLOWS still clears governance bindings beyond the row's own namespace. Two properties make this lane's exposure to #2503 sharper than the already-confined `deletions[]` lane: the gate added here is ENROLLED-only, so under zero-config the pendings lane retains the primitive untouched; and the arm discards `delete`'s boolean return, so the cleanup runs even when `pa.memory_id` names no local row. #2503's remedies change `storage::delete`'s signature or semantics with a blast radius across every local delete funnel, which is why it is a separate node. Nothing here should be read as closing it.
- **Tests:** `tests/federation_pending_ns_scope_2478.rs` (sqlite, 9 cells) + `tests/federation_pending_ns_scope_2478_pg.rs` (postgres controls, 2 cells). **Seven sqlite cells FAIL at the parent commit** `d2d93f86` and pass after: the pendings+decisions store exploit, the decisions-only exploit against a pre-existing local pending, the delete arm escaping its declared namespace by id, the promote arm cloning into an out-of-scope ancestor, the `pendings[]` clobber of a foreign governance row, the invisible-delete counter, and refusal visibility. The two CONTROLS are green in both directions by design — an enrolled-SCOPED peer acting IN scope must still apply, and the ZERO-CONFIG posture must be byte-identical to pre-#2478 (a gate that runs unconditionally is the #2491 silent-outage class in a new lane). The file builds its OWN router with `AI_MEMORY_FED_SYNC_TRUST_PEER` explicitly REMOVED, because the shared `build_router_fixture` pre-sets it and masks exactly these refusals — the #2497 lesson. Every assertion is on DB ROW STATE with counters secondary, and posture teardown is an RAII drop guard so a panicking assertion cannot leak an enrolled allowlist into the next test in the binary. The postgres cells were validated against live PostgreSQL 18.4 + `vector` + `age`.
- **Residuals, named rather than implied.** Zero-config keeps the arbitrary-namespace primitive on this lane (parity with #2447/#2488, called out in the source); the `store` / `promote` / `reflect` arms still increment no effect counter (only the destructive `delete` arm is fixed here, per the issue); an inbound `pendings[]` upsert can still resurrect a DECIDED pending back to `pending` and overwrite `decided_by` / `approvals`; a federated REJECT of a foreign-namespace pending remains an unauthorized veto; and the refusals added here are `skipped` inside a 200 with no DLQ enqueue ([#2498](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2498)). Separately still open: [#2479](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2479) (`namespace_meta[]` lane — closed by the entry immediately below), [#2503](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2503), [#2480](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2480) (pull direction), [#2489](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2489) (`links[]` / `signals[]`).

### Fixed (federated governance-standard namespace confinement — `namespace_meta[]` / `namespace_meta_clears[]`)

- **The federated `namespace_meta[]` lane let a peer rebind or re-parent ANY namespace's governance standard, with no scope gate whatsoever** (refs [#2479](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2479), CWE-284). Both loops validated `validate_namespace` / `validate_id` and nothing else before calling `db::set_namespace_standard` / `db::clear_namespace_standard`; neither consulted the peer's `allowed_namespaces`. That is an authz-CONFIG takeover rather than a data write: the row selects the standard memory whose `metadata.governance` `resolve_governance_policy` returns, so it rewrites the rules every subsequent LOCAL write to that namespace is judged against — approval level, approver identity, delete gating — and `namespace_meta_clears[]` is the same reach in the destructive direction. Reachable under **DEFAULT config** by a correctly-enrolled, correctly-scoped, TOFU-passing peer. Both lanes now route through the SHARED `receive_auth` verdict the `memories[]` / `deletions[]` / `archives[]` / `restores[]` / `pendings[]` lanes use, under the same ENROLLED-posture (`has_allowlist()`) wrap and honouring `AI_MEMORY_FED_REQUIRE_PUSH_NAMESPACE_SCOPE` (env row 147). Design decided by a 5-agent adversarial vote (`4d3ea1c5`): the union-with-declared-parent variant won on both plurality and Borda across five lenses, and one amendment was UNANIMOUS 5/5.
  - **The gated subject is the UNION of the row's namespace AND its declared `parent_namespace`.** `set_namespace_standard` persists the explicit parent that `build_namespace_chain` walks, and that chain is what `resolve_governance_policy` consumes — so the parent field changes which OTHER namespace's policy governs **by reference** rather than by value. A peer that owns the root namespace `alpha` could splice a namespace it may not touch into `alpha`'s chain and thereby displace the restrictive global standard for every `alpha/**` write. Two honest caveats are recorded in the source: `build_namespace_chain` consults the explicit parent only on the ROOT `/` segment of a queried namespace, so a parent stored on `a/b` is dead config and this gate is behaviour-relevant only for single-segment namespaces; and a parent of literal `*` is likewise inert (the chain walk skips it) yet is still gated for uniformity — an operator hitting that refusal should drop the redundant field, since the global standard is already in every chain.
  - **AMENDMENT E (5/5 unanimous) — the global `*` standard is refused unless the peer declared `**`.** `validate_namespace("*")` passes, so the literal global-standard key is reachable over the wire, and `build_namespace_chain` prepends `*` to EVERY namespace's inheritance chain: one row is the substrate-wide default policy. Meanwhile `glob_match("*", "*")` is `true` — a bare `*` pattern matches any single-segment target, and `"*"` contains no `/` — so an operator writing `allowed_namespaces: ["*"]`, documented as "any TOP-LEVEL namespace", would silently also be granting governance authority over every DEEP namespace that peer explicitly may not write. That is exactly the whole-tree widening [#1902](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/1902) closed inside `glob_match`, re-opened by a different door. The check therefore asks a different question — "did the operator declare `**`?" — answered by LITERAL comparison with no glob semantics involved (`receive_auth::peer_scope_is_allow_all`), and it runs BEFORE the layered verdict so it is **not** governed by env row 147: that knob is a per-peer rollout hatch for one config shape, and a hatch that hands over the governance default of every namespace on the node is not that.
  - **Refusing on the STORED parent was considered and REJECTED, twice over.** It looks like the #2447 merge-clobber lesson, but `namespace_meta`'s PRIMARY KEY *is* the namespace, so there is no id under which a row could be relocated and no stored-vs-claimed split to resolve — which is also why this gate needs no probe and the verdict is BACKEND-BLIND (it takes no connection), so a future trait-covered postgres funnel can call it verbatim. Refusing on the stored parent would BRICK the row: a namespace whose operator-set parent is out of a peer's scope could never be updated by that peer again — the stale-stricter failure made permanent, the [#2491](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2491)/[#2497](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2497) availability lesson. And it would not even hold: entries apply in wire order, so entry #1 could rewrite the parent to an in-scope value and entry #2 would then pass the probe — laundered inside a single request. A verdict that can be laundered in-batch is worse than an honest log line, because it reads as a control while providing none.
  - **What it DOES emit instead — the data-loss signal.** `set_namespace_standard` is `ON CONFLICT(namespace) DO UPDATE SET … parent_namespace = ?4`, and when the wire carries no parent the value written comes from `auto_detect_parent`, which resolves from the namespace STRING rather than from what is already stored. So an entirely in-scope push can silently NULL an operator-configured link to an out-of-scope ancestor, and a clear deletes it outright — unintentional config loss that was previously visible nowhere. A WARN now names the severed link and the remedy. It is OBSERVABILITY ONLY and deliberately best-effort in the fail-OPEN direction (a read error logs and proceeds), which is safe precisely because no verdict consults it — the inverse of the `CAUSE_NAMESPACE_PROBE_UNRESOLVABLE` sites, where an unresolvable probe MUST fail closed. Stated honestly rather than flatteringly: BOTH `namespace_meta` accessors collapse a read error into "no row" today — `db::get_namespace_parent` ends in a bare `.ok()`, and `db::get_namespace_meta_entry` is `#[allow(clippy::unnecessary_wraps)]` and does the same before wrapping in `Ok` — so this site's `Err` arm is UNREACHABLE as the code stands and a genuine storage fault silently costs the WARN. The latter accessor is used anyway because it returns the whole row and its signature can already carry an error, making a future tightening a one-line change there rather than a call-site rewrite; the source comment says so in those words so nobody later reads this as "fails closed on a read error".
  - **A new `namespace_meta_refused` counter, deliberately NOT folded into `skipped`.** This funnel enqueues nothing to the push DLQ ([#2498](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2498)), so a refused entry is LOST rather than retried, and `skipped` already aggregates malformed ids, absent standard memories and quota refusals — the sender, the only party that can retry, could not attribute it. A governance-replication stop is invisible in a way a memory-replication stop is not: both nodes keep answering `get_standard` confidently with divergent policy. The clear lane also gets its own lane token so `lane_is_destructive` gives it the destructive refusal prose (the #2488 lesson: never tell an operator "your write scope would be unbounded" about a `DELETE`).
- **Postgres — no behaviour change, and the claim is deliberately narrow.** `federation_signing_check::sync_push_via_store` already buckets `namespace_meta[]` + `namespace_meta_clears[]` into `unsupported_on_postgres` and never calls `MemoryStore::set_namespace_standard` / `clear_namespace_standard`, so the **federated** governance-standard lanes never reach a namespace-standard write on postgres — fail-closed AND honest, since `unsupported_on_postgres > 0` is a sender-side non-ack rather than a silent drop. That is NOT "namespace-standard writes are unreachable on postgres": they ARE reachable there through the LOCAL surfaces (`handlers::hook_subscribers::{set_namespace_standard, clear_namespace_standard}`, the MCP `memory_namespace_set_standard` / `_clear_standard` tools), which are governed by local authz rather than peer scope and are out of scope here. Per the #2488 lesson the pg disposition is an executable assertion rather than a comment, asserted in BOTH directions — an out-of-scope target and an IN-SCOPE one — because the structural claim is that the funnel applies NOTHING on this lane, which is strictly stronger than the sqlite gate's claim.
- **Tests:** `tests/federation_ns_meta_scope_2479.rs` (sqlite, 11 cells) + `tests/federation_ns_meta_scope_2479_pg.rs` (postgres controls, 3 cells). **Four exploit cells FAIL on ROW STATE at the parent commit** `5510158f` and pass after: the out-of-scope rebind (parent applies it, `namespace_meta_applied: 1`), the out-of-scope clear (parent destroys the row, `namespace_meta_cleared: 1`), the out-of-scope parent splice, and the Amendment-E global-standard push. The controls are green in both directions by design — an in-scope bind, an in-scope clear, an in-scope parent that must actually MOVE the resolved policy (otherwise the parent exploit cell would be vacuous), the deliberate `**` allow-all still reaching the global standard, ZERO-CONFIG byte-identical, env-row-147 honoured at the enrolled-unscoped shape, and per-entry refusal with the batch surviving. Two traps are pinned in the file header because each would have shipped a green test over an open hole: `set_namespace_standard` REFUSES when the `standard_id` memory is absent and the loop counts that as `skipped` with `namespace_meta_applied == 0` — the exact observable a scope refusal produces — so the exploit/control pair uses an identical seed and a BYTE-IDENTICAL body where only the allowlist differs, and every exploit cell positively asserts the standard memory EXISTS; and the parent cell asserts the RESOLVED POLICY on a SINGLE-SEGMENT namespace, since the same cell written against `public/x` would be vacuous. The file builds its OWN router with `AI_MEMORY_FED_SYNC_TRUST_PEER` explicitly REMOVED (the shared `build_router_fixture` pre-sets it and masks exactly these refusals), pins env row 147 explicitly in every cell rather than leaving it ambient, and tears posture down through an RAII drop guard. The postgres cells were validated against live PostgreSQL 18.4 + `vector` + `age`.
- **Residuals, named rather than implied — this closes the LANE, not the class.** (1) A peer scoped to an ANCESTOR still sets the DEFAULT policy of out-of-scope DESCENDANTS: `resolve_governance_policy` walks leaf-first and returns the first level carrying a policy, so a peer scoped exactly `["secure"]` governs every `secure/**` namespace that carries none of its own. Closing that needs pattern-vs-pattern subsumption, which the shared `glob_match` primitive structurally cannot express (it matches a pattern against a CONCRETE target), so the subtree variant was ranked LAST by the vote and disqualified rather than forked off the one #239 glob SSOT — filed as [#2536](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2536). (2) `standard_id` may still bind a memory in ANY namespace: that is the documented shared-policy feature, but `mcp::inject_namespace_standard` / `lookup_namespace_standard` then `db::get` that memory with NO visibility filter and inject it verbatim into every recall / session_start response for the bound namespace, while `memories.retain(…)` silently drops that id from the results array and decrements `count` — cross-tenant read amplification plus retrieval suppression, reachable from an entirely IN-SCOPE meta write and equally reachable from the LOCAL set-standard surfaces, so it is a separate node: [#2537](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2537). (3) `ApproverType::Agent(required)` is a bare string compare on BOTH backends — it never calls `is_registered_agent` and never rejects self-approval, unlike the `Human` and `Consensus` arms; filed with evidence as [#2538](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2538) rather than folded in, because it is an all-surfaces × both-backends governance-semantics flip needing its own vote and its own env/surface gating. (4) Zero-config keeps the arbitrary-namespace primitive on this lane (parity with #2447/#2488/#2478, called out in the source). (5) Refusals here are `skipped` inside a 200 with no DLQ enqueue (#2498) — the new counter is the mitigation, not a fix. Separately still open: [#2503](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2503), [#2480](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2480) (pull direction), [#2489](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2489) (`links[]` / `signals[]`), [#2498](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2498).

### Fixed (CI integrity lane — test-infra flake, L0-j family)

- **The six MCP-stdio subprocess suites no longer bound each JSON-RPC response with a fixed per-file `READ_TIMEOUT`; the bound is now elastic and fails fast on real breakage** (refs [#2525](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2525); test-only — no `src/` change, no MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration touched, no SSOT count moved). Observed on PR #2522 (a workflow-trigger-only diff, so the failure cannot be caused by the PR content): `cli_mcp_subprocess_reflect_empty_metadata_preserves_canonical_shape` panicked `mcp response did not arrive within READ_TIMEOUT: Timeout` at `tests/issue_1317_cli_reflect_wire_layer_preserves_caller_metadata.rs:205` after 10.21s, while its sibling in the SAME binary passed and a re-run of the whole cycle was fully green — timing, not logic. Six binaries each hand-rolled the same shape (spawn `ai-memory mcp`, pump the child's stdout into an `mpsc` channel on a reader thread, pop each response with one blocking `recv_timeout`) against three different hand-picked constants — 10s (`issue_1317_cli_reflect_wire_layer_preserves_caller_metadata`, `mcp_integration`), 15s (`issue_1590_default_namespace_write_paths`, `mcp_governance_pre_write_hook_1583`), 20s (`mcp_governance_pre_action_1685`, `secret_screen_g29`) — with no stated basis for the spread. All six now route through the shared leaf helper `tests/common/mcp_wait.rs::recv_mcp_response`. **Why this is not merely a bigger constant, in three parts.** (1) **The budget is no longer a constant**: it is `MCP_RESPONSE_BASE_TIMEOUT × AI_MEMORY_TEST_TIMING_BUDGET_MULT`, the repo's existing slow-CI-host knob (CLAUDE.md env row #68, already `#[cfg(any(test, debug_assertions))]`-scoped in `src/hooks/timeouts.rs`), so a slower host widens the window with one env var in its job definition rather than a code change and a fresh round of constant-negotiation. (2) **Raising the base is now free, which is the only reason it could be raised at all** — the old 10s had to stay small because a large window also made *genuine* breakage slow to surface, the fail-fast half of the [#1713](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/1713) fix. The helper discriminates the two `RecvTimeoutError` variants: when the child dies, exits early, or closes stdout, the reader thread's `Sender` drops and the channel reports `Disconnected` in MILLISECONDS **independent of the budget**, with a distinct panic that says so, so a real failure is never mistaken for a timing flake and never waits out the window. The budget's only remaining job is bounding a genuinely-wedged-BUT-ALIVE child — #1713's orphaned-subprocess shape — where a generous bound costs a green run nothing. (3) **The base is derived, not guessed**: 60s matches this repo's own generous-bounded-wait precedents for subprocess work that should take well under a second (`GOVERNANCE_CLI_DEADLINE_SECS = 60` in `tests/integration.rs`, #1522; `FANOUT_OBSERVED_TIMEOUT = 1 min` in `tests/common/mod.rs`), i.e. ~20-30× the observed 2-3s cold-spawn `initialize` latency versus the ~3× the old constants carried. **Poll-until-deadline was considered and deliberately not implemented as a loop**: `mpsc::Receiver::recv_timeout` already wakes the instant a line arrives AND the instant the sender drops, and a single JSON-RPC response exposes no observable intermediate progress, so a slice-polling loop over the same channel would be behaviourally identical with extra wakeups — the substance of that option (a generous overall budget that still fails fast on real breakage) is delivered by (2) and (3). The legacy panic substring `mcp response did not arrive within READ_TIMEOUT` is preserved verbatim so CI-log greps for the old signature still match (the panic-shape-continuity discipline `tests/common/mod.rs::WaitForReadyError` follows for #1194), and the new message additionally names the failing request method, the elapsed wall time, the resolved budget, and the env knob that widens it. The helper is a `std`-only leaf module pulled in via the `#[path]` submodule idiom already used by `tests/atomisation.rs` / `tests/cli.rs`, deliberately NOT re-exported from `tests/common/mod.rs`, because that module drags `reqwest` + `ed25519_dalek` + `rusqlite` into every binary declaring `mod common;` and per-binary link weight in this repo has already caused a real CI failure once (the #1381 `postgres_env` doctest-link `Bus error`). **Deliberately NOT changed:** `tests/integration.rs` (its `drive_mcp_bounded` / `wait_child_bounded` pair is already the poll-against-a-generous-deadline shape from #1522, write-all-then-EOF-then-wait-for-exit, not a per-response blocking read), `tests/serve_integration.rs` and `tests/doctor_cli.rs` (HTTP-daemon readiness polls with `try_wait` liveness — already correct), `tests/erasure_cold_tier_2064.rs` (in-process channel assertions, several of which use a SHORT `recv_timeout` as the *assertion itself* — that no event fires — so widening it would invert the test), and `tests/mtls_nodelay_acceptor.rs` (a TCP socket `set_read_timeout` handshake budget, not an MCP subprocess).

### Fixed (CI integrity lane, GA blockers — required-check soundness)

- **The cancelled-duplicate carrier class is now statically HARD-BLOCKED across every workflow, not just the one that surfaced it** ([#2508](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2508) **structural half** — the carrier itself was fixed in [#2509](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/pull/2509), and this entry adds no new required context and moves no SSOT count). New **rule (d)** in `scripts/check-required-contexts.sh` fails a workflow that satisfies all three of: **(i)** it triggers on BOTH `push` and `pull_request`; **(ii)** at least one `push.branches` pattern can match a PR HEAD branch; **(iii)** it declares a `concurrency.group` with `cancel-in-progress: true` whose key is not event-distinct. That is the exact #2508 shape: on a push there is no `pull_request` context, so the house key's ternary falls through to `github.ref_name` = the head branch, while the same-repo `pull_request` event resolves to `head.ref` = the identical string — one group, two runs per SHA, one **always** cancelled, and the cancelled check-run row is permanent. `cancelled` READS AS PASS in `gh pr checks` while branch protection does not count it as satisfied, so the standard triage command conceals it and the branch wedges the day that context is added to `required_status_checks.contexts`. **Scope is every workflow in `.github/workflows/`, deliberately wider than the required-context carriers the other rules police**, because the artefact pollutes any PR's rollup and turns into a wedge the moment anyone requires that context — the class has to be dead *before* someone reaches for that reasonable-looking hardening step. **(ii) is decided against a declared corpus, not guessed:** each pattern is `glob_match`-ed (the same routine rule (a) uses, so the two cannot disagree about what a pattern means) against `PR_HEAD_PROBES` — the commit-type vocabulary CLAUDE.md pins, cross-checked against the measured head-branch prefixes of this repo's 300 most recent PRs (`fix` 150 · `feat` 38 · `docs` 35 · `campaign` 34 · `test` 8 · `refactor`/`ci`/`chore` 5 · `sec` 3 · `local` 1), plus a slash-less and a deep-nested structural probe so a bare `*` / `**` is caught. `main` / `develop` / `release/**` are deliberately absent (this repo's base branches), and an exact LITERAL that merely looks like a head — `feat/v0.7.0-grand-slam` in `coverage.yml` — matches no probe and is correctly NOT flagged, because it names one historical branch and cannot match a class of future heads. The residual is DECLARED rather than unmodelled: a merge-up PR (`release/v0.9.0` → `main`, 4 in repo history) does carry the twin while open; narrowing `push.branches` on the integration branch itself would cost the primary push lane, so the twin is accepted and named at the corpus. **(iii) is a deliberately conservative structural test, not an expression evaluator:** a group containing `${{ github.event_name }}` is proven event-distinct and exempt, and everything else is treated as colliding. Evaluating the expression for real would be the wrong kind of clever — the house key is precisely the shape that LOOKS event-aware and collides anyway, so a rule smart enough to see that will be wrong about the next expression, whereas requiring the discriminator to be VISIBLE is both checkable and confirmable by eye. A workflow with no `concurrency` block, or with `cancel-in-progress: false`, is NOT flagged: two SUCCESS runs are wasteful, not the cancelled-duplicate defect. **One live carrier found by the rule's first run and fixed in the same commit** ([#2523](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2523)): `c8-precheck.yml`'s `push.branches` carried `local/**`, and `local/install-815-816` was opened as a PR into `release/v0.7.0` — so eight gate contexts, several of them required, were one `local/**` PR away from the wedge. Narrowed to `main` / `develop` / `release/**`, the #2509 shape. A gate cannot land while it reds the workflow that runs it, and ledgering a defect the same PR could simply fix would be a pending-fix entry with nothing pending. **`token-budget.yml` is ledgered, not fixed here** ([#2506](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2506) is repairing it in parallel): its repair is not the one-line narrowing — its `pull_request.branches` omits `release/**`, so narrowing `push.branches` alone would leave a `feat/**` → `release/v1.0.0` PR with NO token-budget run at all, trading a cancelled row for a fail-OPEN. The new **pending-fix ledger** `scripts/qc-allowlists/dual-trigger-cancel-allow.txt` takes `<workflow-file> <push-branches-pattern> #<issue>` and the format is ENFORCED: the pattern scopes the excuse to the one overlap that was reviewed (a workflow that later acquires a DIFFERENT overlapping pattern fails normally), and the issue reference is mandatory so the ledger cannot rot into an unexplained suppression. Unlike the (b2) burn-down ratchet, a STALE entry here is a loud NOTICE rather than a failure — an entry excuses exactly one `(workflow, pattern)` pair, so once the carrier is fixed the line can only suppress a failure that no longer happens, and failing on it would red whichever PR merely LOST THE RACE to the carrier fix. **R-203:** the `--self-test` caught fixture is the VERBATIM pre-#2509 `tool-count-drift.yml` trigger + concurrency block (git `e74cac70`), not a paraphrase, so the leg is anchored to the text that actually produced the cancelled rows observed simultaneously on PRs #2499 and #2505. Four NEAR MISSES must each PASS — the #2509-narrowed triggers, `cancel-in-progress: false`, a push-only workflow, and an `event_name`-keyed group — so the rule is proven to fire on the defect and not on its neighbourhood; a rule that also rejects its own remedy is worthless. Three ledger directions are pinned (correct entry passes, an entry for a different pattern does not absolve, an issue-less entry fails). **Mutation-proved load-bearing:** nine mutants of the new code were run against the self-test — removing the rule, dropping each of (i)/(ii)/(iii), dropping the `event_name` exemption, keying the ledger by file instead of `(file, pattern)`, dropping the issue-format check, and making ledger suppression unconditional — and eight are caught. The ninth (dropping the `push`-trigger condition) is an EQUIVALENT mutant, since the parser only records `push.branches` underneath `on.push`; the check stays as defence against a future parser change and is commented as such. Two real weaknesses surfaced *from* that exercise and were fixed rather than documented around: the ledger now stores presence separately from the issue citation (keyed by the citation, a malformed entry stored an empty value and was silently ignored, so the format check "passed" for the wrong reason and could have been deleted unnoticed), and the pending/stale notices no longer read an assoc-array element unguarded under `set -u` (an unconditional-suppression mutant was hiding behind that crash). Parser extensions are additive — new `PUSH` and `CONC` records on the `--dump` stream, top-level `concurrency:` only (a job-level one cannot coalesce whole runs), `cancel-in-progress` read fail-closed as cancelling unless literally `false` — and all 17 workflows parse: 6 dual-trigger with base-only push branches (`ci` / `coverage` / `bench` / `batman-mode-acceptance` / `clients-ci` / `mobile-runtime`), 1 dual-trigger fixed by #2509 (`tool-count-drift`), 1 fixed here (`c8-precheck`), 1 ledgered (`token-budget`), 8 single- or no-trigger. Complements — does not duplicate — Section C4 of `scripts/test/test-ci-workflow-invariants.sh`, which pins the same precondition for the two DECIDER carriers specifically; rule (d) is the repo-wide structural version.
- **`tool-count-drift.yml` no longer leaves a permanent `CANCELLED` check-run on every PR from a `fix/**` or `feat/**` branch** ([#2508](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2508), duplicate-cancellation carrier only — the structural gate rule stays open). The workflow triggered on BOTH `push` and `pull_request` with `push.branches` including `feat/**` + `fix/**` — patterns that OVERLAP PR HEAD branch names — under a concurrency group that resolves to the SAME key for both events with `cancel-in-progress: true`. The push event has no `pull_request` context, so the ternary falls through to `github.ref_name` = the head branch; the same-repo `pull_request` event resolves to `head.ref` = the identical string. Collision guaranteed, not occasional: two runs fire for one SHA, one is always cancelled, and the cancelled check-run row is permanent. That matters beyond noise because `cancelled` is a fifth required-context disposition that **blocks a merge while reading as pass** — `gh pr checks` renders a cancelled run's rows as `pass`, so the standard triage command actively conceals it, and the moment anyone adds `tool-count grep gate` to `required_status_checks.contexts` (a reasonable-looking hardening step) `release/v1.0.0` wedges on every `fix/**` PR with the cause invisible in the obvious place. **Fix:** `push.branches` narrowed to `main` / `develop` / `release/**` — the shape `ci.yml` and `coverage.yml` already use, and the reason their always-run classify jobs were safe to require while this one was not. The `pull_request` trigger is UNTOUCHED and its `branches:` list is a BASE-branch filter, so every PR into `main` / `develop` / `feat/**` / `release/**` is still gated from any head branch; the only runs lost are push-event runs on a feature branch with no PR open, which is not where this gate's verdict is consumed. Concurrency-key semantics are unchanged — the collision is removed at the source rather than papered over with a per-event key suffix. Sibling carriers found by the same scan are NOT folded in: `bench.yml` already has the correct shape, and `token-budget.yml` has the same `feat/**` overlap but its `pull_request.branches` omits `release/**`, so narrowing its push list alone would leave a `feat/**` → `release/v1.0.0` PR with NO token-budget run at all — a fail-OPEN, tracked rather than shipped blind.
- **`token-budget.yml` now runs on `release/v1.0.0` PRs — before the merge, not after it — and stops emitting a cancelled twin on `feat/**` PR-head pushes** ([#2506](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2506), the sibling carrier #2509 deliberately left tracked). Its two trigger lists were asymmetric: `push.branches` was `[main, develop, feat/**, release/**]` while `pull_request.branches` was `[main, develop]`. On the branch that actually ships, the token ceiling (`TRIMMED_FULL_PROFILE_CEILING_TOKENS`, `tests/token_budget_guard.rs`) was therefore only ever evaluated on the POST-merge push — post-hoc notification, never prevention: a PR that pushed the MCP `tools/list` wire payload over budget merged green and the gate reddened afterwards on the shared branch, attributable to no PR and blocking nobody. **Both edits land in the same commit, because either alone is worse than the status quo.** Narrowing `push` alone (the one-line #2509 treatment) would have removed the `feat/**` PR-head overlap — the #2508 duplicate-cancellation class, where the push and same-repo `pull_request` events resolve this workflow's concurrency key to the same string and `cancel-in-progress: true` guarantees one run is cancelled, leaving a permanent cancelled check-run that `gh pr checks` renders as pass — but it would ALSO have left a `feat/**` → `release/v1.0.0` PR with no token-budget run at all, converting "a gate that never gates PRs" into a fully silent fail-open. Widening `pull_request` alone would have kept the cancelled twin. **Fix:** `push.branches` narrowed to `[main, develop, release/**]` (no PR-head patterns) AND `pull_request.branches` widened to `[main, develop, release/**]` — the shape `ci.yml`, `coverage.yml` and `c8-precheck.yml` already use. Net: every PR into `main` / `develop` / `release/**` is gated BEFORE merge, and each SHA produces exactly one run. Concurrency semantics are UNCHANGED; the workflow carries no `paths:` / `paths-ignore:` filter and deliberately gains none (a path-filtered trigger on a gate is its own wedge class, `scripts/check-required-contexts.sh` rule (c)). **Scope:** trigger lists only — no job, step, ceiling or `required_status_checks.contexts` change. Whether this gate belongs in the required set for `release/v1.0.0` remains a separate, operator-class branch-protection decision.
- **A code PR whose LAST push is docs-only no longer skips every heavy gate, and `release/v1.0.0` is no longer wedged by an absent required context** ([#2496](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2496), [#2494](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2494); INTEGRITY / one atomic commit **by necessity**). Two defects that partially cancelled each other, so fixing either alone was unsafe. **(A) The wedge.** `ci.yml`'s `mobile-cross-compile` was BOTH a `strategy: matrix` job AND carried a job-level `if: needs.classify.outputs.docs_only != 'true'`. GitHub evaluates a job-level `if:` **before** matrix expansion, so a skipped matrix job emits exactly ONE check-run bearing the UNEXPANDED template name — probed on docs-only commit `82d95ed2`: `skipped Cross-compile (${{ matrix.target }})` while BOTH required contexts `Cross-compile (aarch64-apple-ios)` and `Cross-compile (aarch64-linux-android)` were **never created**. An absent required context is `pending` forever and `enforce_admins: true` means no admin merge clears it. The same commit proves the correct shape: `Check (ubuntu/macos/windows-latest)` all EXPANDED and reported `success`, because the `check` job carries **no** job-level `if:` and guards every STEP instead. `mobile-cross-compile` now follows that pattern — job-level `if:` deleted, `needs: classify` kept, the guard moved onto every step. `if: always()` was **rejected**: it would report success even when `classify` failed or was cancelled, i.e. green on an unclassified diff; with plain `needs:` a failed classify skips the job and the required contexts go absent, which fails CLOSED by blocking the merge. Dropping the two contexts was also rejected on the merits — iOS and Android are shipped release channels (`release.yml` `mobile-ios` → xcframework, `mobile-android` → jniLibs) and this PR-time job is the Layer-1 catch for ~80% of mobile bit-rot. **(B) The classifier fail-open.** `classify` resolved ONE diff base for BOTH `docs_only` classification AND test-impact selection; on `pull_request` `synchronize` that base was `github.event.before` — the PREVIOUS PR HEAD — so a PR whose last push was docs-only classified docs-only **for its entire head**, and eight required contexts reported `skipped` (which branch protection counts as SATISFIED) while the three `Check` contexts reported `success` **vacuously** (the job runs and no-ops). This already merged into production: PR [#2031](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/pull/2031) landed on `main` as `4226d8d9` with **22 of 23 files non-docs** (`tests/conformance_corpus.rs`, two interpreter readers, 18 `.hex` vectors) and zero compilation, zero tests, zero clippy, zero cross-compile — its final commit was `docs(#1837): …`. It fired again on PR [#2497](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/pull/2497), a CWE-284 federated-delete confinement fix whose third commit was `CLAUDE.md`-only: the classify log reads `PR_BEFORE: 3023f6bb` / `--- Changed files (1 files) --- CLAUDE.md` / `docs-only diff — skipping Rust pipeline` on a 12-file two-backend security change, and Lint / MSRV / Postgres / SAL-only / vectorlite all skipped. The two bases are now **split**: classification uses `$PR_BASE_SHA` (the FULL PR diff) for every `pull_request` action, while test-impact selection alone may use the incremental `$PR_BEFORE` on `synchronize` — narrowing which `tests/*.rs` binaries run is a cost optimisation INSIDE an already-running job and never decides whether a gate runs. `coverage.yml`'s classifier already used the PR base and correctly reported `docs_only=false` on that same commit, so the correct behaviour existed in-repo and is now the shape both classifiers share (its load-bearing base resolution is commented so it cannot be "harmonised" back). **(C-bis) The impact lane carried its own copy of the same fail-open, one layer down — caught by probing this fix's OWN CI run, and it means the base split alone is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT.** `__SKIP__` is a DOCS-ONLY VERDICT: the consumer steps (`Run tests (impact-aware)` in `check`, `pg_test` in `postgres-feature`) treat it as "no-op the test step". But `scripts/ci-test-impact.sh` derives it from the INCREMENTAL base, so on a code PR whose last push is docs-only it still emitted `__SKIP__` even with `docs_only=false`. Measured on head `10e36665` of this very PR (a `CHANGELOG.md`-only last commit over 9 non-docs files): every heavy gate correctly RAN — `MSRV`, `actionlint`, `Dockerfile`, and both EXPANDED `Cross-compile` contexts all green — and then `Check (macos-latest)` logged `TEST_IMPACT: __SKIP__` / `docs-only diff — test step is a no-op`, so compilation and clippy were restored while `cargo test` still ran ZERO tests. A verdict the classifier did not reach must never be inferred from a narrower diff: `__SKIP__` is now honoured ONLY when `docs_only` is genuinely true and otherwise degrades to `__ALL__` (run more, never fewer), with the script run against a scratch `GITHUB_OUTPUT` so its emission is inspected BEFORE it can reach the real outputs — structural, not a hope that a later duplicate key wins. Both directions are pinned: the override fires on the code-then-docs shape and does NOT fire on a genuinely docs-only PR (the fast path survives). **(C) The empty-diff arm now fails CLOSED** on BOTH classifiers: `git commit --amend && git push --force` yields a fresh SHA with an identical tree, and the old `docs_only=true` inference let that neutralise eight required gates (plus `Per-Module Coverage Thresholds`) on a PR that is not docs-only at all — an empty diff vs the PR base means "no NET changes", never "docs only". **Why atomic:** on `release/v1.0.0` the wedge was the only thing holding the fail-open shut — a mis-classified code PR was jammed by the absent `Cross-compile` contexts — so fixing the wedge alone would have converted a latent fail-open into a live one. On `main` and `develop`, which require only the three vacuous `Check` contexts, no such accident existed, which is why #2031 merged. **New soundness gate** `scripts/check-required-contexts.sh` (bash + awk, fail-closed, `--self-test`, `--dump`; house idiom of `check-migration-ladder.sh`) statically enforces the whole class against a HAND-AUTHORED mirror of the required set at `scripts/qc-allowlists/required-contexts-release.txt`: **(a)** every mirror context equals a parsed static job `name` or an expanded matrix name from a workflow whose `pull_request.branches` covers the protected branch; **(b1) HARD-FAIL, never allowlistable** — a required context's job has BOTH `strategy.matrix` AND a job-level `if:` (the exact wedge); **(b2)** a job-level `if:` at all (the skipped-counts-as-satisfied class) fails unless listed in the burn-down ratchet `required-contexts-joblevel-if-allow.txt`, where a STALE entry also fails so the ledger cannot rot; **(c)** the carrying workflow's `pull_request` trigger exists and has no `paths:`/`paths-ignore:` filter (an out-of-filter PR wedges the branch identically with no `if:` in sight); **(b3)** in any `needs: classify` job with no job-level `if:`, EVERY step carries the `docs_only` guard, with a bare `actions/checkout@*` as the single structural exemption. The mirror is hand-authored from intent and **must never be regenerated from live API state**: one required context is `L3-boundary perma-ban gate (§25.3 S5 / RQ-10`, a YAML truncation artefact where the unquoted ` #1853)` at `c8-precheck.yml:75` opens a comment ([#2473](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2473)) — it matches today and is deliberately left alone, because regenerating the mirror would launder the truncation into the declaration and make rule (a) a tautology that passes forever. The gate's awk parser implements the real YAML scalar rule (a `#` preceded by whitespace opens a comment, `(#1174 PR10)` does not) and was cross-checked against PyYAML on all 58 jobs across all 17 workflows with zero mismatches. Wired into `c8-precheck.yml` unconditionally — no `needs: classify`, no job-level `if:`, no `paths:` filter, because a gate that polices the docs-only short-circuit must not be subject to it. **R-203:** `scripts/test/test-ci-workflow-invariants.sh` EXTRACTS the classifier shell verbatim from `ci.yml` and drives it over throwaway git fixtures (8 scenarios), then runs the same fixtures against the pre-fix block frozen at `scripts/test/fixtures/ci-classify-prefix-2496.sh` — the code-then-docs shape must classify `docs_only=false` against the live workflow and `true` against the frozen one, so a silently-broken extraction cannot make the assertions vacuous (the frozen block is a committed fixture rather than a `git show`, so the regression leg survives CI's shallow checkout instead of silently SKIPping). **Also fixed:** three stale `ci.yml` comments claiming `Lint (fmt + clippy)` / `actionlint` / `MSRV` are "Advisory (not in required-status-checks)" — live protection REQUIRES all three. **Deliberately NOT done at the time** (branch protection was frozen): requiring `Classify changes` + `Coverage classify (docs-only short-circuit)`, the two always-run jobs that between them decide the disposition of eleven required contexts. Both were declared as known gaps in the mirror — **that residual is CLOSED by the #2494-residual entry below, which supersedes this sentence.**
- **A single transient test flake no longer discards every later test binary's result** ([#2500](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2500), diagnostic completeness). `--no-fail-fast` was absent from `.github/workflows/ci.yml` entirely, so `cargo test` exits after the FIRST failing test executable. On PR #2497's run `30518877707` **attempt 1** (job `90794703373` — the attempt the default `/runs/{id}/jobs` endpoint hides, since it returns only the latest attempt, where the job shows `cancelled` and the abort is invisible), `e2_post_ship_dry_run` failed on a crates.io `[16] Error in the HTTP2 framing layer` inside its nested `cargo build`, the invocation aborted, and `tests/federation_delete_ns_scope_2488_pg.rs` — the binary proving a CWE-284 GA-blocker closed on postgres — appears NOWHERE in that log. A network hiccup in an unrelated tool crate silently withheld the evidence the PR existed to produce. Both watchdog-wrapped invocations (`run_tests` in `check`, `pg_test` in `postgres-feature`) now pass `--no-fail-fast`. **Probed, not assumed:** on a two-binary throwaway crate, the default run executed 2 binaries and never reached the later one at exit 101, while `--no-fail-fast` executed 3 and reached it at exit **still 101** — the flag cannot turn a red run green, only a red run into a red run carrying more evidence. Runtime stays bounded by the pre-existing #1492 per-invocation watchdog (1500s / 2100s) plus `timeout-minutes`, so fail-fast was buying early termination at the cost of the diagnostic remainder — and the remainder is where the proof lives. A static guard in `test-ci-workflow-invariants.sh` (Section B) keeps the flag from being silently dropped, including from the un-watchdogged fallback arm. Note for future triage: that abort evidence is reachable only via `/actions/runs/{id}/attempts/{n}/jobs` — the default `/actions/runs/{id}/jobs` endpoint returns the LATEST attempt only, where the job showed `cancelled` and the abort was invisible.
- **The two jobs that DECIDE the docs-only short-circuit are now declared required contexts, and a new hard rule keeps them decidable** ([#2494](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2494) residual; INTEGRITY). #2505 closed the wedge and the classifier fail-open but left the third finding of #2494 open: **the gating job was not itself gated.** `Classify changes` (`ci.yml`) and `Coverage classify (docs-only short-circuit)` (`coverage.yml`) between them decide whether ELEVEN required contexts run at all — the seven ratcheted `ci.yml` gates, `Dockerfile build (no push)`, the three `Check` contexts' work steps, and `Per-Module Coverage Thresholds` — while being required by nothing. One unrequired job pair governed the disposition of the entire required set outside `c8-precheck.yml`. **Both are now DECLARED in the hand-authored mirror** `scripts/qc-allowlists/required-contexts-release.txt` (24 declared; the live set is 22 until the companion branch-protection API call). **The safety premises are asserted, not assumed** — each is a live property that could regress: both jobs have no `needs:`, no job-level `if:`, no `strategy:` and no `paths:` filter, so they ALWAYS run and always report a real `success`/`failure`; on the docs-only commit `82d95ed2` that PROVED the #2494 wedge both reported `success`, making them the only two contexts in those pipelines that report a genuine success rather than `skipped` on a docs-only diff; and the [#2508](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2508) cancelled-duplicate hazard does not apply, because neither carrier's `push:` branch list (`main` / `develop` / `release/**`, plus the legacy literal `feat/v0.7.0-grand-slam` on `coverage.yml`) can match a PR HEAD branch, so exactly ONE run exists per SHA — probed on the heads of PRs #2497 / #2505 / #2499, each classify context present exactly once, versus `tool-count-drift.yml`'s context appearing TWICE (`cancelled` + `success`) on PR #2505's head `655ba732` because its push branches include `fix/**`. **New rule (b4) in `scripts/check-required-contexts.sh` — HARD-FAIL, never allowlistable:** a required context whose job is a DECIDER (another job in the same workflow declares `needs:` it, derived from the parsed `needs:` edges rather than a hardcoded job-id list) must not carry a job-level `if:`. Requiring a decider is free, but it creates an obligation that rule (b2)'s burn-down ratchet must NOT be able to absolve: a skipped decider skips its whole dependent subtree, and branch protection counts every skipped required dependent as SATISFIED — so a single allowlist line would buy the subtree, converting the control back into the #2494 fail-open with a paper trail that reads like an acknowledged carry-over. (b4) is therefore checked BEFORE (b2) and cannot be allowlisted. Mutation-proved against the REAL workflows: a job-level `if:` planted on `ci.yml`'s `classify` fails with `RULE (b4) HARD-FAIL` naming all nine dependents (`lint actionlint msrv check postgres-feature mobile-cross-compile sal-feature vectorlite-feature dockerfile-validate`). **Landing order is load-bearing and documented in the mirror.** The mirror is a PR and branch protection is an API call, so the two halves cannot be atomic. For an ADDITION the mirror lands FIRST: the gate can only apply its rules to a context the mirror declares, so mirror-first means the soundness proof is green in CI BEFORE the context becomes load-bearing — prove, then enforce. The intermediate state (declared, not yet required) blocks nothing, because GitHub never reads that file. The reverse order produces the strictly worse state — a live-required context that no in-repo file declares — which this gate structurally CANNOT detect (it runs statically, with no admin-scoped API token, by design), so its rule coverage would silently narrow while it still exits 0. For a REMOVAL the order inverts for the same reason. **R-203 SECTION C** in `scripts/test/test-ci-workflow-invariants.sh` pins all four premises per decider (declared name, no `if:`/matrix, `pull_request` covering `release/**` unfiltered, push-branch ratchet for the #2508 precondition), re-deriving the context STRINGS from the workflows through the gate's own audited `--dump` parser instead of hand-copied literals — so an unmirrored job rename fails here as well as at rule (a), the [#2473](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2473) class applied to the new contexts. Its regression leg runs against the mirror frozen at `scripts/test/fixtures/required-contexts-prefix-2494.txt`: under that pre-fix mirror the planted decider `if:` passes the gate SILENTLY, which is both the blind spot the declaration closes and the proof the leg is not tautological (a committed fixture, not a `git show`, so it survives CI's shallow checkout — the #2496 lesson). Each new leg was mutation-tested: renaming the decider fails C1, a `paths:` filter fails C3, adding `fix/**` to `ci.yml`'s push branches fails C4, and "repairing" the frozen fixture fails the regression leg. Harness 29/29. **Residual on #2494 after this lands:** the branch-protection API call itself (Fable 5, sole approver — files only in this change), and two `c8-precheck.yml` integrity gates that run on every PR but are still not required (`Installer checksum fail-closed gate (#2449)`, `Non-Rust conformance-reader proof gate (#2452)`) — both declared in the mirror's KNOWN GAPS block, neither a wedge risk. `main` / `develop` still require only the three vacuous `Check` contexts (#2496 fix 3, out of scope here). No MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration / Rust source touched — no SSOT count moves.

### Fixed (federation outbound TLS lane, L-FED-OUTBOUND)

- **`--insecure-skip-server-verify` is refused by default — outbound federation TLS must now verify the peer's SERVER certificate** ([#2448](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2448), SECURITY / confidentiality; **BREAKING** for anyone passing that flag). Federation replicates **plaintext** memory content — it is NOT end-to-end encrypted (`src/encryption/mod.rs`, [#1968](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/1968) is open with zero implementation) — so an unverified peer *server* certificate is a direct content-disclosure surface: an adversary in DNS or BGP position presents any certificate, the handshake completes, and this node pushes it every memory. The compensating control that posture leaned on cuts the **other way**: the peer fingerprint-pinning *our* client cert via `--mtls-allowlist` protects the PEER from an impostor CLIENT; it does nothing to protect US from an impostor SERVER, and that is the direction governing confidentiality. **The issue's headline premise was stale and is corrected here rather than repeated:** the daemon quorum client (`federation/peer.rs`) has always CA-validated, the `ai-memory sync` CLI has CA-validated since [#1794](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/1794), and the cited `src/tls.rs:1034` `DangerousAnyServerVerifier` site sat inside `tls::build_rustls_client_config`, a **public but production-DEAD** builder with zero callers outside tests. Two real residuals remained. **(1)** The accept-any disposition was a single flag away, with no env-level or posture-level way to forbid it. New `AI_MEMORY_FED_REQUIRE_SERVER_VERIFY` (env-table row #148) defaults **ON** using the house `env_flag_default_on` grammar (the `AI_MEMORY_FED_REQUIRE_WRITE_SIG` #94 / `_CHECKPOINT_SIG` #125 / `_POLICY_CURRENT` #132 shape), with an explicit falsy token as the staged-rollout escape hatch. It is **strictly additive, never a cheaper path**: accept-any still ALSO requires the flag plus BOTH `--client-cert` and `--client-key` — four conditions, not one — so the env var raises the bar rather than opening a second door. The refusal lives in the **pure** `tls::select_sync_tls_mode` (now `-> Result<SyncTlsMode>`) rather than at the call site, so it is *structural*: no present or future caller can resolve `AcceptAny` without explicitly threading `false` through. Server-cert PINNING still wins outright — a pinned host is verified by SHA-256(DER), so the flag alongside an active pin map is a no-op, not a refusal. The refusal message names the SECURE remedies first (`--ca-cert`, `AI_MEMORY_FED_PEER_FINGERPRINTS`) and the escape hatch last, pinned by an ordering assertion, so an operator hitting it is steered to fix the posture rather than to disable the control. **(2)** The `asi-hard` PROCUREMENT posture pinned **zero** network access-control knobs — its 14-knob SSOT was 100% crypto/attestation/durability, so an operator deploying `docs/deploy/asi-hard.env` verbatim could still run `--insecure-skip-server-verify`. `AI_MEMORY_FED_REQUIRE_SERVER_VERIFY` is now pinned at floor `1` in `security_profile::KNOBS` (14 → 15), which also makes the new escape hatch **itself no-disable** under `asi-hard`: a falsy override refuses boot. **`tls::build_rustls_client_config` is DELETED**, not deprecated — pre-GA is the only free window to drop a `pub fn`, and `#[deprecated]` emits a warning while leaving the accept-any arm live and callable by anyone who ignores it; `tests/mtls_nodelay_acceptor.rs` ports to a local builder with **every assertion byte-identical** (construction only, so the mTLS client-cert-pinning contract that file exists to pin is exercised exactly as before). `cli::sync::build_sync_client` was extracted so the TLS posture is constructible without entering the daemon's infinite sync loop. **Migration:** pass `--ca-cert <peer-ca.pem>` for a self-signed / private-CA peer, or set `AI_MEMORY_FED_PEER_FINGERPRINTS` to pin the peer's server cert by SHA-256 (strongest); only if you must keep the insecure posture for a rollout window, set `AI_MEMORY_FED_REQUIRE_SERVER_VERIFY=0` — settable BEFORE the upgrade, and refused under `asi-hard`. R-203: `tests/fed_require_server_verify_2448.rs::insecure_skip_server_verify_is_refused_by_default_2448` drives the production `cli::sync::run_daemon` (signature unchanged, so it compiles at both commits) and FAILS at parent `6d7b59d9` — the daemon accepts the insecure posture and enters its sync loop until the timeout elapses — and PASSES after. Three siblings drive REAL rustls handshakes against a self-signed fixture peer, proving the refused disposition genuinely WAS forged-certificate acceptance and that the CA-validated default rejects that same certificate. **Doc truth-fixes shipped alongside** (the docs described a control that no longer matched the code): `docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md`'s issue-#232 section flatly asserted `sync-daemon` "accepts ANY server cert" without `--client-cert` — false since #1794 and now replaced with a posture table; CLAUDE.md env row #85, `docs/federation.md` and `docs/federation-identity.md` each claimed the `ai-memory sync` CLI keeps `UnpinnedHostPolicy::AcceptAny`; `docs/federation-identity.md` also still listed `AI_MEMORY_FED_REQUIRE_WRITE_SIG` as "default `0` permissive" after #1954 flipped it; and `src/tls.rs` twice pointed operators at `docs/runbook/federation-tls.md`, **a file that does not exist**. Design resolved by a 3x3 adversarial vote (9 lenses, 6-3), citing `5-agent vote (4d3ea1c5)`. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration / schema-version bump — no SSOT-count move.

### Security (federation write-lane confinement, GA blocker)

- **The federated inbound WRITE lane is namespace-scoped — a peer scoped to `public/*` can no longer push into `secure/ops`** ([#2447](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2447), CWE-284 broken access control, HIGH; the one confidentiality/integrity finding in the v1.0.0 GA gap review, where everything else was a degrade class). `peer_attestation::namespace_allowed` had exactly ONE production call site in `src/` — inside the `deletions[]` loop (the #1934 fix). The pull lane (`/sync/since`) filters its projection through the peer's `allowed_namespaces`; the delete lane resolves each target row's namespace; the `memories[]` WRITE loop consulted **neither**. So an enrolled peer attested with `allowed_namespaces: ["public/*"]` could `POST /api/v1/sync/push` a memory whose `namespace` is `secure/ops`, have it persisted, and have it thereafter served to that tenant's agents as substrate truth — the peer did not need to escalate, the scope it was granted was simply not enforced on this lane. **The comment that hid it is deleted:** the text above the delete loop asserted the write lane was already confined *"via `resolve_inbound_attribution`"*, which is false — that resolver gates WHO you may claim to be (`metadata.agent_id` against `allowed_sender_agent_ids`), never WHICH namespace you may write into — and that false claim is why #1934 closed believing the whole class was covered. **BOTH namespaces are checked, and the second is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces:** `merge_memory` resolves the `namespace` field by LWW and `merge_inbound` field-merges ANY inbound row whose `id` matches an existing local row, so a claimed-namespace-only gate would still have let a `public/*` peer push `{id: <a known secure/ops row id>, namespace: "public/x", updated_at: now}` and thereby RELOCATE the protected row into its own scope while clobbering the title and content — a strictly worse outcome than the hard-delete #1934 already blocks. The R-203 before-run demonstrates exactly that (`left: "public/loot", right: "secure/ops"`). The same by-id reach was closed on the two sibling lanes in the same handler: `archives[]` (the soft-delete twin — still removes the row from every live read of a denied namespace) and `restores[]` (its resurrection twin, probing `archived_memories`). **Postgres carried, plus a second unfiled hole closed:** the twin `sync_push_via_store` received the same shared verdict function on `memories[]` AND the #1934 delete gate, **which had never landed on that backend at all** — `PostgresStore::apply_remote_deletion` discards its `_ctx`, so until now a `public/*`-scoped peer could hard-delete any `secure/ops` row on any postgres-backed node, and no test would have caught it (the #1934 regression test builds a sqlite router). The postgres namespace probe deliberately uses an admin context: `PostgresStore::get` folds a #910 visibility denial into `NotFound`, so a tenant-scoped context would report a hidden foreign row as "no such row" — fail-OPEN on precisely the rows the gate exists to protect. **Zero-config federation is byte-identical:** the gate short-circuits on `PeerAttestationConfig::has_allowlist()`. Calling `namespace_allowed` verbatim (as the delete lane does) would have refused EVERY inbound memory on every unconfigured deployment — its `scope_for == None` arm falls through to `sync_trust_peer_bypass()`, false by default — a silent total replication outage returning `200 {applied: 0}`; `zero_config_federation_write_still_applies_2447` pins that this can never regress. New knob `AI_MEMORY_FED_REQUIRE_PUSH_NAMESPACE_SCOPE` (env-table row 147, default ON via the shared `env_flag_default_on` grammar) governs only the residual shape — an enrolled peer whose `allowed_namespaces` is empty/absent, which today has zero read scope and zero delete scope while its write scope was unbounded; recover per-peer with `["**"]` or fleet-wide with the falsy token. Design crossroad resolved by a 3x3 adversarial vote (`4d3ea1c5` protocol); the permissive-default variant was ranked last by both voting lenses. Regression: `tests/federation_write_ns_scope_2447.rs` — 4 exploit tests FAIL at the parent commit `6d7b59d9` and pass after, plus 2 posture guards. Reads use new scalar `storage::{namespace_by_id, archived_namespace_by_id}` helpers rather than `db::get`, which would have re-run the full row decode + AES envelope open per pushed memory under the held global mutex and, under `DecryptFailurePolicy::FailClosed`, returned `Err` for a row sealed to another agent's key. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.
### Fixed (SUPPLY-CHAIN lane, GA blocker)

- **`install.sh` now refuses to install an unverified binary, and every release artifact ships a `.sha256` — the checksum step no longer passes by doing nothing** ([#2449](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2449), GA BLOCKER, HIGH supply-chain). Two halves composed into one control that always reported success. `install.sh` wrapped its entire verification block in `if download "$CHECKSUM_URL" … 2>/dev/null; then … fi`, whose `else` arm printed *"Warning: Checksum file not available, skipping verification"* and installed the binary anyway. Meanwhile `release.yml` emitted `.sha256` for exactly three assets — the CycloneDX SBOM, the iOS xcframework, and the Android bundle — and **none** for the desktop/server tarballs, the Windows zip, or the `.deb`/`.rpm` that the installer actually downloads. (`release.yml:631` does compute a sha256 per tarball, but that value is substituted into the **Homebrew formula**, never uploaded as a release asset.) So `$CHECKSUM_URL` 404'd on **every ordinary install**, the fail-open arm fired every time, and **no install via `install.sh` had ever verified the binary it installed** — this was the normal path, not an edge case. The fix is both halves: the `release` job now runs a whole-directory checksum **sweep** over `dist/` on both OS legs, in the same job that packages the artifacts, so a future artifact type is checksummed automatically rather than shipping unverified because someone forgot a line (the existing `files: dist/ai-memory*` glob then publishes the checksums for free; output shape is sha256sum's `<hash>  <name>`, matching the three pre-existing assets, and the Windows leg pins `-Encoding ascii` because Out-File/Set-Content default to UTF-16 on Windows PowerShell — a checksum file neither installer could parse). A sweep emitting zero files **fails the job**, because a sweep that silently did nothing would be this very defect. **`install.ps1` had no checksum verification whatsoever** — strictly worse than the fail-open branch, since it never even attempted a fetch — and now carries the same gate. **Three further fail-open/robustness defects were found in the same block and fixed:** a malformed or empty checksum body yielded `EXPECTED_HASH=""`, which fell straight through the `[ -n "$EXPECTED_HASH" ]` guard and installed the binary with **no message at all** (a second, quieter fail-open that a 200-response carrying a captive-portal or proxy error page hits exactly); the checksum download was called with `2>/dev/null`, swallowing `download()`'s own diagnostics so an operator never learned whether the cause was a 404, DNS, or the network; and a trailing value-taking flag (`install.sh --dir`) shifted past the end of the argument list so the bottom-of-loop bare `shift` tripped `set -e` with an opaque shell error. Both the expected and the computed digest are now validated as 64 lowercase hex characters, so any parse surprise fails CLOSED instead of comparing garbage. The hashing ladder is `sha256sum` → `shasum` → `openssl dgst -sha256` → abort (parsed from the DEFAULT output shape, never `-r`, so OpenSSL 3's `SHA2-256(f)= …` and LibreSSL/1.1's `SHA256(f)= …` both yield the digest as the last field); `python3`/`hashlib` is deliberately **not** a rung, because an interpreter whose own presence and version are unverified is not a supply-chain integrity tool. The bypass is `--insecure-skip-checksum` / `-InsecureSkipChecksum`, a **flag only and deliberately never an environment variable**: an env var can be set once in a base-image layer, a CI provider's env UI, or a shell profile and is then silently inherited fleet-wide forever, recreating the fail-open default invisibly, whereas a flag lives in the literal invocation and is greppable in every CI transcript and Dockerfile diff (`SKIP_CHECKSUM` is initialised to `0` before argument parsing and set only by the flag, so an exported `SKIP_CHECKSUM=1` cannot enable it; using it prints a DANGER banner on **both** stdout and stderr). All aborts route through one helper emitting the machine-readable token `ai-memory: install aborted (checksum gate #2449)`. **Scope stated honestly in the scripts themselves:** the checksum is served from the SAME origin as the archive, so this proves INTEGRITY (no corruption, truncation, or mirror/CDN substitution), NOT AUTHENTICITY against a compromised release pipeline — signed build provenance (cosign/sigstore/SLSA) remains tracked for v1.x per ROADMAP §17, and this entry does not claim otherwise. **Deliberately excluded** from the sweep: the bare, non-architecture-qualified `ai-memory` / `ai-memory.exe` binary the packaging step leaves in `dist/`, which all five matrix legs already publish under the same asset name and overwrite one another — a checksum for it could be raced against a different leg's binary, and a WRONG checksum is worse than none (no installer path fetches it). Design resolved by a 3×3 (9-agent) adversarial vote per the crossroads protocol (`4d3ea1c5`), trigger T3; the escape-hatch shape was decided 3-for-flag-only vs 1-for-env-only vs 2-for-both, and the openssl rung was admitted only on the condition — satisfied here — that it be exercised by a dedicated test. Regression: the new `scripts/check-install-checksum.sh`, wired into `c8-precheck.yml`, whose `--self-test` plants a missing and a mismatched checksum against the REAL unmodified `install.sh` and asserts it rejects both **by its abort token**, not merely a non-zero exit (writing that assertion caught the harness itself passing for the wrong reason twice), plus a valid-checksum accept, a no-hashing-tool abort, the openssl rung in isolation, and six planted static regressions (a deleted gate region in each installer, a restored fail-open phrase, a removed abort branch, a deleted release.yml sweep, a dropped sibling `.sha256`) with an unmutated control first. `--r203 <ref>` reproduces the bug against any historical revision: at base `6d7b59d9` the installer exits 0 and installs an unverified binary; after, it exits 1 and installs nothing. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.
### Fixed (DR lane, GA blocker)

- **`ai-memory backup` no longer fails OPEN on a Postgres deployment — a backup that cannot capture the configured store now ERRORS instead of writing an empty artifact with a valid checksum** ([#2444](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2444), GA BLOCKER, unintentional total data loss / false assurance). `run_backup` took the `--db` path unconditionally and handed it to `db::open`, which **creates the file when absent** (`src/storage/connection.rs`) and then runs the bootstrap `SCHEMA` + the whole migration ladder on it. So on a Postgres-backed daemon the product's own backup verb created an EMPTY SQLite database at the placeholder path, `VACUUM INTO`-ed it to a timestamped snapshot, wrote a **valid** sha256 manifest over those bytes, rotated `--keep` against it, and **exited 0** — every signal the operator had said the backup succeeded, and the discovery moment was the DR restore. **The issue's own suggested check would not have fired:** it proposed refusing when the source has no `schema_version`, but `db::open` migrates the file it just created, so a conjured database carries a full, current, valid schema and is indistinguishable from a real one by any schema probe. The only honest discriminator is *it did not exist*, which must be checked BEFORE the open — and it now is. `resolve_sqlite_source` resolves the CONFIGURED store through the same channels `serve` uses (`daemon_runtime::resolve_store_url`: `AI_MEMORY_STORE_URL_FILE` > `AI_MEMORY_STORE_URL` > the new `--store-url` flag, #1927) and REFUSES a `postgres://` store naming `pg_dump` / `pg_basebackup` (DSN password redacted per #1579 A3), an unrecognised scheme (no silent fallback to the local `--db` file), and a `--store-url` that DISAGREES with the environment (`resolve_store_url` gives env precedence over argv, so a silent divergence was reachable — on a durability command "which store did I snapshot?" must never be a guess). **`restore` carried the same defect in the direction that hurts more** and is fixed in the same change: restoring a SQLite snapshot onto a Postgres deployment copied the file to the placeholder path, printed `Restored` and exited 0 while the real corpus was untouched — false assurance at the exact moment of a disaster rehearsal. Three further fail-open paths on the restore side, found by the completeness sweep and not named in the issue: (a) restore performed **no structural validation** — the sha256 only proves the bytes match a manifest *we* wrote over whatever was produced (and `--skip-verify` proves nothing), so a truncated or foreign file was copied straight over the live corpus after moving it aside; the snapshot is now probed READ-ONLY before anything is touched; (b) restore renamed `<db>` aside but **left `<db>-wal` / `<db>-shm` in place**, where SQLite can replay the previous database's stale WAL frames INTO the freshly restored file (silent corruption of the restore) while leaving the moved-aside safety copy without its own WAL — the sidecars now move with the database; (c) a snapshot from a NEWER binary opened cleanly (the ladder only migrates forward) and then silently dropped the newer columns on the next write — `BackupManifest` gained `backend` / `schema_version` / `memory_count` (all `#[serde(default)]`, so pre-#2444 manifests still restore) and restore refuses a cross-backend snapshot and a forward-schema snapshot. A zero-memory snapshot is **WARNed, not refused** (3x3 adversarial vote, this session): a row count cannot distinguish a legitimately fresh SQLite deployment from a wrong-store capture, it misses the migrated-host case entirely, and on a Postgres host the local sqlite sidecar legitimately holds 0 memories while carrying the only on-disk copy of the `signed_events` governance spine — so refusing would both miss the real case and destroy a real one, and its escape hatch would be baked into every cron template within a week. `SQLITE_URL_SCHEME` / `POSTGRES_URL_SCHEMES` / `is_postgres_url` were hoisted out of the `sal`-gated `crate::migrate` into ungated `crate::daemon_runtime` (and re-exported verbatim, so every existing call site is unchanged) because the guard has to fail closed on the DEFAULT build too; `storage::index_coverage::SQL_TOTAL_MEMORIES` became `pub(crate)` so the corpus probe reuses the existing named statement rather than re-scattering the literal (pm-v3.1). R-203: `tests/backup_fail_closed_2444.rs` drives the real binary through the `AI_MEMORY_STORE_URL` env channel and references no new struct field, so the identical source compiles and runs against the parent commit — where it fails (exit 0, snapshot + valid manifest, source DB created).
