Two new CLI FLAGS on existing subcommands (`backup --store-url`, `restore --store-url`) — no new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration / schema-version bump, so no SSOT-count move.

### Fixed (SDK-RELEASE lane, GA blocker)

- **Cutting the v1.0.0 tag no longer auto-publishes two untested, broken SDKs to PyPI and npm** ([#2455](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2455), GA BLOCKER; three defects that composed into one release event). `publish-sdks.yml` triggers on `push: tags: v*` and its steps were setup -> build -> publish, with **no test step anywhere on the path** — while its sibling `publish-sdk-shims.yml` deliberately runs each package's suite first. Compounding that, `clients-ci.yml` was path-filtered to `clients/**`, so it covered only the four shim packages: `sdk/python` and `sdk/typescript` shipped test files that **no workflow executed at all**. That file's own header names this exact hazard — *"a broken shim could publish green at the GA release moment"* — and closed it only for the shims. Both gaps are closed: the path filter now covers `sdk/**` with two new jobs (`pytest (sdk/python)`, `jest + tsc (sdk/typescript)` — the latter also runs `npm run build`, so a type error can never first surface during a tag-triggered publish), and each `publish-sdks.yml` job runs the package's own suite BEFORE its build+publish steps so a red suite aborts with nothing uploaded. A published version cannot be un-published cleanly, which is why this is a release-integrity fix and not a convenience one.
- **The webhook HMAC was wrong in BOTH SDKs — `verify_webhook_signature` could never return true for a genuine delivery** ([#2453](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2453) / #2455, HIGH). The daemon signs `HMAC-SHA256(key = SHA256(plaintext_secret), "{timestamp}.{body}")` and emits `sha256=<hex>` with the timestamp in a separate `X-AI-Memory-Timestamp` header (`src/subscriptions.rs:983-990`, contract stated at `:980-982`). Both SDKs used the **plaintext secret as the key** over the **bare body** (`sdk/python/ai_memory/webhooks.py:47`, `sdk/typescript/src/webhooks.ts:57`, and `signWebhookBody` at `:79`) — two independent errors, either of which alone makes every real webhook verify as forged. **The test that should have caught it was tautological:** `sdk/python/tests/test_client.py:111-120` computed its "expected" signature with the *same wrong construction* the implementation used, then asserted the implementation agreed with itself; it passed while the SDK could not verify a single real delivery (the TypeScript suite had the identical shape, building its expectation from `signWebhookBody`). Both suites now assert against `sdk/fixtures/webhook_hmac_vector.json`, whose values were **printed by the Rust signer** (provenance + regeneration recipe documented in the fixture) — the SDK cannot influence them, so the tests can never again agree with a wrong implementation. R-203 before-evidence: the current verifier returns `false` for the genuine Rust-signed delivery; after, `true`. **Both fixtures are pinned back to the shipped Rust code** so neither can silently go stale: `subscriptions::tests::webhook_hmac_fixture_matches_the_shipped_signer_2455` guards the HMAC vector (its helpers are `pub(crate)`, so the pin must live in the unit-test module), and the new `tests/qual_sdk_attestation_fixture_2455.rs` guards the attestation envelope against the fixture FILE. Without them a fixture is the same defect one layer up: change the signing contract and the fixture goes stale, both SDKs break at RUNTIME, and CI stays green on both sides because neither is comparing against the daemon any more. The timestamp is now REQUIRED (keyword-only in Python, a required options object in TypeScript) so a call site not updated for the wire contract fails LOUDLY rather than silently verifying the wrong construction, and the replay window is enforced (300s age / 60s future skew, mirroring `APPROVAL_HMAC_MAX_AGE_SECS` / `APPROVAL_HMAC_MAX_SKEW_SECS`) so an authentic-but-stale capture is refused.
- **`client.store()` can now succeed against a default daemon — both SDKs gained Ed25519 write attestation** (#2455, HIGH). `POST /api/v1/memories` is `WriteSurface::HttpDirect`, which **fails closed by default** (`src/identity/attest.rs:130-136`: the `_` arm returns `true` for `HttpDirect` when `AI_MEMORY_REQUIRE_AGENT_ATTESTATION` is unset). Neither SDK's `CreateMemory` carried `signature` / `created_at` / `kind`, and neither shipped a signing helper, so every store returned `403 ATTESTATION_FAILED` — this is #1981 (the MCP attestation break) repeating on the HTTP surface. Rather than document a `AI_MEMORY_REQUIRE_AGENT_ATTESTATION=0` requirement — which would mean shipping an SDK that only works against a deliberately weakened daemon — the SDKs now reproduce the daemon's `SignableWrite` envelope: new `ai_memory.attestation` / `@alphaone/ai-memory/attestation` modules implement the RFC 8949 §4.2.1 deterministic-CBOR encoding and Ed25519 signing, `store(..., signing_key=)` / `.store(body, { signingKey })` sign automatically, and `bind_agent_pubkey()` / `.bindAgentPubkey()` call `PUT /api/v1/agents/{id}/pubkey` for the one-time key enrollment. Byte-equality of the envelope with the Rust encoder is pinned by `sdk/fixtures/write_attestation_vector.json` (also emitted by the Rust encoder); the Ed25519 primitive is pinned separately against RFC 8032 §7.1 TEST 3, an authority outside this project. Documented limits rather than hidden ones: the daemon secret-screens content before verifying, `created_at` must sit inside the ±300s freshness window, and the signature commits to six fields only. Python's `cryptography` dependency is the optional `[attestation]` extra; TypeScript uses `node:crypto` with no new dependency.
- **`UpdateMemory` gained no `version` field — deliberately; optimistic concurrency rides `If-Match`** (#2455). The issue asked for a `version` field on the update body, but Rust's `struct UpdateMemory` (`src/models/memory.rs:1602`) has no such field: the daemon reads the expected version from the `If-Match` header (`src/handlers/memories.rs:245-260`). A `version` key in the body would have been swallowed by the SDKs' permissive models and ignored by the server — handing callers a **false** sense of lost-update protection over a write that stayed last-write-wins, which is worse than no feature at all. Both SDKs instead expose `expected_version=` / `expectedVersion`, which set `If-Match`; a stale value surfaces the server's `409` as `ConflictError`.
- **The Python SDK's four conflicting version strings now derive from one literal** (#2455). `pyproject.toml:10` said `1.0.0`, `__init__.py:60` said `0.8.0`, the `_common.py:52` User-Agent said `0.6.0-alpha.0`, and `README.md:8` said *"0.6.0-alpha.0 — scaffolding, unpublished"* — so a published wheel would have reported one version to PyPI, another to `ai_memory.__version__`, and a third in the `User-Agent` every daemon logged, making server-side triage of a client bug actively misleading. All four now derive from `ai_memory/_version.py` (`pyproject.toml` reads it via `dynamic = ["version"]` + `[tool.setuptools.dynamic]`), pinned by `tests/test_version.py` — which fails if any surface drifts again.

### Fixed (POSTGRES-LADDER lane, L-PG-UPGRADE — GA BLOCKER)

- **A pre-v84 postgres deployment can start v1.0.0 again — the bootstrap schema no longer indexes columns the migrate ladder adds** ([#2424](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2424), GA BLOCKER, HIGH data-integrity / availability). `PostgresStore::connect` executes `src/store/postgres_schema.sql` on EVERY open, ALWAYS BEFORE `migrate` — but that file carried file-scope `CREATE INDEX` statements over columns the ladder ALTER-adds. On a LEGACY database the pre-existing table makes `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` a no-op, so the column is simply ABSENT when the index DDL runs and `connect()` dies with `init schema: column "…" does not exist`: the deployment CANNOT START. `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` was no defence — it keys on the INDEX NAME, which a legacy DB sitting below the arm that would have created it does not have. Two live instances confirmed it (v67–v73 died on `memories.cid`, v74–v83 on `memories.embedding_space`). **Root cause was a FALSE BELIEF, not three typos:** a comment in the same file asserted the bootstrap "is applied only at fresh schema-init, never replayed over a legacy DB, so the #1861 sqlite crash-on-legacy-open hazard does not apply" — flatly untrue, and it is what kept arming a NEW instance on every schema bump (v67 → v74 → v84). The claim is DELETED and replaced by a file-scope statement of the real rule; the fix removes **15** violating indexes, not the 3 that had already fired — a grep-and-widen sweep found the class also latent on `memory_links` (v15/v23 temporal + attest), `signed_events` (v33 `sequence`), `recall_observations` (v58 identity), `subscriptions` (v19 `event_types`), `memory_transcripts` (v25 `archived_at`) and `subscription_events` (v27 `correlation_id`), each of which bricks an open from a database older than its owning arm. Every one already had a `migrate_vN` owner, so the fix is a pure deletion from the bootstrap with NO ladder change and NO migration: fresh installs are unaffected because `migrate_locked` reads `current_version = 0` on a fresh DB and executes EVERY arm. `idx_agent_subkey_certs_instance` is deliberately KEPT and its legality re-derived from the real rule (`instance_key_id` belongs to a table no ladder arm ever `ALTER`s, so a pre-v79 DB has no relation at all and the `CREATE TABLE` genuinely creates it). **The class is closed by one invariant, not by 15 patches:** `bootstrap(fresh)` ≡ `ladder(v0 → tip)`. `scripts/check-migration-ladder.sh` gained rule **(f)** — no bootstrap `CREATE INDEX` on either adapter may reference a ladder-`ALTER`-added column (table-QUALIFIED, so `agent_quotas.namespace` cannot false-positive `memories_namespace_idx`) — plus two `--self-test` cases that plant the exact v84 postgres shape and the #1861 sqlite `cid` shape and confirm the gate rejects both. The gate FAILS against the parent commit (17 findings) and PASSES after. `tests/migration_ladder_integrity.rs::bootstrap_never_indexes_a_ladder_added_column` is the `cargo test` twin (no database required, so it runs in every CI leg), and the new `tests/postgres_ladder_replay.rs` proves it against a REAL postgres: for each of v67 / v73 / v83 it synthesises a genuine legacy database (stripping every column/index/table the ladder introduces above V — the strip set DERIVED from the ladder source, so it cannot rot as arms land), POPULATES it across `memories` / `memory_links` / `signed_events` / `recall_observations`, runs the production `connect()`, then asserts it reached `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`, that every row survived byte-intact, and that the resulting column set, column types and FULL `pg_indexes.indexdef` text are IDENTICAL to a greenfield install. That last assertion is the equivalence itself — it also fails if the ladder ever creates something the bootstrap does not, or vice versa. Why the pre-existing guardrails could not see this: `tests/postgres_schema_parity.rs` bootstraps a FRESH disposable database (greenfield only — it never migrates an existing one), and the guardrail-D checks assert the ladder's SHAPE (prefix uniqueness, gap freedom, arm monotonicity, cross-adapter tip agreement) but never its AGREEMENT WITH THE BOOTSTRAP. Verified against live PostgreSQL 18.4 + pgvector 0.8.5 on both the `pg-main` and `pg-ladder` instances. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration / schema-version bump — no SSOT-count move.

### Fixed (coordination-substrate lane)

- **A coordination action whose worker died is no longer lost forever — an expired lease now returns a still-`claimed` action to `pending` so it re-appears on `memory_action_frontier`** ([#2419](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2419), HIGH data-integrity / manageability). `memory_action_frontier` (and `memory_action_next`) select `state = 'pending'` only. The hourly lease sweep DELETEd every lease with `expires_at <= now` and stopped there, leaving the action in `claimed` — so a node whose holder died was simultaneously (a) not leased by anyone, and (b) invisible to every frontier/next caller FOREVER. The work was neither done nor surfaceable: the lease and the state had DIVERGED, because the substrate already treated the action as free (any caller could `memory_lease_acquire` it) while the state machine still said "claimed". This is not theoretical — it stranded three DAG nodes in this campaign, and recovery required knowing to run a full `memory_action_list` census by hand instead of trusting `frontier`. The sweep now reconverges the two: in the SAME transaction as the lease delete it transitions the action `claimed -> pending` (clearing `claimed_by`) over the **already-legal** state-machine edge — no new `ActionState` variant, no schema change, no migration, and **no change to any read surface** (`frontier` / `next` / `list` are byte-identical; the node reappears because it IS pending again). The requeue is compare-and-swap-guarded on `state = 'claimed'` (sqlite reuses `actions::transition_cas`; postgres uses a set-based `UPDATE … WHERE id = ANY($2) AND state = 'claimed' RETURNING id` inside the sweep transaction), so an action a live worker concurrently advanced is left ALONE. Deliberately NOT auto-requeued: an `in_progress` action (there is no legal `in_progress -> pending` edge — re-offering work a live worker may still be executing would risk double execution; it stays reachable via `memory_action_list { state: "in_progress" }` and its holder's lease loss is still recorded by the `coordination.lease_expire_reclaim` audit row) and any terminal action (the CAS guard rejects it, so completed work can never re-enter the frontier). Each applied requeue emits its own `coordination.action_lease_expire_requeue` `signed_events` row, deliberately DISTINCT from both the `coordination.lease_expire_reclaim` lease row (#2371) and the caller-driven `coordination.action_transition` — a FORCED state reversion no operator requested must be distinguishable in the audit trail from one a caller asked for, the same asymmetry that separates `lease_expire_reclaim` from the voluntary `lease_release`. The `memory_action_frontier` / `memory_lease_acquire` / `memory_lease_renew` tool docs now state the recovery contract (docs are wire-stripped, so the `tools/list` token budget is unmoved). Both backends (R-303). Regression: `tests/issue_2419_lease_expiry_requeue.rs` (7 tests — 3 fail against the unfixed sweep, 4 pin the behaviour that must NOT change) + the live-PG `store::postgres::tests::lease_sweep_expired_requeues_stranded_claimed_action_2419`. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.

### Fixed (federation outbound lane, L-FED-OUTBOUND)

- **Commit-checkpoint resolutions now actually federate — the FED-RQ-01 outbound leg has a production caller** ([#2391](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2391), HIGH; "landed" feature that could never fire). `federation::broadcast_checkpoint_resolution_quorum` shipped at v1.0.0 alongside the FED-RQ-01 (#1936) RECEIVE leg (`handlers::federation_receive` + `checkpoints::apply_inbound_resolution` + the fail-closed `AI_MEMORY_FED_REQUIRE_CHECKPOINT_SIG` gate, env #125), and `ROADMAP.md` §27 Gate 1 recorded the transport as discharged — but the broadcast fn had **ZERO production callers**: a repo-wide grep returned exactly one hit, its own definition. Federation fanout is only reachable from a handler holding `AppState::federation`, and checkpoints were the ONE coordination primitive the #1718 Pillar-1 write-surface pass never gave an HTTP route (actions got `POST /api/v1/actions/{id}/transition`, signals got `POST /api/v1/signals`; checkpoints got neither, and the MCP `memory_checkpoint_resolve` handler is a synchronous direct-sqlite path with no federation handle). The result was the worst failure shape a transport can have: **dead-but-covered** — the integration suite called the fn directly, so the coverage floor reported the outbound leg GREEN while two nodes running this build could never exchange a checkpoint resolution, which is the §25.2 epoch-freeze contract's ONLY cross-node mechanism. "Federate" was half true: inbound worked, outbound was structurally impossible. The new `POST /api/v1/checkpoints/{id}/resolve` (`handlers::resolve_checkpoint`) closes the leg, mirroring `transition_action` / `send_signal` exactly — local resolve FIRST, then W-of-N fanout, `503` under-replicated on a failed quorum with NO rollback (ADR-0001), single-node fast path when no peers are configured. **Node-granular attestation:** `resolved_by` is the resolved NODE agent id and is deliberately NOT a body field (the `send_signal` `from_agent` posture), because the receiver's fail-closed gate binds `resolved_by` to a locally-**enrolled** key — a body-supplied resolver could never attest. **Postgres is explicitly carried, not silently skipped:** the fanout sits ABOVE the sqlite/SAL backend split, so a postgres-backed daemon federates checkpoint resolutions identically via the existing `MemoryStore::checkpoint_resolve` trait method, and `postgres_gate` gained the matching allow arm — the #1552 lesson (a fanout wired INSIDE backend-specific branches, so the postgres arm silently degraded to catch-up-only) structurally cannot recur in this shape. Note the receive-side asymmetry is unchanged and still honest: a postgres RECEIVER reports inbound checkpoints as `unsupported_on_postgres`, so pg→pg checkpoint federation remains incomplete on the inbound half (tracked separately); this change closes the SEND half on both backends. Regression: `tests/fed_outbound_checkpoint_route_2391.rs` (4 tests; the fanout assertion runs W=2 over N=2 so a `200` is unreachable without a real peer ack — an unwired outbound leg returns `503` instead) plus the new class-level gate `tests/qual_fed_broadcast_reachability.rs`, which asserts EVERY `broadcast_*_quorum` in `federation::sync` has a caller OUTSIDE `src/federation/` and FAILS at the parent commit naming `broadcast_checkpoint_resolution_quorum` as the sole unreachable entry point (a test-only caller does not satisfy it — that is the precise blind spot being closed). SSOT moved in lockstep: `EXPECTED_PRODUCTION_ROUTES_COUNT` 93 → 94, `EXPECTED_PRODUCTION_UNIQUE_PATHS_COUNT` 79 → 80, and the narrative counts in README / ROADMAP / CLAUDE.md / DEVELOPER_GUIDE / API_REFERENCE / a2a-harness-integration / v1.0.0 release-notes. No new MCP tool / CLI subcommand / DB migration.

### Fixed (L-EXPIRY-CANON lane, GA-campaign DAG node)

- **`expires_at` is now canonicalized at EVERY sqlite write funnel — the TTL-extension floors and both archive-restore paths no longer re-inject a non-canonical rendering into the lexicographically-compared column** ([#2418](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2418), HIGH data-integrity; backend divergence). sqlite stores `memories.expires_at` as TEXT and every expiry consumer compares it **lexicographically** — the GC reap (`expires_at IS NOT NULL AND expires_at < now`), list/recall visibility (`expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > ?`), the #1596 `MAX(expires_at, floor)` extension floors, and `storage::lifecycle::is_expired`. That is only chronological when every stored value shares ONE fixed-width rendering; RFC3339 admits many spellings of the same instant, and a non-UTC offset mis-orders by up to 26 hours (`2027-01-01T00:00:00-11:00` is SIX HOURS LATER than a canonical `2027-01-01T05:00:00.000000Z` yet sorts BELOW it — a premature reap, and under `AI_MEMORY_ENCRYPT_AT_REST` an unrecoverable premature crypto-erase). Postgres stores `expires_at` as `TIMESTAMPTZ` and is structurally immune, so the drift was also a **cross-backend divergence**. Schema v87 (`normalize_expiry_rows`) healed the rows that already EXISTED and #2331/#2332 (FBL-01/02) closed the `insert` / `insert_if_newer` / `update_with_expected_version` funnels — but five ingresses stayed OPEN and re-accrued the drift on every write, so the corruption regrew after the heal. **The three #1596 TTL-extension floors** (`storage::touch`, `touch_many`, `fold_recall_accesses`) bound a Rust-side `now + extend` rendered with chrono's bare `to_rfc3339()` — `+00:00` with an `AutoSi` fraction (0/3/6/9 digits) — straight into `expires_at = MAX(expires_at, ?N)`; these are WRITES, not read-path comparisons, so every explicit touch and every periodic recall-access fold re-stamped a non-canonical value onto the live column (measured pre-fix: `2026-07-29T21:22:25.066980883+00:00` and `…056+00:00` where the contract is `…Z` at fixed microsecond width). **Both archive-restore funnels** (`restore_archived`, `restore_archived_for_caller`) copied `archived_memories.original_expires_at` straight back into `memories.expires_at` through an `INSERT … SELECT` that sqlite cannot canonicalize inside, so any archive row predating the v87 heal — or re-materialized from an erasure cold-tier bundle written before it (#2064 `try_restore_archived_row_from_bundle`) — re-infected the live table on restore. All five now render through the ONE canonicalizer: the existing `validate::canonicalize_valid_time` gained a `render_canonical_utc(DateTime<Utc>) -> String` sibling that IS its rendering step (one contract, no second canonicalizer), the three floors call it directly, and the new `storage::canonical_archived_expiry` reads + canonicalizes `original_expires_at` as a bound parameter on both restore paths — making restore a HEAL rather than a re-infection. Fail-safe in both directions, per the #2332 precedent: a `NULL` expiry stays `NULL` (a permanent row never acquires a synthetic deadline) and an unparseable value passes through byte-for-byte (degrade, never destroy a value the validation gates admitted). No crossroads vote — a single-correct-answer data-integrity fix extending an established precedent to the funnels it had not yet reached. Regression: `tests/expiry_canonical_ingress_2418.rs` (9 tests; the 5 covering the open funnels FAIL on the pre-fix binary and PASS after, plus NULL / unparseable fail-safe pins, a chronological-ordering pin on the create funnel, and a sqlite↔postgres `TIMESTAMPTZ`-contract parity assertion with an `#[ignore]`-gated live-PG twin). No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.

### Fixed (federation authority-lane, 3x7-round23 finding N15)

- **Inbound checkpoint resolution is now a compare-and-swap — an already-resolved checkpoint can no longer be overwritten** ([#2396](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2396), N15; MED data-integrity). `checkpoints::apply_inbound_resolution` was get-then-UPDATE with no state guard: it read the row, branched on "local is `pending`", then ran an unconditional `UPDATE … WHERE id = ?` — a TOCTOU window in which a concurrently-committed LOCAL resolution (or a second inbound resolution) was silently clobbered by the later writer. Because a resolved commit-checkpoint is an AUTHORITY-granting write (the separation-of-duties freeze anchor the epoch-apply consumer trusts, incl. `EpochAdvance`), a late writer could flip a coordination verdict after the fact — violating the documented **first-resolution-wins** contract (`AI_MEMORY_FED_REQUIRE_CHECKPOINT_SIG` env row #125, `docs/federation.md`). The pending→resolved transition now carries `AND state = 'pending'` in the UPDATE, and the "no local row" arm treats a losing INSERT (PRIMARY-KEY violation) as the same disposition: the loser is reported as `InboundResolutionOutcome::Conflict` (or `Noop` when byte-identical) and counted in the receive loop's existing `checkpoints_conflicted` — never an overwrite, never a silent drop, never a batch abort. The postgres receive funnel still reports inbound checkpoints as `unsupported_on_postgres` (`src/handlers/federation_signing_check.rs`), so there is no postgres twin to guard. Single-correct-answer bug fix restoring code to the shipped contract (no crossroads vote). Regression: `tests/checkpoint_cas_2396.rs` (4 tests, incl. a cross-connection interleaving + a threaded concurrent-resolver race).

### Fixed (POSTGRES-PARITY lane, roadmap-3x7 round-23 net-new findings N12/N17)

- **Six postgres write funnels now persist `kind_provenance` — the v79/#1945 epistemic-typing provenance no longer diverges by backend** ([#2393](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2393), round-23 net-new N12, MED parity). `kind_provenance` records HOW a memory's `memory_kind` was assigned (closed vocab `declared`/`channel_derived`/`regex`/`llm`) and is denormalised at the persist funnel from the `metadata.kind_provenance` carrier via `storage::extract_kind_provenance`. Every sqlite write funnel routes through `storage::insert` / `insert_if_newer`, both of which bind the column — so a postgres funnel that omitted the bind landed NULL where sqlite landed a value, the same cross-backend divergence class #2289 closed for `store_batch` and #2333/FBL-03 closed for the archive lane. The column + bind (+ the `COALESCE(EXCLUDED.kind_provenance, memories.kind_provenance)` upsert arm, copying the `store()` precedent) now land on all six divergent funnels: the three the issue named — `store_with_embedding` (the PRIMARY embedded-write hot path: sqlite has no override, so its trait default forwards to `store()`), `capture_turn_idempotent` (L4), `recover_turn_idempotent` (L2) — plus the three the completeness sweep found that it did not: `update_with_archive_on_supersede` (a supersede reset the provenance to NULL while the sqlite twin carried it forward), `reflect_with_hooks` (every synthesized reflection), and `apply_remote_memory` (the FEDERATION RECEIVE funnel, whose sqlite twin `insert_if_newer` binds it and whose comment already CLAIMED a postgres parity that was never wired — so every memory replicated INTO a pg node landed provenance-blind). Two arms the issue named were reconciled rather than changed: `archive_restore` ALREADY carries the column (landed by #2333/FBL-03, with a metadata-carrier COALESCE fallback for legacy pre-v87 archive rows), and `consolidate` is left UNCHANGED on BOTH backends — neither binds it, and neither binds `memory_kind` either (a consolidated row takes the SQL column DEFAULT `'observation'`), so no one assigned the kind, there is no provenance to record, and NULL is the honest value; binding on postgres alone would have MANUFACTURED a divergence where the backends currently agree (2×3 adversarial vote: 4 of 6 for leave-symmetric, 0 of 6 for postgres-only). Regressions: `tests/store_parity_gaps.rs::postgres_side::pg_{store_with_embedding,capture_turn,recover_turn,supersede,apply_remote_memory}_persists_kind_provenance_2393` (live-PG, `--include-ignored` + `AI_MEMORY_TEST_POSTGRES_URL`) plus the backend-blind `tests/qual_pg_write_funnel_parity_2393_2397.rs`, which runs with no database at all. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.
- **A superseded memory is now unprojected from AGE — no more ghost `:Memory` nodes in `memory_graph`** ([#2397](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2397), round-23 net-new N17, MED data-integrity). `PostgresStore::update_with_archive_on_supersede` archives the OLD row then hard-DELETEs it, but the AGE projection is MERGE-only: without an explicit `DETACH DELETE` the superseded id survived in `memory_graph` as a ghost `:Memory` node whose incident edges AGE-routed `kg_query` / `find_paths` kept serving — the derived graph serving deleted state as live, diverging from the relational source of truth. Every sibling hard-delete path already unprojected (`delete` / `apply_remote_deletion` / `forget` / `consolidate` / `run_gc` / `size_gc`, and `archive_by_ids` since #2315); this was the last one that did not. A same-tx `unproject_memory_from_age`, gated on `KgBackend::Age` and mirroring the `forget()` shape, now commits the projection cleanup atomically with the relational delete. Regression: `tests/store_parity_gaps.rs::postgres_side::pg_supersede_unprojects_from_age_2397` (AGE-gated, `--include-ignored` + `AI_MEMORY_TEST_AGE_URL`). The probe counts `:Memory` nodes via direct Cypher rather than through `kg_query` **deliberately**: the `kg_query` dispatcher silently falls back to the relational recursive-CTE on any AGE runtime failure, and the CTE reads the already-cascaded `memory_links` table, so a `kg_query`-based ghost assertion passes vacuously against a pre-fix binary (empirically confirmed). Also pinned backend-blind by `tests/qual_pg_write_funnel_parity_2393_2397.rs`. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.

### Fixed (AGE-DEFERRED-PROJECTION lane, roadmap-3x7 findings #7/#8/#9)

- **`kg_invalidate` is no longer a silent no-op under `AI_MEMORY_AGE_PROJECTION_MODE=deferred`** ([#2375](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2375), roadmap-3x7 #7; data-integrity class). `PostgresStore::kg_invalidate_cypher`'s step-1 `MATCH (a)-[r:related_to]->(b)` MISSED for a link that exists relationally (`memory_links`) + in `kg_projection_outbox` but has not yet been drained into AGE, so the method returned `found=false` WITHOUT running the relational `memory_links` UPDATE (the relational mirror was on the HIT path only) — the temporal invalidation (a `:supersedes`/`:contradicts` retraction) was SILENTLY LOST. The MATCH-miss branch now commits the AGE tx (so the `SET LOCAL` search_path does not leak across the pool checkout) then falls through to `kg_invalidate_cte`'s relational `UPDATE … RETURNING`, so a relationally-present edge is ALWAYS invalidated regardless of projection lag (also covers a projected-then-unprojected edge and a quarantined-outbox edge); the drainer re-reads `valid_until` at projection time (#2377) so the deferred AGE edge lands already-invalidated. Precedent-copy of the existing degrade-not-fail posture (no crossroads vote). Regression: `tests/age_deferred_projection_cluster_2375_2376_2377.rs::deferred_invalidate_before_drain_takes_effect_2375`.
- **`delete_link` now unprojects a DRAINED AGE edge under deferred mode** ([#2376](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2376), roadmap-3x7 #8; data-integrity class). The AGE edge unprojection in `PostgresStore::delete_link` was gated on `matches!(mode, Sync)`, but `kg_query`/`kg_timeline` stay AGE-cypher-served under `deferred`, so an edge already drained into AGE and then deleted was served by cypher FOREVER — no drainer work-item removes a *deleted* edge from `memory_graph`. The `Sync`-mode gate is dropped: the savepoint-wrapped `unproject_link_from_age` now runs on `KgBackend::Age` UNCONDITIONALLY, mirroring `run_gc`'s unproject posture (no crossroads vote). Under deferred mode the cost is one best-effort statement (the SAVEPOINT already degrades any AGE runtime failure to a WARN); a still-pending (un-drained) edge's DETACH-DELETE MATCH is a clean no-op, and the drainer's existence-check drops the orphaned outbox row. Regression: `tests/age_deferred_projection_cluster_2375_2376_2377.rs::deferred_delete_after_drain_removes_edge_from_kg_query_2376`.
- **AGE projection no longer drops a link's temporal-validity at creation** ([#2377](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2377), roadmap-3x7 #9; data-integrity class). `project_link_into_age` MERGEd the edge with only `{relation}`, so a link BORN with `valid_until` set — a federation relay of an already-invalidated edge, or a caller temporal link — was served as VALID by the current-view Cypher filter (`e.valid_until IS NULL OR e.valid_until > $now`) FOREVER, while relational reads correctly excluded it. `project_link_into_age` now threads the relational row's `valid_from`/`valid_until` and `SET`s each on the MERGEd edge when non-NULL (RFC3339 `to_rfc3339()` form so the agtype string comparison byte-matches the relational mirror); the deferred drainer re-reads them from `memory_links` inside its existence-check query (no `kg_projection_outbox` schema change), and all five call sites are updated (sync inline `link_internal`, deferred drainer, `apply_remote_link` federation-receive, the consolidate lineage-edge, archive_restore). Precedent-copy of `kg_invalidate_cypher`'s `valid_until` contract (no crossroads vote). Regression: `tests/age_deferred_projection_cluster_2375_2376_2377.rs::deferred_born_invalid_link_excluded_from_kg_query_2377`.
### Security

- **`asi-hard` posture enforcement relocated to the SYNCHRONOUS pre-runtime phase of `fn main()` — no more `std::env::set_var` on the live multi-threaded tokio runtime** ([#2386](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2386), round-23 net-new N5, HIGH; the closed-#1889 data-race class re-introduced). `security_profile::enforce_at_boot` pins up to 14 unset fail-closed knobs via `unsafe { std::env::set_var }`, but its call site sat inside the async `daemon_runtime::run` body — executing on the multi-threaded runtime with the tracing appender worker + tokio workers live, where a concurrent `getenv` is glibc UB. The env-mutating enforcement now runs via the new `security_profile::enforce_at_boot_pre_runtime()` from `fn main()` under the same #1889 pre-runtime contract as `apply_startup_env` (before `init_file_logging` spawns the appender worker, before the runtime is built), and the async body consumes the new READ-ONLY `security_profile::runtime_boot_report()` to log the stashed pin report — which also fails CLOSED for a direct library caller of `run()` (a below-floor OR un-pinnable/unset knob under `asi-hard` refuses the boot; pinning from async context is never attempted). The fail-closed "no-disable" semantics are byte-preserved (shared `loosening_refusal` message-construction site). Regression: `tests/security_profile_prerun_2386.rs::{enforcement_is_pre_runtime_and_absent_from_the_async_body_2386, below_floor_abort_still_fires_after_relocation_2386}`; the existing `tests/security_profile_dispatch_1961.rs` matrix (pins-take-effect, loosening refusal, garbage token) now exercises the relocated seam end-to-end. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.

### Fixed (round-23 net-new, GA loop)

- **Upsert-merge under `AI_MEMORY_ENCRYPT_AT_REST` no longer seals content to the INCOMING writer's key while keeping the EXISTING row's `agent_id` — the namespace-wide AEAD read-poison class is closed on BOTH backends** ([#2383](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2383), round-23 net-new N1, HIGH data-integrity). Every `ON CONFLICT (title, namespace) DO UPDATE` arm takes the incoming writer's `encrypted_envelope` while the metadata overlay preserves the existing row's provenance keys (#1784 authorship immutability), so an upsert by agent B onto agent A's row left a durable row keyed to B but attributed to A — `open_content` resolves the key from the row's persisted `metadata.agent_id`, so EVERY subsequent read AEAD-failed. Because the discovery scans collected `Result`, ONE such row denied every `list` / `search` / `recall` in the namespace. **Write side** — content is now sealed to the identity the SURVIVING row RETAINS (`retained_agent_id_for_upsert` → `seal_content_for_upsert`), so agent B's content is stored (never dropped) under the key the row's own `agent_id` resolves to and authorship immutability is untouched; an atomic post-write `reconcile_envelope_owner` backstop (keyed on the exact envelope bytes we wrote) re-keys the row inside the same transaction if a concurrent first-creation changed the answer, closing the postgres READ-COMMITTED race. Applied at EVERY arm: sqlite `insert_inner` + the federation twin `insert_if_newer` (both now wrapped in `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` when they own the tx, gated on the encryption flag so the default path is byte-identical) + `update_with_expected_version`; postgres `store`, `store_batch` (batched `UNNEST` pre-read + a zero-round-trip reconcile off the extended `RETURNING`), `store_with_embedding`, `capture_turn_idempotent`, `recover_turn_idempotent`, `apply_remote_memory` (which gained the transaction it never had), `reflect_with_hooks`, `consolidate`, and both by-id update funnels. `merge_inbound` / `supersede` were already self-consistent (content, envelope and metadata all come from one resolved struct) and are unchanged. **Read side** — the new `DecryptFailurePolicy` splits the posture: TARGETED reads (`get` by id, `get_by_prefix`) and completeness-critical EGRESS (`export_all`) stay fail-CLOSED, while BEST-EFFORT discovery scans (`list` / `search` / `recall` / `get_many` / kind + `source_uri` listings / the federation catch-up SEND, both backends) SKIP an undecryptable row with a structured WARN (`encryption.undecryptable_row_skipped`) + the `corrupt_provenance_rows_total{column="encrypted_envelope"}` counter — fewer results, never WRONG results, and never a namespace-wide outage. A skip NEVER modifies or deletes the row; the new `AI_MEMORY_STRICT_DECRYPT_READS` knob (env #146) reverts scans to the pre-fix uniform fail-closed posture. Design resolved by a 2x3 adversarial vote (`4d3ea1c5`): mechanism A4 hybrid (2 waves; A1 x1 / A2 x3 / A4 x2 / A3 x0), read-posture B2 unanimous 6/6. Regression: `tests/encryption_upsert_key_2383.rs` (10 tests) + `tests/config_precedence.rs::strict_decrypt_reads_2383`. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.

- **The sqlite federation catch-up SEND path now carries all 31 durable columns, not 16 — a `Decision` no longer relays to a peer as a defaulted `Observation`** ([#2384](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2384), round-23 net-new N2, HIGH data-integrity). `storage::memories_updated_since` — the sqlite side of `SqliteStore::list_memories_updated_since`, which backs the peer-pull `GET /api/v1/sync/since` catch-up surface — projected a HAND-WRITTEN 16-column list out of the 39 `memories` columns. `row_to_memory` reads every column BY NAME, so each unnamed column silently resolved to its Rust-side DEFAULT rather than erroring, and the receiving peer's `apply_remote_memory` → `insert_if_newer` then DURABLY PERSISTED those defaults. A `Decision`-kind memory carrying a #1834 claim-validity window crossed the node boundary and landed on the peer as an `Observation` with `valid_from`/`valid_until` STRIPPED, `version` reset to 1, and `cid` (the v74 content-address integrity anchor), `lifecycle_state`, `source_uri`, `citations`, `source_span`, `entity_id`, `persona_version`, `reflection_depth`, `confidence_source`, `confidence_signals` and `confidence_decayed_at` all DEFAULTED — silent, durable, cross-node corruption of the source-of-truth metadata with no error anywhere in the pipe. The postgres twin (`PostgresStore::list_memories_updated_since`) has always selected `*` and never had the defect, so a MIXED sqlite/postgres fleet corrupted rows only on the sqlite hop: divergence BY BACKEND. The projection now names all 31 columns `row_to_memory` reads (the 30 `Memory` fields + `encrypted_envelope`, whose #2303 decrypt is untouched). **Named list, not `SELECT *`, deliberately:** `memories` carries 39 columns and the 8 extras are derived/storage-internal — including `embedding` (up to 3072xf32 = 12 KiB/row), which measured ~+14% (~+7 us/row) on a 2000-row / 12 KiB-embedding corpus over 20x1000-row pages, on exactly the path that accumulates corpus-scale backlogs (#1578/#1579 B5); excluding the embedding columns is also CORRECT, since per #2167 a vector from the SENDER's embedding space must never be adopted by a receiver on a different space (the receiver re-derives from the durable TEXT). `kind_provenance` still federates via its durable `metadata` carrier, and no excluded column is a `Memory` field, so none could cross the wire under any projection. The list cannot silently drift back: three fail-closed guards pin it — a full-field parity test (the SEND row must equal the targeted `SELECT *` read of a row whose every field is non-default), a `memories` column census (every live column must be classified projected-or-derived, so a future migration's column cannot escape the decision), and a `Memory::FIELD_COUNT` pin. Regression: `tests/federation_catchup_column_fidelity_2384.rs` (6 tests + an `#[ignore]`-gated live-PG twin); the two fidelity tests FAIL on the pre-fix 16-column projection and PASS after. No crossroads vote — a single-correct-answer data-loss fix restoring the path to its documented contract. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.

- **`redact_pem_blocks` no longer over-redacts — every redacted span is bounded to its OWN `BEGIN…END` block, so certificates and prose survive the secret screen** ([#2387](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2387), round-23 net-new N6, HIGH data-integrity). Pre-fix the PEM redaction scanned for the SECOND `PRIVATE KEY-----` occurrence after ANY `-----BEGIN` across the WHOLE remainder: a certificate followed by a key folded into ONE redacted span (cert + intervening prose wiped), and a non-key `BEGIN` block appearing AFTER a key block hit the no-footer fallback and wiped the ENTIRE remainder including non-secret prose. Both shapes are funnel-FORCED on the federation-receive / import redact path (`redact_for_storage` — `refuse` degrades to `redact` there), so the over-redaction destroyed non-secret durable content and produced durable replica divergence. The scan now bounds each candidate block at the next `-----BEGIN`: a complete private-key block is masked through its OWN footer, a truncated key block (header, no footer) is masked only up to the next `BEGIN` (never the whole tail), and a non-key PEM block (certificate, CSR, public key) is preserved byte-for-byte. Key-material masking is unchanged (all FBL-16 termination + fuzz shapes still mask every key byte). Mixed-version note: nodes on pre-fix builds redact the affected multi-block shapes differently, so the screened cid/attest preimages for SUCH content can transiently differ across a mixed fleet until peers upgrade (cid is detect-and-log, never a refusal — env #102). Regression: `tests/secret_screen_pem_block_bounds_2387.rs::{key_then_prose_then_cert_then_prose_masks_only_the_key_2387, cert_then_key_do_not_fold_into_one_span_2387, truncated_key_block_never_swallows_a_later_block_2387}`. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.

### Security (SECURITY-GATE lane, roadmap-3x7 round-23 net-new findings)

- **Inference-egress gate now covers the curator + atomise LLM builders** ([#2388](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2388), N7, HIGH) — `curator::build_curator_llm` and `atomise::build_llm_curator` constructed their outbound LLM clients WITHOUT consulting `evaluate_inference_egress`, so memory content still egressed to an external vendor for curation/atomisation even under `AI_MEMORY_INFERENCE_EGRESS=deny` / `loopback-only` (the #1963 gate was wired only at `daemon_runtime::build_llm_client` + `reload::resolve_and_build_mcp_llm`). Both builders now consult the gate BEFORE `build_from_resolved`; a refused egress class yields NO constructed network client (`None` for the curator, a typed `Err` for atomise) plus a best-effort signed `egress.inference_refused` row, matching the `expand.rs` / `build_llm_client` precedent. The best-effort audit is threaded the operator-resolved `db_path` (the #1991 fix) instead of a recomputed `effective_db(DEFAULT_DB)`. Pinned by `cli::curator::tests::build_curator_llm_deny_egress_returns_none_n7_2388` + `cli::commands::atomise::tests::build_llm_curator_deny_egress_returns_err_n7_2388`.
- **`POST /api/v1/memories/bulk` now consults the PE-1 PreStore enforcement gate** ([#2389](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2389), N8, HIGH, CWE-288) — `bulk_create` had ZERO `http_pre_event_gate` consults, so `[hooks].enforce_mode = enforce` + `required_events = ["pre_store"]` with no enabled hook DENIED single creates (`POST /memories`, #1924) with 503 while every BULK create committed with NO hook running (silent PreStore bypass on the bulk surface). The bulk path now runs ONE content-invariant `PreStore` presence consult BEFORE any write (covering both the sqlite and postgres branches), returning the same typed 503 Deny — byte-parity with single-create and the whole-batch fail-closed shape of the existing #1919 attestation gate. Pinned by `tests/http_bulk_pre_event_gate_2389.rs`.
- **Namespace-scoped pre-event hooks actually FIRE — every pre-* dispatch site now carries the substrate-resolved namespace** ([#2390](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2390), N9, HIGH, CWE-288). `HookChain::fire` gated per-hook namespace scoping by reading `payload["namespace"]`, but 11 of the 13 pre-event dispatch sites built a payload with NO namespace (`{"id": …}` for delete/promote, `{"ids": […]}` for consolidate, the raw caller body for link/reflect, the raw MCP arguments elsewhere). Since `HookConfig::matches_namespace(None)` is `false` for a scoped hook, a namespace-scoped required/enforce hook was skipped on EVERY pre-event — namespace-scoped governance was structurally dead, the same silent-no-enforcement class `AI_MEMORY_HOOKS_ENFORCE_MODE` (#1734 PE-1, wired at #1885/#1924) exists to close. The gate funnels (`mcp::consult_pre_event_gate`, `handlers::create::http_pre_event_gate`, `hooks::dispatch_pre_event_enforced`) now take the namespace set as a REQUIRED parameter, so the compiler enumerates every dispatch site and a 14th cannot be added silently. Each site resolves the namespace exactly as its own handler does: PreStore via the #1590 default ladder (`params.namespace` > `[storage].default_namespace` > compiled default), PreDelete/PrePromote from the TARGET ROW, PreLink from BOTH endpoints, PreConsolidate/PreReflect from the resolved target namespace plus the source rows. Three consequential sub-fixes: **(a)** the set is multi-valued with fire-if-ANY matching (`HookConfig::matches_any_namespace`), because a link spans two namespaces and anchoring on the source alone let a caller pick which guard hook fires by swapping `source_id`/`target_id`; **(b)** the funnel OVERWRITES the payload's `namespace` key, closing a live spoof vector where a caller could add `"namespace": "unwatched"` to `memory_link` arguments (permissive MCP tool schemas) or an HTTP link/reflect body and evade a scoped guard hook; **(c)** an UNRESOLVABLE namespace with a scoped hook configured now fails CLOSED under `enforce` (`hooks::enforce::unresolved_namespace_deny`, staged `enforce`=deny / `advisory`=WARN+allow / `off`=no-op) rather than silently skipping the control, which a caller could otherwise force by passing an id that does not resolve. HTTP id→namespace resolution routes through the SAL `MemoryStore` trait so sqlite and postgres behave identically, and the read happens ONLY when the gate is installed (`enforce_mode != off` AND non-empty `required_events`), so the default deployment is byte-identical at zero added cost. `preflight_report` / `doctor --hooks` now flags a required event whose hooks are ALL namespace-scoped ("writes OUTSIDE that scope run UNGOVERNED") — previously that config printed a bare `(OK)`. Design resolved by a 2×3 adversarial vote (`5-agent vote (4d3ea1c5)` protocol; verdict memory `f52abdd7`): fire-if-ANY 5/6, fail-closed-on-unresolvable staged by mode, and the namespace-aware mandatory-PRESENCE gate DEFERRED (2 YES / 2 NO — it would manufacture fleet-wide 503s in namespaces the operator never named, and namespaces are unbounded runtime data no boot-time preflight can enumerate; tracked as namespace-qualified `required_events`). Regression: `tests/hooks_pre_event_namespace_scope_2390.rs` (4 tests: in-scope fires / out-of-scope does not, cross-namespace fire-if-ANY both directions, caller-`namespace` spoof cannot evade, delete+promote use the target-row namespace) + `tests/hooks_pre_store_namespace_scope_2390.rs` (2 tests) + 6 pure unit tests in `hooks::{config,enforce}`. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.
- **Model-weights attestation + signed-identity verification use `verify_strict`** ([#2403](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2403), N23, MED; [#2404](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2404), N24, LOW) — `inference::verify_attested_weights_signature` and `mcp::server_identity::verify_signed_identity` verified Ed25519 signatures with the malleability-tolerant `.verify` instead of `.verify_strict`; both now reject non-canonical / small-order-component signatures, mirroring the existing `verify_strict` sites in `src/approvals.rs`.

### Fixed (COORDINATION-AUDIT lane, roadmap-3x7 findings)

- **Postgres maintenance loop now runs the K2 pending-timeout sweep — governance `pending_actions` expire on postgres-backed daemons** ([#2379](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2379), FBL-22 residual) — the merged FBL-22 fix (`spawn_postgres_maintenance_loop_if_enabled`) ported only fold + `run_gc` + `archive_purge` + `lease_sweep_expired` into the pg maintenance loop and OMITTED the K2 pending-timeout sweep, which was spawned unconditionally against the LOCAL sqlite `Db` mutex (`spawn_pending_timeout_sweep_loop` → the rusqlite-only free fn `db::sweep_pending_action_timeouts`). On a `--store-url postgres://…` daemon the governance `pending_actions` queue therefore NEVER expired stale rows (approvable forever + unbounded queue growth), even though the pg schema already carried `default_timeout_seconds` + `expired_at` (v21) FOR this sweeper. Following the CLAUDE.md SAL new-operation recipe, a new `MemoryStore::sweep_pending_action_timeouts(default_secs) -> Vec<(id, namespace)>` trait method (default `UnsupportedCapability`) is delegated by `SqliteStore` to the existing free fn and implemented on `PostgresStore` as an atomic `UPDATE pending_actions SET status='expired', expired_at=NOW() WHERE status='pending' AND requested_at + make_interval(secs => COALESCE(default_timeout_seconds,$1)) < NOW() RETURNING id, namespace` (a non-positive default disables the sweep, backend-parity with the sqlite guard). The maintenance loop gained a 4th WARN-not-abort leg that drives it at the GC cadence and fans out the SAME `pending_action_expired` lifecycle event the sqlite loop dispatches via `dispatch_event_postgres` per expired row (both backends fire the identical event). Pinned by `store::sqlite::tests::sweep_pending_action_timeouts_delegates_and_returns_pairs_fbl22`, the `daemon_runtime::tests::spawn_postgres_maintenance_loop_if_enabled_*` spawn tests, and the sal-postgres `store::postgres::tests::sweep_pending_action_timeouts_expires_stale_row_fbl22`. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.
- **Lease sweeper now emits a `signed_events` coordination-audit entry per reclaimed lease on both backends** ([#2371](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2371)) — the FORCED reclamation of an expired coordination lease was the ONE lease op with no forensic trace (the voluntary acquire/renew/release ops all append signed-chain rows), so the ROADMAP "sweeper … emits `signed_events` audit entry" claim was false. The sqlite `sweep_expired_leases` now returns the reclaimed `(action_id, holder)` pairs via an atomic `DELETE … RETURNING`, and the new `sweep_expired_leases_audited` wrapper (driven by `background::lease_sweep` + the `SqliteStore` SAL path) appends one `coordination.lease_expire_reclaim` row per reclaimed lease attributed to the reclaimed holder; the postgres `lease_sweep_expired` twin does the same via `DELETE … RETURNING` + a byte-parity `signed_events` append (shared `coordination_audit::coordination_payload_hash`). Pinned by `actions::tests::sweep_expired_leases_audited_emits_one_row_per_reclaimed_lease`, `background::lease_sweep::tests::run_lease_sweep_emits_coordination_audit_per_reclaimed_lease`, and the sal-postgres `lease_sweep_expired_emits_coordination_audit_2371`.

### Fixed (STORAGE-CHAIN lane, fable-3x7 findings)

- **sqlite `memory_update` tier→long now clears the stale short/mid `expires_at`** ([#2331](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2331), FBL-01) — the #1626 tier→long ⇒ `expires_at = NULL` coupling, previously postgres-only, landed on the sqlite `update_with_expected_version` + supersede funnels so the tier-blind GC can no longer archive (or hard-delete + crypto-erase under `archive_on_gc=false`) an explicitly-promoted permanent row at its leftover TTL deadline. Pinned by `tests/storage_chain_fbl.rs`.
- **`expires_at` renderings are canonicalized at every sqlite write funnel** ([#2332](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2332), FBL-02) — every expiry predicate (GC reap, recall/list visibility, the #1596 touch/fold `MAX()` floors) compares the TEXT column lexicographically, and a caller/peer-supplied non-UTC-offset RFC3339 rendering mis-ordered as bytes (premature reap / over-retention / voided extension floor). The v86 `canonical_valid_time_opt` machinery now applies to `expires_at` at `insert`, `insert_with_conflict`, `update_with_expected_version`, `insert_if_newer`, and `overwrite_full_row_by_id`; unparseable values pass through byte-for-byte (fail-safe). Postgres unaffected (`TIMESTAMPTZ`).
- **schema v87 — `archived_memories.kind_provenance` + one-time expiry-rendering heal** ([#2333](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2333), FBL-03; heals #2332 pre-fix rows). The third v79/#1945 column is finally mirrored onto the archive on BOTH backends (its two v79 siblings landed at v85/#2035): carried through every sqlite archive `INSERT...SELECT`, re-inserted by both `restore_archived*` paths (legacy pre-v87 archive rows re-derive it from the `metadata.kind_provenance` carrier, vocab-guarded), and stamped/merged by the federation `insert_if_newer` funnel (pg store-lane parity). The sqlite v87 arm additionally normalizes legacy `expires_at` / `original_expires_at` renderings to the canonical fixed-UTC form (`normalize_expiry_rows` — instant-preserving, idempotent, fail-safe). `migrations/sqlite/0071_v87_archived_kind_provenance.sql` + `migrations/postgres/0044_v87_archived_kind_provenance.sql`; `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` 86→87 in lockstep on both adapters. The postgres archive/restore column-list carry is the tracked cross-backend follow-up on #2333.

### Fixed

- **Postgres branch of `PUT /api/v1/memories/{id}` now charges storage-growth quota — the FBL-12 per-agent storage-cap can no longer be bypassed on a postgres daemon** ([#2378](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2378), FBL-12 residual, roadmap-3x7 finding #14, v1.0.0 pre-ship; data-integrity/manageability class). The merged FBL-12 fix charged the storage-byte GROWTH of an in-place `memory_update` against the row owner's per-namespace cap on the MCP `memory_update` twin and the SQLITE branch of the HTTP `PUT` only; the POSTGRES branch of `update_memory` (`src/handlers/memories.rs`) early-returned through `app.store.update()` / `update_with_expected_version()` with NO quota logic, and `PostgresStore::update` never touched `agent_quotas` — so an agent on a `--store-url postgres://…` daemon could grow each stored row toward `MAX_CONTENT_SIZE` via repeated PUTs while `current_storage_bytes` reflected only the store-time bytes (the exact unbounded-growth bypass FBL-12 documented, un-fixed on the multi-tenant network surface). New SAL trait method `MemoryStore::charge_update_growth` (default `UnsupportedCapability`): `SqliteStore` delegates to the existing `crate::quotas::charge_update_growth` (cross-backend semantic parity; the sqlite HTTP branch still charges inline via the rusqlite conn), and `PostgresStore` charges via a contention-free `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` row-ensure plus ONE TOCTOU-free conditional `UPDATE agent_quotas SET current_storage_bytes = current_storage_bytes + $delta WHERE … AND current_storage_bytes + $delta <= max_storage_bytes` (`rows_affected()==0 ⇒ typed QuotaExceeded → HTTP 429`) — composing with the #2311 single-statement conditional-record shape rather than reintroducing a check-then-act race — with a best-effort `refund_update_growth` compensating decrement wired into the pg branch's update-failure path (mirroring the sqlite `refund_storage_only`). SAL new-operation recipe (prescribed precedent — trait method + both adapter impls); no crossroads vote. Regression: `tests/handler_postgres_branches_fake_pg.rs::pg_update_growth_charges_quota_returns_429` (fake-pg handler branch → SqliteStore delegate) + the `#[ignore]`+`AI_MEMORY_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` live-pg `tests/store_parity_gaps.rs::pg_charge_update_growth_over_cap_returns_quota_exceeded_2378`. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.
- **Offload TTL sweep no longer holds the global `Db` mutex across its per-row sleeps — up to ~10s of full HTTP stall per pass eliminated** ([#2359](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2359); v1.0.0 pre-ship, roadmap-3x7 #18). `src/background/offload_ttl_sweep.rs::spawn` acquired the single `Arc<Mutex<(Connection, …)>>` that serves EVERY HTTP handler and held it across the whole sweep pass, while `offload::sweep_expired` runs a synchronous `std::thread::sleep(10ms)` between each of up to `MAX_PER_RUN=1000` deletes — worst case ~10s where every concurrent HTTP request blocked on `state.lock()`, plus a tokio worker parked on a blocking sleep inside an async task (the module doc admitted the hazard and deferred it to a "v0.8.0" that never shipped). `spawn` now locks **per chunk**: it acquires the lock, deletes at most `CHUNK_CAP=50` rows with `Duration::ZERO` in-pass sleep, drops the lock, then performs the `SLEEP_BETWEEN_CHUNKS=10ms` pacing sleep OUTSIDE the lock via `tokio::time::sleep`, repeating until the cumulative `MAX_PER_RUN` cap is reached or a chunk drains the backlog — so concurrent HTTP handlers acquire the shared mutex between chunks. `offload::sweep_expired` is unchanged (it already accepts a per-run cap + sleep `Duration`); the `SweepAdapter` trait's per-pass `run_sweep` became the chunked `run_sweep_chunk(now, chunk_cap)`. Regression: `background::offload_ttl_sweep::tests::lock_released_between_chunks_2359` (a `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` proving the mutex is free during the inter-chunk sleep while the sweep is mid-pass). No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.

Per-release history is now explicit and cited: 74 (v0.7.0) → 100/99 (v0.8.0) → 101/100 (v0.9.0) → 103/102 (v1.0.0, `Profile::full().expected_tool_count()`).
- **§11.6 E2E federation encryption placed in the DEFERRED ledger** ([#2411](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2411), N31). The item appeared in NEITHER the landed nor the deferred set — invisible to release accounting and to operators asking whether federated memory CONTENT is E2E-protected. It is not: v1.0.0 ships transport mTLS plus optional **per-node at-rest** encryption, and `src/encryption/mod.rs:4-16` says so explicitly ("**NOT end-to-end across federation (#1809)** … the receiving peer re-seals under its own per-node key, so a federated peer holds plaintext transiently at apply time"). The ruling's "Three items" becomes "Four", tracking [#1968](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/1968) (OPEN); §25.3's "F-53/#1809 federation E2E" pointer is corrected in lockstep (#1809 was the CLOSED docs-drift fix, not the feature carrier).

### Fixed (bulk write reported success it had not achieved — five defects, one root cause)
- **`POST /api/v1/memories/bulk` now REUSES the single-create funnel instead of re-implementing it, and reports a truthful per-row outcome ledger** (closes [#2550](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2550), [#2551](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2551), [#2552](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2552), [#2588](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2588), [#2594](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2594); 3x3 adversarial vote, 9 lenses). The five issues were five stages the re-implementation omitted, so they are fixed structurally rather than patched individually: `create::{resolve_create_metadata, build_create_memory}` are now THE projection for all four create-family write funnels (single sqlite + postgres, bulk sqlite + postgres), and a field added there reaches every funnel by construction.
  - **#2550 — caller `scope` was accepted, never read, and DROPPED.** The row landed on the `scope_idx` generated column's `'private'` default, so a caller who asked for a fleet-visible `collective` write got an owner-only row and **every other agent silently saw zero results** — a wrong-visibility outcome reported as `200 {"created":N,"errors":[]}`. `kind_provenance` was dropped the same way (NULL on bulk, `declared` on single-create). Both are now resolved by the shared funnel, pinned by a surface-parity test that posts the SAME body to both endpoints and asserts byte-equal `(scope, kind_provenance)`.
  - **#2550, security half.** The bulk branches stamped the resolved caller OVER a disagreeing `agent_id` / `metadata.agent_id` claim, silently. Single-create has refused that with a 403 since #907. Bulk now refuses it too, typed `AGENT_ID_MISMATCH`.
  - **#2551 — `created` counted rows SENT, not rows PERSISTED.** Measured at corpus scale: **7,912 sent -> `created: 7912` -> 7,855 in the table, `errors: []`.** The envelope is now `{sent, created, updated, deduped, rejected, errors, pending}` with the reconciliation identity `created + updated + deduped + rejected + pending.len() == sent`. `created` counts rows INSERTED, `updated` rows upserted onto an existing `(title, namespace)`. An in-batch `(title, namespace)` collapse is a **result the caller must be told about**, not a silent success: `deduped` counts them and `deduped_rows[]` makes each one addressable by input index, so a loader can identify exactly which of its 1,000 source records was discarded. All of it is derived from the persist stage's returned ids — `id` is absent from BOTH backends' `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET`, so `returned == minted` is an exact zero-round-trip insert-vs-update discriminator. That property and the last-wins collapse order are now part of the `MemoryStore::store_batch` trait contract, because a first-wins adapter would make the handler name the WRONG row's content as durable.
  - **#2552 — every row error collapsed to `"validation failed"`**, with no field and no row index, so a 1,000-row batch yielded 1,000 identical, information-free strings and diagnosing a corpus load meant bisecting field-by-field through the single-create endpoint. `errors[]` entries are now `{index, code, field?, error}`. The #851 sanitization is PRESERVED — `error` keeps the same allowlisted labels — and `field` passes a server-authored-slug shape guard at the serializer so no future refactor can route caller-influenced text through the new channel.
  - **#2588 — a total quota rejection returned HTTP 200.** `sanitize_bulk_row_error` had no quota arm, so `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` fell through to `"internal error"`; **31,000 of 32,000 rows were dropped behind a `200` with zero log lines** while the single-row surface on the same daemon returned a typed 429. Now: a quota arm (matched on the slug, so a failed quota READ still classifies as internal — a broken substrate is not a signal to back off), a status that reflects reality (`200` only when every row landed as its own distinct row; `207` on partial; `202` when all rows are queued for approval; otherwise the dominant cause, with RETRYABLE causes winning by precedence so a mixed quota+validation batch reports 429 rather than telling the fleet "never retry"), and ONE structured summary WARN per call. The postgres branch additionally classified its own typed `StoreError::QuotaExceeded` as `internal error` because its prose matched no arm; typed SAL errors are now classified by `code()`, not by prose, so the two backends agree.
  - **#2594 — bulk performed NO embedding on either backend** while single-create embedded inline, so bulk-ingested rows were invisible to semantic recall until the paced backfill sweep reached them — and in an MCP-stdio or CLI-only topology that sweep never runs. Bulk now embeds before the DB lock via `Embedder::embed_batch` (chunked, so a 1,000-row ingest costs ~10 vendor round trips rather than 1,000), persists vectors on both backends, warms the HNSW index on sqlite, and reports `embed_status` truthfully when vectorisation degraded. A failure DEGRADES — the durable memory TEXT still lands and vectors are regenerable derived data.
  - **Also closed: the sqlite bulk branch had NO namespace-governance consult at all** — it went straight from the quota check to `db::insert`, while the postgres branch has enforced it since #705 and single-create enforces it on both backends. Same re-implementation-omits-a-stage root cause, on the funnel's most security-relevant stage.
  - **Wire change.** `errors[]` elements move from bare strings to objects, and a partial batch now answers `207` instead of `200`. Both are pre-GA corrections to a contract that was reporting outcomes it had not achieved; `docs/API_REFERENCE.md` carries the full envelope and `sdk/python`'s `BulkCreateResponse` — which already declared `errors: list[dict]` and a phantom `ids` field the daemon has never emitted — is corrected to match the real wire.
  - Pinned by `tests/bulk_write_truthfulness_2551.rs` (12 cells, all failing at the parent commit with the exact values the issues report, plus two CONTROL cells proving the new refusals do not pass trivially; counter assertions are ALWAYS paired with an out-of-band `SELECT`, because a counter-only assertion is precisely how #2551 hid) and by live-Postgres cross-backend assertions in `tests/g6_postgres_quota_enforcement_1795.rs`.

### Security

- **The #1946 rollback-evidence head-anchor log is now scoped PER DATABASE — a second healthy DB sharing one witness mount can no longer false-positive `RollbackCheck::Evidence` and be boot-REFUSED under `AI_MEMORY_REQUIRE_ROLLBACK_CHECK=1`** ([#2370](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2370), 2x3 adversarial vote `9e369e74` + `4d3ea1c5`; v1.0.0 pre-ship). The off-table `head-anchor.log` was keyed only on the witness mount and `read_head_anchor_high_water` took MAX over ALL lines, so DB B's surviving head was compared against DB A's higher anchor (boot DoS under the asi-hard-pinned require-mode). The witness `resolution` wire now carries an OPTIONAL signed `db_id` (v3, present-only `#[serde(skip_serializing_if)]` — v1/v2 on-disk lines stay BYTE-IDENTICAL and keep verifying) derived as domain-tagged, length-prefixed SHA-256 over the GENESIS (`sequence=1`) `signed_events` row's stable stored columns (`id`+`agent_id`+`payload_hash`; deliberately NOT `canonical_chain_bytes` (#1930 encoding change) nor a TIMESTAMPTZ readback (#2203 drift)), emitted on BOTH backends (`try_emit_audit_head_witness` sqlite; `pg_emit_audit_head_witness_in_tx` postgres, with the C2b NULL-`sequence` legacy-chain fallback to v2). The open-time check + `verify_audit_trail` filter v3 lines on the opener's db_id; a v3-only log of ALIEN lines resolves the new clean `RollbackCheck::NotApplicable`; a fresh (head-0, genesis-less) opener bootstraps `NotApplicable` ONLY when the log has NO pinned lines — against any pinned line it STAYS Evidence/fail-closed, so a rollback that wipes `signed_events` to empty remains detectable (C2). LEGACY id-less v1/v2 anchor lines are counted CONSERVATIVELY for every opener for one release (over-detect toward Evidence, never suppression) with a WARN naming the re-emit remediation, and the operator restore-sanction record now binds the database it clears (closing the cross-DB `(old_head,new_head)` integer-collision replay of a signed sanction; legacy id-less sanctions keep clearing for one release, WARN'd). Residuals disclosed in `docs/v1.0.0/release-notes.md` + the `signed_events` module doc: wipe-and-reinit db_id rotation (same ESTIMABLE-not-ATTESTABLE imaged-disk boundary) and the mixed-version-fleet high-water freeze (old readers withhold, never mint a false verdict). Postgres CHECK-side db_id parity (its `verify_audit_trail` keeps the conservative count-every-anchor posture) is tracked as [#2373](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2373). Regression matrix: `tests/rollback_evidence_1946.rs` (two-DB no-cross-Evidence both directions, require-mode bootstrap vs head-0 regression guard, same-DB rollback still refuses under require, legacy-line conservatism, per-DB sanction binding, sqlite + `#[ignore]` live-pg v3 emission shape) + `governance::audit::tests::{witness_resolution_v1_bytes_are_byte_identical_without_rollback, witness_resolution_v2_carries_rollback_and_bumps_version, witness_resolution_v3_carries_db_id_and_round_trips}`. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.

- **Federation W-of-N acks now require the receiver's structured applied report — a bare HTTP 2xx no longer meets quorum nor retires push-DLQ rows for writes the peer never applied** ([#2341](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2341), Grok W1A2-01/02, HIGH; v1.0.0 pre-ship). `src/federation/sync.rs::post_once` classified ANY `status.is_success()` response as `AckOutcome::Ack` without reading the receiver's own envelope, so (a) a postgres peer's 200 carrying `unsupported_on_postgres` counts — the FED-RQ-01 honest count of subcollections its funnel cannot apply (archives / restores / pendings / pending-decisions / namespace-meta / checkpoints) — counted toward W-of-N quorum for writes that never landed on that peer, and (b) a receiver that SKIPPED items (validation failure, #1464 per-write attestation refusal, #1934 namespace-scope refusal, substrate error) still acked — and `push_dlq` replay permanently retired (`mark_dlq_row_replayed`) rows the peer never applied. Silent replication loss with a success verdict. The 2xx arm now parses the report (`success_report_non_ack_reason`): `unsupported_on_postgres > 0` or `skipped > 0` ⇒ `AckOutcome::Fail` (quorum miss; DLQ retained/retried; deterministic non-applies quarantine at `MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS` with the closed-set `permanent` cause). Idempotent replays land in the receiver's `noop` counter — never `skipped` — so converged no-op pushes still ack; counter-less legacy 2xx bodies keep the backward-compatible Ack; `checkpoints_conflicted` (first-resolution-wins convergence) stays an ack by design; the 429 quota leg is UNCHANGED (already `Throttled`, verified NOT a false-ack). Envelope keys are SSOT consts (`handlers::{SKIPPED_FIELD,UNSUPPORTED_ON_POSTGRES_FIELD}`) shared by both receiver envelopes and the sender classifier so report and ack decision cannot drift. Regression: `federation::tests::{success_with_unsupported_on_postgres_is_not_ack, success_with_skipped_items_is_not_ack, success_with_clean_or_absent_report_stays_ack, success_report_non_ack_reason_arms}` + the extended `classify_quarantine_cause_maps_to_closed_set`. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.
- **Federation receive now redacts inbound bytes BEFORE per-write content attestation — `agent_attested` can no longer be stamped over raw bytes that differ from the persisted (secret-screened) content** ([#2340](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2340), Fable FBL-32 stamp-then-redact; v1.0.0 pre-ship). Both receive funnels (`src/handlers/federation_receive.rs` sqlite + `src/handlers/federation_signing_check.rs` postgres) verified + stamped `metadata.attest_level=agent_attested` over the RAW inbound content/title, then the storage funnels redacted the persisted bytes under the forced `refuse`→`redact` federation-receive posture (env #95) — so a cross-mode row (an `off`-mode origin signing raw secret-bearing bytes) landed labeled `agent_attested` with a `write_signature` that does not cover its own stored content, violating the `attest.rs` signed-bytes==persisted-bytes contract and env row #94, silently halting multi-hop propagation (hop N+1 rejects the row as forged under the v1.0.0 `AI_MEMORY_FED_REQUIRE_WRITE_SIG=1` default) and making forensic verify flag legitimate rows as forged. The new shared `receive_auth::redact_inbound_before_attestation` (the #1801 authoring-side redact-before-sign discipline mirrored onto the receiver) folds `redact_memory_for_storage` onto the row BEFORE the attestation step in BOTH funnels; when the SIGNED surface (content/title) mutated, the now-uncoverable raw-bytes signature is dropped (+WARN) so the row lands honestly `claimed` — never a cryptographically false `agent_attested` — while same-mode / clean traffic is byte-identical (the screen is a no-op or idempotent, signatures keep verifying to `agent_attested`, and the storage funnel's own later redact becomes an idempotent no-op, so stamped bytes == persisted bytes always). Regression: `federation::receive_auth::tests::{screened_signed_surface_drops_stale_signature_and_lands_claimed_2340, clean_screen_keeps_signature_and_agent_attested_2340, unsigned_surface_only_redaction_keeps_signature_2340}` + `tests/federation_write_sig_emit_1801.rs::{receive_redacts_before_attestation_so_raw_signed_secret_lands_claimed_2340, receive_helper_is_noop_for_redact_before_sign_traffic_2340}`. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.
- **The v2 bundle import now redacts a staged row BEFORE re-deriving attestation — a bundle row signed over RAW secret-bearing bytes can no longer land `agent_attested` over redacted stored bytes under `AI_MEMORY_SECRET_SCREEN_MODE=redact`** ([#2353](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2353), the portability sibling of [#2340](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2340), found while auditing every `stamp_attestation` caller during the #2340 fix). `import_full_envelope` re-derived attestation (`apply_import_attestation`, the pre-ship 3x7 HIGH-1 gate) over the RAW staged content, then `storage::insert_imported`'s origin-blind screen redacted the persisted bytes — the same stamp-then-redact class, narrower because the DEFAULT `refuse` mode already refuses secret-bearing bundle rows at the L1-parity `validate_memory` gate (only `redact`-mode destinations manifested it). The import loop now calls the shared `receive_auth::redact_inbound_before_attestation` (#2340) before the attestation re-derivation: same-mode/clean bundles are byte-identical; a cross-mode raw-signed row lands redacted + honestly `claimed` with the uncoverable signature dropped — which ALSO prevents the alternative failure where the stale signature would verify-fail against the redacted bytes and the legitimate row would be skipped as forged. Regression (mutation-pinned — fails on pre-fix code): `tests/portability_import_redact_attest_2353.rs::{import_redacts_before_attestation_so_raw_signed_secret_lands_claimed_2353, import_clean_signed_row_still_lands_agent_attested_2353}`. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.
- **`AI_MEMORY_INFERENCE_EGRESS` no longer silently WIDENS egress to `allow` on an unrecognised token — a typo now fails CLOSED to `deny`** (FBL-14, v1.0.0 pre-ship 3x7; `security` class, T3 posture). `resolve_inference_egress_mode` (`src/egress.rs`) previously fell through to the MOST-permissive `InferenceEgressMode::Allow` (with only a WARN) whenever the env value failed to parse, so a restriction-intending operator who typo'd the token (`deny-all`, `denied`, `local-only`, …) got full external-vendor inference egress — memory content leaving the host — instead of the intended restriction. The unrecognised-token arm now falls to the MOST-RESTRICTIVE-SAFE posture `InferenceEgressMode::Deny` (fail closed: no LLM/embedder client is constructed, so no memory content can be POSTed to any vendor) with a loud one-shot WARN naming the accepted tokens. The UNSET arm is UNCHANGED (byte-identical-legacy `Allow`) so a deployment that never opted in is unaffected — only a SET-but-unrecognised value (evidence of restriction intent) is treated as fail-closed. This DEGRADES loudly rather than crashing the boot (North Star manageability — a single typo'd knob across a fleet must reduce function + self-describe, never crash-loop). T3 decision (≥2 viable dispositions — `deny` vs `loopback-only` vs boot-refuse): chose `deny` (most-restrictive-safe) over a hard boot-error because `resolve()` is a non-fallible `-> Self` consumed at the `build_llm_client`/`build_embedder` chokepoints (no boot-error channel without a larger blast radius) and degrade-not-crash is the manageable posture for a trillion-agent fleet. Regression: `src/egress.rs::tests::unrecognised_token_fails_closed_to_deny_not_allow_fbl_14`. No new MCP tool / HTTP route / CLI subcommand / DB migration — no SSOT-count move.

- **Postgres-backed `serve` now runs periodic TTL gc / archive-purge / lease-sweep maintenance — pg corpora no longer grow unbounded** ([#2342](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2342), FBL-22, v1.0.0 pre-ship 3x7; manageability/data-integrity class). Every background maintenance loop `bootstrap_serve` spawned (gc + archive-purge, lease sweep, pending-timeout) bound the local sqlite `Db` mutex and called rusqlite free-functions, so on a `--store-url postgres://…` daemon they ticked against the placeholder sqlite DB while the pg corpus's expired rows / stale archives / expired leases accumulated unbounded (the CLAUDE.md "GC runs every 30 minutes; archive-before-delete" contract was silently false on postgres). Only the recall-access FOLD loop had a pg twin. New `spawn_postgres_maintenance_loop_if_enabled` (`src/daemon_runtime.rs`, pg twin of the sqlite serve bootstrap) drives the EXISTING SAL trait methods `run_gc(archive_on_gc)` / `archive_purge(admin, archive_max_days)` / `lease_sweep_expired(now)` on the `GC_INTERVAL_SECS` cadence with fold-before-gc parity and per-leg WARN-not-abort (degrade, never corrupt). Spawned only for the postgres backend (sqlite already has the under-lock loops). Regression: `src/daemon_runtime.rs::tests::spawn_postgres_maintenance_loop_if_enabled_{spawns_for_postgres_backend,skips_for_sqlite_backend}`. Storage-layer files untouched. No SSOT-count move.
- **`hooks.toml` per-hook `namespace` pattern is now enforced — a scoped hook no longer fires (Modify / Deny) in every namespace** ([#2343](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/2343), FBL-29, v1.0.0 pre-ship 3x7; data-integrity class). Both hook-selection paths (`HookChain::for_event`, `effective_hooks_for_event`) filtered only on `enabled && event`; the parsed + validated `namespace` field had ZERO consumers, so `namespace = "team/secure/*"` fired on every store in EVERY namespace — silently mutating / blocking writes contrary to explicit operator scope. New `HookConfig::matches_namespace` (exact → longest `prefix/*` → `*`/empty match-all, mirroring `TranscriptsConfig::auto_extract_for`) is now consulted inside `HookChain::fire` — the single chokepoint every dispatch surface funnels through (pre-event enforce gate, post-event observers, the MCP-boot reused signal chains) — so the gate fixes every path in one place. A `*`/empty pattern (schema default) matches everything → byte-identical for un-scoped hooks; a scoped hook never fires outside its scope, and never fires on a namespace-less payload.
